chat_messages.text:
Sharp objection — and it's the real cost of (b). Let me be precise about what's actually lost, because I don't think it's the whole assembly model.

**What Nexus knows that HubSpot doesn't:** the assembly tree. Parent SKU, children, `qty_per_parent`, and the roll-up (`assembly.requiredSell = Σ children.requiredSell × qty_per_parent`). That structure is Nexus-native and has no representation in a HubSpot line item.

**But look at SO2454 again.** The Item Group has a header (`TCS-BAR-01`, qty 15,000, no amount) and members carrying the amounts. That's a *flat* structure with a grouping marker — not a nested tree. NetSuite Item Groups are one level deep. **Our assembly hierarchy was already going to flatten at the NetSuite boundary under design (a) too.**

So the question isn't "do we lose assemblies." It's **whether HubSpot line items can carry enough for the workflow to reproduce that group structure.** Three possibilities:

1. **The grouping comes from NetSuite item config** — `TCS-BAR-01` is defined *as* an Item Group in NetSuite, with members already configured. Then HubSpot sends one line and NetSuite expands it. **(b) works, and Nexus just names the right item.**
2. **HubSpot line items carry a grouping property** the workflow reads. Then Nexus writes them accordingly — more work, still viable.
3. **The workflow can't produce groups at all**, and SO2454's group came from the item being pre-configured. Then neither design creates groups dynamically, and our "push creates a new Item Group per assembly at SO time" decision was wrong under *both* architectures.

**Possibility 1 is the likely one, and it would be good news** — it means assemblies are a NetSuite master-data concern, configured once per product, not created per order.

**This is checkable right now:** open `TCS-BAR-01` in NetSuite. Is its record type "Item Group," and does it have members defined? If yes, possibility 1 holds and (b) loses nothing on assemblies.

**Worth stating plainly:** if assemblies require creating NetSuite master data per order, that was always a heavy lift, and it's the part of 8c I'd most want to avoid. Design (a) doesn't make it easier — it just makes Nexus the one doing it.

Check `TCS-BAR-01`. That single record decides this.

chat_messages.text:
**Possibility 1 confirmed. This resolves the assembly objection.**

`TCS-BAR-01` is a **pre-existing NetSuite Item Group record** (internal id 64026) with three components already configured: `OTC-0012` (freight), `TCS-BAR-01` (the physical item), `OTC-0036` (customs). Each at quantity 1.

**So the grouping is NetSuite master data, not something created per order.** HubSpot sent one line item referencing `TCS-BAR-01`; NetSuite expanded it into header → members → `End of Group` on SO2454. The workflow never created a group — it referenced one that already existed.

**Three consequences:**

**1. Our locked decision was wrong.** "Push creates a new Item Group per assembly at SO time — master data as a side effect" is not how this system works, and shouldn't be how it works. Item Groups are configured once per product, deliberately, by someone who decides which components belong. Creating them per-order would pollute master data and produce a group per quote for the same product.

**That also dissolves the Item Group create permission concern** — we don't need it.

**2. Design (b) loses nothing on assemblies.** If the group already exists in NetSuite, Nexus writing a HubSpot line item for `TCS-BAR-01` produces exactly the same SO. Design (a) would too — neither needs to create anything.

**3. But it surfaces the real problem, which is bigger than the architecture choice.**

Look at the components: freight, customs, and the physical item are baked into the group with **quantity 1** each. The *composition* is fixed in NetSuite. Nexus's assembly model — parent, children, `qty_per_parent`, roll-up pricing — is far richer than what this group encodes.

**So: does a NetSuite Item Group exist for every assembly Nexus can quote?** Almost certainly not. Nexus lets you build arbitrary assemblies; NetSuite has groups only for products someone configured. **A newly quoted assembly has no NetSuite counterpart**, under either design.

That's the same class as the "line item not syncing" errors — it's the item-matching problem, one level up.

**Which means 8c's real question isn't (a) vs (b). It's: what happens when Nexus quotes something NetSuite doesn't have an item for?** Options: block the send with an unmatched flag (R9 already designed this), fall back to flat lines, or require someone to configure the item first.

That's a process decision, not an engineering one — and it's yours.

Then I was wrong to call the locked decision a mistake — it was a deliberate solution to a real labor problem, and I read it as an architectural accident. My apologies for that.

That reframes everything. Nexus knows the assembly composition at quote time; accounting is currently reconstructing it by hand in NetSuite. Automating that is genuine value, and it's a job only Nexus can do — HubSpot doesn't have the tree.

**It also settles (a) vs (b), but not cleanly either way.**

Design (b) can't create Item Groups — writing HubSpot line items only lets us *reference* items that exist. So if group creation is the point, (b) is out for that half.

But (a) still means reimplementing everything the workflow does well: Project creation, Sales Rep, PM, SharePoint, Class per line, OTC codes.

**So the answer is probably neither, and it's better than both:**

**Nexus creates the Item Group in NetSuite (master data), then writes the HubSpot line item referencing it, and the existing workflow creates the SO.**

Two operations, each doing what it's uniquely good at. Nexus solves the labor problem it was meant to solve. The proven integration keeps handling everything it already handles. No duplicate SO writer, no cutover, no reimplementation.

**Consequences:**

- Item Group **create** permission is needed after all — that's the master-data mutation, and it's the intended one.
- Idempotency moves to the group: `find-or-create` keyed on something stable, so requoting doesn't spawn duplicates. The existing `TCS-BAR-01` naming suggests SKU-based keys.
- The SO is still asynchronous — R9's receipt shows "sent," not "SO #".
- **The real design question becomes:** what does Nexus name the group, and what are its components? `TCS-BAR-01`'s components are freight + item + customs at qty 1 — that's a *cost-bucket* structure, not the assembly tree I assumed.

**Which is what I'd look at next:** how is accounting building these by hand today? What's the rule for what becomes a component and what the quantities are? Because Nexus has to reproduce that rule, and `TCS-BAR-01` suggests it isn't a straight dump of the assembly tree.

Do you know the convention, or is it worth asking whoever does it?

chat_messages.text:
That explains `TCS-BAR-01`'s shape, and it's the key insight: **the group isn't the assembly tree — it's the invoice presentation.**

Freight + item + customs at qty 1 each. Those aren't components of a travel case; they're the cost buckets that need to appear as one turnkey line to the customer while staying separate for accounting. # Item Group Conventions — questions for accounting

**Context to open with:** Nexus knows the full cost breakdown for every quote — packaging, production, raw materials, services, freight, duty, tariff, each with its own markup, rolled into a turnkey price per unit. The goal is for Nexus to create the Item Group automatically at order time so it doesn't have to be built by hand. We need to learn the rules well enough that what Nexus generates matches what you'd have built yourself.

**Best format:** have them build one live, or walk through a recent one, narrating decisions. What people do and what they say they do often differ, and the edge cases only surface in the doing.

## 1 · When does a group get created at all?

- Some orders have groups (SO2454, Dr. Squatch travel case), others don't (SO2646, Epicuren masks). What's the deciding factor?
- Is it the presence of freight/duty? One-time charges? Turnkey pricing? Something about the customer or project type?
- Is that judgment, or a rule you could state?
- Roughly what fraction of orders need one?

## 2 · What goes inside it?

`TCS-BAR-01`'s components are `OTC-0012` (Freight, Duties, Tariff), `TCS-BAR-01` (the physical item), `OTC-0036` (Customs), each at quantity 1.

- Why those three? Why is freight one component and customs another when `OTC-0012` already says "Duties, Tariff"?
- Is the component list always item + cost buckets, or does it vary?
- **Why quantity 1 on every component?** Does quantity ever differ?
- If an order has multiple physical SKUs, is it one group with several items, or a group per SKU?

## 3 · The OTC codes

- Is there a **fixed list** of OTC codes, or do new ones get created?
- Which cost types map to which code? So far: `OTC-0012` freight/duties/tariff, `OTC-0036` customs, `OTC-0051` small batch setup, `OTC-0016` micro testing.
- If a quote has a cost with no matching OTC code, what happens today?
- Does the *same* cost always use the same code, or does it depend on context?

## 4 · Naming and identity

- What's the convention? `TCS-BAR-01` looks like a SKU code — is it always the SKU?
- What if the **same SKU is quoted again** at a different tier, quantity, or price — new group, or reuse the existing one?
- Can two groups share a name? Does NetSuite prevent it?
- Does the group belong to a product, a customer, or an order?

**This one matters most for us.** If a group is per-product and reused, Nexus does find-or-create. If it's per-order, Nexus creates every time. The answer changes the design.

## 5 · Pricing inside the group

- The group header shows quantity and unit cost but **no amount** — amounts sit on members. Is that automatic, or configured?
- How are prices assigned to components? On SO2454: freight 0.5264, customs 0.4195, item 1.2731, summing to the turnkey rate.
- **Does the customer see the breakdown, or only the rolled-up total?** ("Display Components on Transactions" is unchecked on `TCS-BAR-01`.)
- If Nexus supplies the turnkey price and the breakdown, is that enough — or is there a step where you adjust?

## 6 · Classification

- `TCS-BAR-01` carries Class "Soft Goods and Accessories." On SO2646 the lines vary — "Filling and Packout Services," "One Time Charges," "Freight."
- Is Class set on the group, on components, or on SO lines?
- What determines it — product type, service type, or something else?

## 7 · The work itself

- How long does building one take?
- What's the trigger — do you wait for the SO, or build ahead?
- What most often goes wrong or needs revisiting?
- **What would you want an automated version to get right that a naive one would get wrong?**

*(That last question usually surfaces more than the rest combined.)*

## 8 · The unmatched case

- What happens today when an order has a product with **no NetSuite item at all**? The workflow errors with "line item not syncing" — who fixes it, and how?
- Should Nexus **create the item** too, or block and ask a human?

**My recommendation to flag in the conversation: block, don't create.** Creating base item master data automatically is a bigger commitment than assembling a group from existing items, and Nexus's UI already has a place to surface it. But if they say the manual item-creation step is also a burden, that's worth hearing.

---

**One thing to watch for:** if the answer to 4 is "per order," Nexus will generate a group for every order and master data grows unboundedly. Ask what they'd think of that — they may have an opinion about NetSuite clutter that we should respect.

If every order gets a group, and groups are keyed per-product-reused, then requoting the same SKU reuses one record and master data stays bounded. If they're per-order, you get a new NetSuite Item Group for **every order you ever write** — hundreds a year, growing forever, each nearly identical to the last.

**That tension is the thing to resolve**, and it's the question I'd put to accounting most sharply:

Whichever they say determines Nexus's identity key and whether find-or-create is even the right primitive.

**No build, no PR, no writes.** Report only. Runs alongside 8b.

**NetSuite sandbox is refreshed.** The setup sequence (§4A steps 2–6: integration record → role → token → env → connection smoke) can run whenever you're ready. Item Group create permission is the one to confirm early — and it *is* needed now that group creation is confirmed as the intended value.

chat_messages.text:
That's an important answer, and it partially contradicts what you told me earlier.

**Aisha's rule: grouping is driven by how the customer wants to be invoiced**, expressed through their PO. Dr. Squatch wants packaging and freight as one unit price → amortize into a single figure → NetSuite breaks it into a group underneath. So it's a **per-customer invoicing preference**, not a property of the order.

**Your answer to Q1 was "create an item group for all moving forward"** — standardize because the business is moving toward turnkey.

Those can both be true, but they're different things and 8c needs to know which governs:

- **Aisha's version** — Nexus needs to know each customer's invoicing preference, which means a field somewhere (customer-level setting, or read from the deal), and PMs need to set it.
- **Your version** — always group, and the customer preference becomes moot because everything is presented that way.

**If you're overriding the current practice, that's a policy change, not just a spec.** Worth being explicit with Aisha that Nexus will group everything, because it changes what she receives for customers who don't currently want it. Better to have that disagreement now than to ship it.

**One thing Aisha's answer also confirms:** *"we amortize them in"* — the amortization happens before NetSuite. On SO2454, freight 0.5264 + customs 0.4195 + item 1.2731 = the turnkey rate. **Nexus already computes exactly this** — `requiredSellPerUnit` folds freight, duty, and tariff with their own markups. So Nexus can supply both the amortized total and the component split natively. That's the strongest evidence yet that this automation is the right job for Nexus.

**Still open, and now more urgent given "always group":** Q4 — same product ordered again with different freight. Does Aisha edit the existing group's prices, or create a second group? If it's per-order, "always group" means a new NetSuite Item Group for every order forever.

That's the one question I'd get answered before CC writes any group logic.

clarification - Melinda Will  [9:23 AM]
When I hear item groupings, I think of NetSuite Item Groups. I just want to make sure we're talking about the same thing. In NetSuite, we use several different item types, including standalone items, Item Groups, and (eventually) Assemblies. An Item Group acts like an umbrella. The group header sits at the top, and the individual inventory items roll up underneath it. For example, with Dr. Squatch, we also include freight within the Item Group. Internally, NetSuite tracks all of the underlying components and calculates the total at the group level, but when the invoice is printed, the customer sees a single line item instead of all of the individual components. It's similar in concept to an Assembly in that multiple components are rolled up into one customer-facing item, although they function differently in NetSuite. Is that the type of grouping you're referring to, or are you thinking about grouping orders from a business process perspective?

chat_messages.text:
Melinda's clarification is worth taking seriously — she's flagging a real distinction we've been eliding.

**Confirm to her: yes, NetSuite Item Groups, exactly as she describes.** That matches `TCS-BAR-01` — group header, inventory items and freight rolling up underneath, single line on the printed invoice ("Display Components on Transactions" unchecked, which is precisely the behaviour she's describing).

**But she raised something we haven't addressed: Assemblies are a separate NetSuite item type, and she says "eventually."**

That matters because **Nexus's internal model is an assembly tree** — parent SKU, children, `qty_per_parent`, roll-up pricing. Nexus's "assembly" and NetSuite's "Assembly" are different things, and we've been mapping ours onto Item Groups. Two questions that follow:

1. **Is Item Group the right long-term target, or is Nexus's assembly conceptually a NetSuite Assembly?** If they're planning to adopt Assemblies, and Nexus auto-creates Item Groups in the meantime, we may be building toward a structure they intend to migrate off.
2. **What distinguishes the two in their practice?** She says they "function differently in NetSuite" — Assemblies typically involve a build/work-order process and inventory transformation; Item Groups are a presentation and pricing wrapper with no build step. If any Nexus quote involves actual manufacturing assembly rather than just bundled pricing, the item type may differ per quote.

**Suggested reply to Melinda:**

> Yes — NetSuite Item Groups, exactly as you describe. `TCS-BAR-01` is the shape we mean: group header, components underneath, one line on the customer's invoice.
>
> Two follow-ups given what you said about Assemblies:
>
> 1. You mentioned Assemblies "eventually." Is there a plan to move some of this to Assemblies? We're building automation to create these groups from the quote, and we'd rather build toward where you're heading than where you are.
> 2. Where's the line between the two in practice — is it about whether there's a physical build step, or something else? Some of our quotes are bundled pricing, others involve actual assembly work, and we may need to pick the item type per quote.
>
> Also, one thing we need to pin down: when the same product is ordered again with different freight costs, do you edit the existing Item Group's prices, or create a new group?

**That last question is still the one blocking CC.** It's been asked twice now and hasn't come back — worth pushing on directly.

Assemblies out of scope — noted, and dropping it.

**Q4 is answered: groups are per-SKU, reused, and only recreated when the SKU changes.** That's find-or-create keyed on SKU code. Master data stays bounded. It's the answer that makes "always create a group" safe.

**Your instinct that it's questionable is right, and here's the specific problem.**

`TCS-BAR-01`'s group contains freight and customs. Those are **per-shipment costs**, not properties of the product. Same SKU, different container rate or different tariff → the group's component prices are now wrong for the new order.

Two possibilities, and neither is comfortable:

- **The group's prices get edited each order** — then it isn't reusable master data, it's a mutable record being rewritten per transaction, and historical SOs referencing it may be affected. Also a race: two open orders for the same SKU can't hold different freight.
- **The prices live on the SO line, not the group** — then the group is just a structural template (which components, in what order) and prices come per-order. That's clean, and it's consistent with SO2454 showing rates on the *SO lines*.

**The second reading is more likely correct**, and it would mean the group is a shape, not a price. Worth verifying directly — open `TCS-BAR-01`'s components and check whether they carry prices at all, or only item + quantity. The screenshot you sent showed Item / Description / Quantity / Units / Schedule columns with **no price column**, which supports the template reading.

**If the group is a priceless template, 8c gets simpler:**
- Find-or-create by SKU, create only when the SKU is new
- Nexus supplies prices on the HubSpot line items or the SO, per order
- Freight variation is handled naturally — no group edits, no races

**One remaining wrinkle:** what if the same SKU is quoted once with freight and once without (domestic vs international)? The component *list* differs, not just prices. Does that need two groups, or does the group carry all possible components with zero-quantity ones suppressed?

That's worth asking Melinda, and it's the last structural unknown I have.

chat_messages.text:
That's the answer, and it's a soft one — "TCS-BAR-02 or -I/-D" means **there is no fixed convention.** Two different schemes, chosen ad hoc.

Which is fine for a human and unworkable for automation. Nexus can't reproduce a convention that doesn't exist; it has to define one.

**My recommendation: `-D` / `-I` semantic suffixes, not sequential numbers.**

- Sequential (`-02`) tells you nothing about *why* a second group exists. It also requires reading existing groups to know the next number — a lookup that can race.
- Semantic (`-D`/`-I`) is derivable from the quote itself. Nexus knows whether there are freight/duty/tariff legs. Given a SKU and a composition, the name is a pure function — no lookup, no race, and find-or-create becomes deterministic.
- It's also self-documenting for accounting: they can tell what a group is by its name.

**The rule:** `{SKU}` when there are no international cost components, `{SKU}-I` when there are. Or `-D`/`-I` explicitly on both if Aisha prefers symmetry — worth asking, since `TCS-BAR-01` is currently unsuffixed and renaming it isn't in scope.

**The risk to raise with her:** if compositions vary in more ways than domestic/international, two suffixes won't cover it and we'd be back to ad hoc. Worth asking directly:

> Is domestic vs international the only reason you'd need a second group for the same SKU, or are there other splits? We want to define one convention Nexus follows every time, rather than have it guess — and it's better to know now if there are more cases than those two.

**And one to flag for you, not her:** existing groups follow neither convention consistently. Nexus's find-or-create will search for `TCS-BAR-01-I`, not find it, and create a new group even if Aisha built an equivalent under a different name. **Some reconciliation of existing groups is likely needed at cutover** — not a Slice 12 problem, but it should be banked so it isn't discovered in production.

**The stronger design: name for humans, key on something machine-owned.**

NetSuite item records support an **External ID** field. Nexus writes a deterministic value there — a hash or composite of SKU + component composition, or simply the Nexus-side identifier for that group configuration. Find-or-create queries External ID; the display name is whatever's most readable for accounting and carries no semantic load. Two groups can share a naming pattern without ambiguity because identity never depends on the string.

- No parsing names to infer composition
- No race on "what's the next number"
- Typos in display names are cosmetic, not corrupting

Agreed — and you've put your finger on the deeper issue. Naming as identity is the antipattern. Any string a human types is a place for a typo, and any convention encoded in a name has to be parsed back out to be useful.

**The stronger design: name for humans, key on something machine-owned.**

NetSuite item records support an **External ID** field. Nexus writes a deterministic value there — a hash or composite of SKU + component composition, or simply the Nexus-side identifier for that group configuration. Find-or-create queries External ID; the display name is whatever's most readable for accounting and carries no semantic load. Two groups can share a naming pattern without ambiguity because identity never depends on the string.

That also means:
- No parsing names to infer composition
- No race on "what's the next number"
- Typos in display names are cosmetic, not corrupting
- Nexus can *report* which group corresponds to which quote configuration, which is the traceability you're asking for

**One thing to verify:** whether Item Group records expose External ID and whether it's queryable. It's standard on NetSuite records, and the SO already uses `Memo` for the HubSpot deal ID — but that's a *transaction* field, and item records may behave differently. That's a sandbox probe once the connection is up.

**And it doesn't fully escape the problem.** Existing groups have no External ID, so find-or-create won't match them and Nexus will create parallel records for products Aisha already configured. Same reconciliation issue as before — it just moves. Worth a one-time backfill: stamp External IDs onto existing groups so Nexus adopts them rather than duplicating.

Wait for Aisha on whether domestic/international is the only split — that still determines how many compositions exist per SKU, which is worth knowing regardless of how we key them.

cd /home/claude && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='SLICE-12-HANDOVER.md'
s=open(p).read()

old = '**Decisions LOCKED (pre-R9, still standing):** assembly → NetSuite Item Group · push creates a new Item Group per assembly at SO time · per-member unit prices rolled under the group · SO status "Pending Fulfillment".'

new = '''### 🔴 ITEM GROUPS — the discovery pass REWROTE this. The old "locked" decision was wrong.

**Superseded:** ~~"push CREATES a new Item Group per assembly at SO time — master data as a side effect; per-member unit prices rolled under the group."~~

**What we found by inspecting `TCS-BAR-01` (internal id 64026) and two real SOs:**

An Item Group is a **pre-existing, PRICELESS TEMPLATE**. Components sit at **$0**; the real prices are entered on the **SO line** at order time. `TCS-BAR-01`'s components are `OTC-0012` (freight) + `TCS-BAR-01` (physical item) + `OTC-0036` (customs), each qty 1, no price column. SO2454 carries the actual rates (freight 0.5264 + customs 0.4195 + item 1.2731 = the turnkey rate). NetSuite expands the group on the SO into header → members → `End of Group`; the **customer sees one line** ("Display Components on Transactions" unchecked).

**Why this matters:** the group is the INVOICE PRESENTATION, not the assembly tree. Aisha: *"DRSQ likes packaging and freight as one unit price so we amortize them in, and in NS we break it into a group."* Nexus already computes exactly this — `requiredSellPerUnit` folds freight/duty/tariff with their own markups AND retains the breakdown. **Accounting is hand-reconstructing a decomposition Nexus produces natively. That labor is the point of automating it.**

**DECIDED — 8c's group logic:**

| Aspect | Decision | Source |
|---|---|---|
| When to create | **Always.** Every order gets a group — turnkey and component deal types alike. No branch on quote shape. | Edward (standardizing as the business moves to turnkey) |
| Identity | **Per SKU × COMPOSITION**, not per SKU alone, not per order. Same SKU domestic vs international = **two separate groups** (Aisha). Master data stays bounded (compositions are few). | Aisha |
| Prices | Components at **$0**. Prices go on the SO line per order. **No group mutation per order** → no race between concurrent orders, historical SOs unaffected. | Aisha |
| Naming | **Generated unique SKU** in the name/number field. **Do NOT encode a human convention** — Aisha's is ad hoc ("TCS-BAR-02, or -I / -D... sometimes"), unprogrammable, typo-prone. The name IS customer-facing (shows on SO + invoice), and Aisha confirms the SKU is definitely unique, so it can carry identity. | Edward |
| Description | Human-readable prose describing the group. Currently blank on `TCS-BAR-01`; **Aisha explicitly asked for it.** Build what she asked for. | Aisha |
| Find-or-create | Keyed on the generated SKU. Same composition → same SKU → reuse. Different composition → different SKU → new group. **Deterministic, no lookup race, no human decision.** | CA |
| Components | Physical item + OTC lines, qty 1, $0. Class per existing convention. | observed |

**Open on group logic:**
- **The SKU generation rule** — must be a pure function of composition (e.g. source SKU + short deterministic composition hash). **Not sequential** — sequential needs a lookup to know what's next, reintroducing the race. Propose something concrete to Aisha before building; she sees these in NetSuite lists daily.
- **Existing hand-built groups won't match Nexus's generated SKUs** → Nexus will create parallel records alongside Aisha's. Needs a one-time reconciliation at cutover, or accepted duplication. **Bank it; don't discover it in production.**
- **Assemblies (the NetSuite item type) are EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE.** Melinda flagged they may move there "eventually." Item Groups are what's used now. Note Nexus's "assembly" ≠ NetSuite's "Assembly".

**Item Group CREATE permission IS required** on the integration role — group creation is the intended value, not an incidental side effect.

### Still locked
SO status on create = **"Pending Fulfillment"** — **verified empirically** on SO2646 (created 7/28/2026, untouched, workflow-created). This is the exact class of assumption that broke in #145; now evidence, not assumption.

### What a workflow-created SO actually contains (SO2646, untouched)
Customer `3471 Epicuren` (numeric entity id + name) · Subsidiary The DPS, Inc. · Location The DPS · Class `Business Segment / TurnKey` · **Memo = HubSpot deal id `40412634025`** (header linkage) · per-line **`HubSpot Line`** ordinals · Source `REST Web Services` · Price Level `Custom` · `Transaction Hold` **CHECKED** at create (unchecked on the billed SO2454 — looks like a create-time default ops clears) · Est. Invoice Date · Project · Sales Rep · Project Manager · Shipping Address · rate ≠ unit cost (9.05 → 11.77) · OTC lines **created by the workflow**, not added by ops.

**Header linkage lives in `Memo`, not External ID** → external-ID-based idempotency may be unavailable on transactions. **Verify directly** — it's the §6.3 linchpin.

### 🔴 EVERYTHING on that SO traces back to HubSpot
Sales Rep ← deal owner · Project Manager ← HubSpot custom field · SharePoint folder ← HubSpot custom field · **and the NetSuite Project record itself is auto-created by HubSpot** (id `174 Epicuren - Pro Masks`, with its own Opportunity link `#OP3228`).

**This nearly inverted the architecture.** Design (a) "Nexus pushes the SO directly" would mean reimplementing the entire HubSpot→NetSuite integration — item resolution, OTC codes, per-line Class, Project creation, PM, SharePoint. Design (b) "Nexus writes HubSpot line items and the existing workflow creates the SO" is far smaller but **cannot create Item Groups**, which is the labor problem Nexus exists to solve.

**Likely resolution (not yet locked):** Nexus creates the Item Group (master data — only Nexus knows the composition), writes the HubSpot line item referencing it, and **the existing workflow creates the SO**. Each system does what it alone can do. No duplicate SO writer, no cutover of the workflow, no reimplementation.
**If that holds, the SO is ASYNCHRONOUS** — Nexus can't stamp an SO number synchronously. 8b's receipt was already built for this (nullable `soId`/`soCreatedAt` props).

### Nexus ↔ HubSpot product sync — ALREADY BUILT AND LIVE
CC's read-only research report. **8c must build on this, not beside it.**
- **Outbound:** `createProduct` (`hubspot.ts:534-581`) wrapped by `createLeaf` (`leaves.ts:56-169`). PM-initiated from `AddProductModal` LEAF mode. HubSpot-first ordering (same discipline as 7b) — on 4xx/5xx the local row never lands. **ASY mode does not push** (assemblies are quote-scoped).
- **Inbound:** `pullFromHubSpot` → `pullProductsBatch`, batch 100, active-then-archived double pass, resumable retry cursor.
- **Join key is `hubspot_product_id`** (unique partial index where not null), **NOT the SKU** — HubSpot allows blank SKUs and so does Nexus.
- **Push maps only** name / sku / unit_cost / url. Pull maps far more.
- **No `synced_at` / `last_pushed_at`**; sync state inferred from `updated_at` + audit rows. No `leaves.source` — the `nexus_authored` vs `hubspot_pull` discriminator lives only in `audit_log.diff_json.source`.
- **`createProduct` is NOT idempotent** — duplicate `hs_sku` errors on retry (partial protection when SKU present); **with no SKU, retry creates a duplicate HubSpot product.** Banked v1-acceptable per Pattern 32.

**8c SHRINKS by reusing:** the outbound single-shot pattern, the pull scaffolding's `caused_by_audit_id` cascade, HubSpot-first ordering, `hubspot_product_id`-as-join-key, Pattern 32 pre-prod tolerance.

**CC fragility flags to carry into 8c:**
- `_productsClient` module-level singleton cached across hot reloads / warm invocations — match the reset discipline if 8c adds a NetSuite client.
- `DPS_SALES_PIPELINE_ID = "108896657"` is **hardcoded** — do NOT repeat that for a NetSuite subsidiary/location id.
- HubSpot-first orphan risk (`leaves.ts:44-50`, unresolved) — 8c faces the same shape. Reuse `markAccepted`'s version-scoped pending pattern as the reference for cross-system writes.
- **Dev/prod token asymmetry:** Products hit the DEV sandbox in dev; Deals hit PROD. **The same trap applies the moment 8c introduces a NetSuite sandbox split.**'''

s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("replaced" if new in s else "FAILED")
PYEOF

**Context that changed since my earlier draft:** an Item Group is a **pre-existing, priceless template**. Components sit at **$0**; real prices go on the SO line at order time. 8c does **find-or-create**, keyed on a generated unique SKU derived from SKU × composition. # Nexus v2 — Progress Update 7/28/26

**The vision:** Nexus is the assembly-aware layer between how PMs think about products and how NetSuite executes them. It owns the full quote lifecycle: inquiry → build → send → accept → NetSuite handoff. HubSpot seeds data, Nexus owns the flow, NetSuite receives the order.

## What moved since yesterday

Yesterday's update had the quote umbrella as "queued to build." It's **~85% built** — seven of ten steps merged today, including the first production HubSpot writes.

**Shipped:**
- **Preview → Send → Client Review** — full sub-tab lifecycle, quote number continuity, snapshot/versioning
- **Revise-in-place** — a sent or accepted quote reopens as an editable new version, same quote number. The customer never sees a different number.
- **Mark Accepted → HubSpot** — recording acceptance moves the deal to Won and pushes the amount. Live, smoke-proven, and fully reversible.
- **Acceptance capture (new design)** — the PM transcribes what the customer actually said, picks the tier they named, and records how it arrived (email/call/portal). One screen, one click.
- **Sales Order receipt** — the pre-send order summary, in review now.

## Design change worth flagging

We found that R8's flow asked PMs to perform **two ceremonies for one customer decision** — accept, then separately select a tier. In practice customers accept and name a tier in the same breath.

The fix wasn't collapsing them, which would have moved the irreversible NetSuite push to the moment the customer says yes. Instead we split **tier choice** (at acceptance, reversible) from **tier commitment** (at the lock, irreversible). Design was re-cut and re-delivered mid-build; the ceremony collapses without moving the point of no return.

## The NetSuite discovery pass — the big one

We spent today scoping the NetSuite integration properly rather than building against assumptions, and it changed the design substantially. **Thanks to Aisha and Melinda for fast, precise answers.**

**What we learned:**

- **Item Groups are priceless templates**, not priced records. Components sit at $0; real prices go on the Sales Order at order time. We had it backwards, and building on the wrong model would have meant Nexus mutating master data on every order.
- **Grouping is driven by how the customer wants to be invoiced** — Dr. Squatch wants packaging and freight as one unit price, so it's amortized in and broken into a group in NetSuite. Nexus already computes exactly this decomposition natively.
- **Accounting is currently building these by hand.** That's the labor Nexus is meant to eliminate, and it's now the core of the NetSuite step.
- **Everything on a NetSuite Sales Order traces back to HubSpot** — Sales Rep, Project Manager, SharePoint folder, and the Project record itself. That nearly inverted our architecture, and we're settling the final shape now.
- **One live conflict found:** the existing "auto-create NetSuite sales order from won deal" workflow enrolls on the same deal stage Nexus sets. It has to be handled deliberately at cutover, not discovered in production. Now tracked.

**NetSuite sandbox connection is set up** — integration record, role, and tokens are in place, with Item Group creation permission confirmed. Read-only probes next.

## Still to come

- **Sales Order push** — the one irreversible step. Held until the NetSuite config questions close, by design.
- Pricing CTA rewire, audit integration, full lifecycle smoke, designer audit
- **Before launch:** Microsoft SSO (pending IT), pre-launch cleanup, SPEC compliance audit, full automated test pass

## Timing

**Target v1: early-to-mid August.** Slipping slightly from the earlier late-July/early-Aug estimate — the NetSuite discovery was worth the day and surfaced things that would have cost more later.

**After v1:** Operations dashboard (BOM generation, packing lists, freight/shipment tracking) → then v2 NetSuite-direct integration with native BOMs.

**Bottom line:** PMs can go Setup → Costs → Pricing end-to-end today. The post-send lifecycle is nearly complete. What's left is the NetSuite handoff, and we now understand exactly what it has to do.

---

Two things to check before you post:

**The date.** Your update said 7/27; today's the 28th. Assuming yesterday's went out on the 27th.

**The timing call is yours.** I moved it to "early-to-mid August" because 8c has open external dependencies — NetSuite probes, the OTC taxonomy work, the workflow cutover. If you'd rather hold the original target, say so and I'll revert it; I'd just rather the slip be deliberate than discovered.

The distinguishing detail: the endpoint is a POST, so the write-safety comes from NetSuite's parser rejecting non-SELECT statements, not from the HTTP verb.

Cheap hardening, worth asking CC for: **assert client-side that every SuiteQL statement begins with `SELECT`** before it's sent. One line, makes the guarantee structural instead of documentary. **Two big findings, and one confusion to clear up before you touch anything.**

## The confusion: SuiteAnalytics Workbook is already granted

You saved it before this run. CC's report says "standing by for role expansion" — but the permission is in place, and CC still got denied on every list query and the metadata catalog.

Two possibilities:

1. **The script ran with a cached credential or before the permission propagated.** NetSuite role changes sometimes need a session cycle; token-based auth usually picks them up immediately, but not always.
2. **SuiteAnalytics Workbook isn't the permission that gates REST `?q=` and the metadata catalog.** Metadata catalog returned `401 INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION`, which is a different error than the list queries' `400 USER_ERROR` — suggesting *two* distinct missing permissions, not one.

**Tell CC the permission is already granted and have it re-run.** If it still fails, we're looking for different permissions, and the metadata-catalog 401 is the thread to pull.

## Finding 1 — `custitem_dps_hubspot_product_type` changes 8c-0

**Every DPS item already carries HubSpot's `hs_product_type` value.** The cross-system taxonomy is bridged on the NetSuite side.

That means 8c-0 as scoped — schema field on `leaves`, mapper both directions, backfill, `AddProductModal` UI — **may not be needed at all.** CC's option (a) or (b) discriminates at read time with zero Nexus schema change.

I'd lean **(b)** — read `hs_product_type` from HubSpot rather than NetSuite. HubSpot is the upstream owner, Nexus already pulls that domain, and it doesn't require a NetSuite round-trip during SO construction. But (a) has a real argument too: reading from NetSuite means Nexus classifies using exactly the value NetSuite will act on.

**Either way, 8c-0 shrinks from a four-part sub-step to a read-time lookup.** That's a significant scope reduction.

## Finding 2 — Item Groups have no `externalId`

Absent on record 64026. Two consequences:

- Nexus must **set externalId explicitly** on every group it creates
- **Existing hand-built groups have none** — so find-or-create can only match them by `itemId`, which makes A4's uniqueness question load-bearing rather than incidental

This is the reconciliation problem we banked, now with a mechanism.

**Incoterms aren't a record type** (404, not a permission error) — plain text passthrough from `incoterms_snapshot`. Simplifies the payload.

Item Group Conventions — Accounting Responses
Context
Below is a summary of how Aisha currently creates and maintains NetSuite Item Groups after orders are received from HubSpot. The purpose is to document the current business process so that, if Item Groups are created automatically in the future, they behave consistently with the existing process.
1. When does a group get created?
Question:
Some orders have groups (SO2454, Dr. Squatch travel case), others don't (SO2646, Epicuren masks). What's the deciding factor? Is it the presence of freight/duty? One-time charges? Turnkey pricing? Something about the customer or project type? Is that judgment, or a rule that can be stated? Roughly what fraction of orders need one?

Answer:
Generally, an Item Group is created when we are selling a turnkey product and want the customer to see a single line item rather than the individual cost components that make up that product.

The deciding factor is not the customer. It is whether the finished product has additional costs that should be rolled into the selling price while remaining separate for tracking purposes, such as freight, customs, testing, setup, or other allocated costs.

Simple orders or service-only work may not require an Item Group. This is generally a business rule, although there may be historical exceptions.
2. What goes inside it?
Question:
Why are those components included? Is the component list always the item plus cost buckets? Why is each quantity 1? If an order has multiple physical SKUs, is it one group or one group per SKU?

Answer:
An Item Group contains the finished product along with any additional cost components that make up the turnkey selling price.

Typical components include:
• Finished inventory item
• Freight
• Duties/Tariffs
• Customs
• Testing
• Small Batch Setup
• Other one-time charges, as needed

The component list varies depending on the project. Not every Item Group contains the same components.

The quantities are generally entered as 1 because each line represents an allocated portion of the finished unit cost rather than a separate quantity being sold.

If multiple finished products are included on the same Sales Order, Aisha generally creates a separate Item Group for each finished SKU.
3. The OTC codes
Question:
Is there a fixed list of OTC codes? Which cost types map to which codes? What happens if a quote contains a cost with no matching OTC code?

Answer:
Aisha uses predefined OTC items for common cost categories.

Examples include:
• OTC-0012 – Freight / Duties / Tariff(names overlap)but item is mapped to Freight on P&L
• OTC-0036 – Customs Item mapped to Customs on P&L
• OTC-0051 – Small Batch Setup
• OTC-0016 – Micro Testing

Each cost type should consistently map to the same OTC item whenever possible.

If a new cost type does not have an existing OTC item, Aisha creates the appropriate OTC item before it can be used. 
4. Naming and identity
Question:
Is the Item Group tied to the SKU, customer, or order? If the same SKU is quoted again at a different price or cost structure, is the existing group reused or is a new one created?

Answer:
The Item Group is tied to the finished product (SKU), not to the customer or to an individual Sales Order.

When the same SKU is quoted again, Aisha reuses the existing Item Group and updates it if the underlying cost structure has changed.

A new Item Group is not typically created for each quote. Instead, the existing Item Group is updated so it reflects the current configuration of that product.
5. Pricing inside the group
Question:
How are prices assigned to the components? Does the customer see the breakdown? Is there a manual adjustment step after the Item Group is created?

Answer:
The Item Group is structured so that the individual component amounts add up to the final turnkey selling price.

Each component receives its allocated portion of the total selling price.

Because "Display Components on Transactions" is turned off, the customer sees only the finished Item Group as a single line item.

Once the Item Group has been built correctly, little or no manual pricing adjustment is typically required.
6. Classification
Question:
Is Class assigned to the group, the components, or the Sales Order lines? What determines the Class?

Answer:
From a process perspective, Class is generally assigned at the component level rather than solely at the Item Group level.

Examples include:
• Inventory Item → Soft Goods & Accessories
• Freight → Freight
• Packout → Filling & Packout Services
• Testing → One-Time Charges

This supports more meaningful financial reporting by class.
7. The work itself
Question:
How long does it take to build an Item Group? When is it created? What typically requires rework?

Answer:
Creating or updating an Item Group generally takes only a few minutes once all required inventory items and OTC items already exist.

The work is typically performed after the Sales Order is received from HubSpot.

The most common issues include:
• Missing inventory items
• Missing OTC items
• Incorrect cost allocations
• Duplicate Item Groups
• Incorrect Class assignments

The greatest opportunity for automation is reducing manual data entry while ensuring the Item Group accurately reflects the approved quote.
8. The unmatched case
Question:
What happens if an order references a product that does not yet exist in NetSuite? Should the system create the item automatically or require human intervention?

Answer:
If the finished product does not exist in NetSuite, the Sales Order cannot sync correctly and requires Aisha's intervention.

Aisha creates or updates the required inventory item before the Sales Order can proceed.

Inventory items require review because they include General Ledger accounts, costing, units of measure, tax settings, purchasing information, and reporting classifications.

The same approach applies if an OTC item does not yet exist.
Accounting Observation
The following observation is independent of how Item Groups are created but may be helpful when evaluating future enhancements.
Currently, most OTC items are configured as non-inventory/service items. As a result, vendor bills posted against these items are recognized immediately in Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) rather than remaining with inventory until the related customer order is fulfilled.
This creates timing differences between cost recognition and revenue recognition. As part of the monthly close, these timing differences require additional GP reconciliation and manual analysis to align costs with the related revenue.
If these costs represent direct costs of acquiring or producing customer inventory (such as inbound freight, customs, duties, tariffs, testing, or similar costs), there may be an opportunity to evaluate whether the current item configuration best supports the desired accounting treatment of inventory and revenue recognition policies.
The purpose of this observation is simply to document a recurring accounting consideration identified during the monthly close process.

CC → CA — Round 2 findings

Decision-invalidating up front

A1 — externalId IS supported + queryable on Item Groups. But 0 of 33 rows have it populated.

SuiteQL confirmed: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(externalid) FROM item WHERE itemtype='Group' → {total: 33, with_extid: 0}. The field is on the schema and can be filtered on — it's just never set on manually-authored Groups. Find-or-create via externalId is viable IF Nexus explicitly writes it on every Group it creates. Legacy UI-Groups don't collide (they have no externalId to collide with) but also can't be found via that key — 8c will only find its own.

A4 — itemId is de facto unique across all 33 Item Groups (zero duplicates from GROUP BY itemid HAVING COUNT(*) > 1). So itemId CAN serve as a join key. Whether it's constrained unique or merely happens to be — metadata catalog blocked (see below), so can't confirm hard uniqueness. But the pragmatic behavior is unique-in-practice. The generated-SKU scheme via itemId is a fallback if externalId writes fail; via externalId is the cleaner primary.

REST list-and-filter WORKS without SuiteQL for basic conditions. Confirmed:
- GET /record/v1/itemGroup?limit=5 → 200, totalResults: 33
- GET /record/v1/customer?q=companyName START_WITH "Epicuren" → 200, found id=131860
- GET /record/v1/itemGroup?q=externalId START_WITH "NX" → 200, 0 items (query syntax accepted, no matches — proves q= executes)

But:
- ?q=externalId IS_NOT_NULL → 400 INVALID_PARAMETER "Invalid search query". IS_NOT_NULL not supported in REST ?q= syntax (SuiteQL WHERE clauses accept it; REST OData does not).

Then the metadata catalog isn't gated by a role permission in this version — it's something else. Three possibilities, cheapest first:

1. **It's not a Setup permission at all.** In some versions the catalog requires the role to have access to the *record type* being described, which we have — meaning the 401 is about something other than permissions.
2. **The endpoint path is wrong.** Some versions use `/services/rest/record/v1/metadata-catalog/{type}` and others expect an `Accept: application/schema+json` or `application/swagger+json` header. A 401 rather than 404 is odd, but NetSuite's error codes aren't always precise.

chat_messages.text:
**Contradiction resolved — and Aisha's model wins on both counts.** Melinda's §5 was describing the *effect* (components' allocated amounts sum to the turnkey price on the SO), not the mechanism.

Melinda's line is decisive: *"When setting up a group you do not have a field to add cost."* That matches CC's probe exactly — members returned as `{item ref, lineNumber, quantity, taxSchedule}`, no price field. Not a projection artifact. **The field doesn't exist.**

**Both questions answered:**

1. **Components are priceless.** Prices live on the SO line, entered at order time. *"If that price changes the item on the SO is updated"* — the SO changes, not the group.
2. **The group is reused, not recreated or updated.** Aisha: *"I usually keep the group if the items are the same."* Same components → same group → different amounts per SO. Melinda's "update it if the cost structure changed" meant updating the SO, not the group.

**So the design I specified holds, unchanged:**

- Identity = **composition only** (which components). Not prices, not quantities, not destinations, not tiers.
- **Find-or-create.** Same composition → reuse. Different composition → new group.
- **No group mutation per order.** No concurrency race, no historical-SO corruption.
- One group, many lines — confirmed by the Dr. Squatch invoice.

**One new detail from Melinda worth capturing:** *"Those individual items for inventory carry the prices, and inside of those you can set up tiered amounts."* Inventory items support **tiered pricing natively** in NetSuite. Not something 8c needs — Nexus supplies the rate per SO line — but if it's already configured on existing items, a rate Nexus sends could conflict with a price level on the item. Worth a follow-up probe on `inventoryitem/41350`'s price levels before 8c writes rates.

**Nothing changes in the handover's decision table.** It was built on Aisha's answers and they've now been confirmed by both the API and Melinda.

Worth closing the loop in Slack so it's settled on the record — something like: *"Got it, thanks both. Confirming: group components are $0, prices go on the SO line, and the group is reused when the components are the same. That's what we'll build."*

## 8a — Acceptance capture · **MERGED (#147)**

DB + HubSpot, zero NetSuite.

The PM transcribes what the customer said, picks the tier they named, records how it arrived (email/call/portal). One screen, one click. Writes `customer_accepted_tier_id` + `customer_response_channel`, plus a second review-feed row carrying the transcription. Pushes HubSpot stage → Won **and** amount in a single atomic PATCH. External-first: push fails, nothing is written, quote stays `sent`.

Migration 0042, additive-nullable. 43/43 smoke. Below-floor server guard patched in later via #148.

**Reversible.** Rollback and revise-from-accepted both work.

---

## 8b — Sales Order receipt UI · **HOLD (#148)**

All three visual states, **zero NetSuite calls**.

`SalesOrderTab` + `OrderReceipt` + `SendOrderModal`. Three states, one layout: **pending** (what's about to be sent), **failed** (order didn't reach NetSuite), **record** (the permanent post-lock record). Twelve dev-switcher variants.

Three structural locks so `complete` stays unreachable: no writer exists · a prebuild verifier fails the build on any `status: "complete"` write · the CTA is disabled with an honest caption.

**CB found 7 items.** P0 turned out to be a fixture defect, not product — CC hardcoded an approximate HubSpot amount in the provisioning script. But the trace surfaced a real production gap: after revise + cost edits, the pushed amount can diverge from the order total with no PM-visible signal. Shipping a divergence flag in 8b as a result.

Open: P1 (disabled CTA gives no reason), P2 (`complete` claims read-only, strip says REVISITABLE), P3–P5.

**What passed:** the failure states. CB confirmed both facts get equal weight and wouldn't walk away thinking everything failed. Highest-risk surface, independently verified.

---

## 8c — NetSuite push · **HELD** — the only irreversible step

**Architecture is still open.** Two candidates:

- **(a)** Nexus pushes the SO directly. Means reproducing everything the existing HubSpot→NetSuite workflow does — project auto-creation, SharePoint links, sales rep, PM, per-line class, ~94 populated fields.
- **(b)** Nexus creates the Item Group and writes the HubSpot line item; the existing workflow creates the SO. Much smaller, but the SO becomes asynchronous.

Evidence keeps pointing at (b). Not decided.

**What's settled:**
- **Item Groups are priceless templates.** Components at $0, no price field exists. Prices go on the SO line. Confirmed by API *and* by Aisha and Melinda after they initially disagreed.
- **Find-or-create keyed on composition.** Reuse when components match. One group, many lines.
- **Identity via `externalId`** — supported and queryable, but 0 of 33 existing groups have it. Nexus only ever finds its own; legacy groups need reconciliation at cutover.
- **NetSuite does not recompute totals.** `subtotal = total = Σ line amounts`. Reconciliation is safe end-to-end.
- **"Pending Fulfillment" verified live.** Terms are free text. Deal linkage goes in `custbody_dps_deal_id`.
- **OTC discrimination is bridged NetSuite-side** — `custitem_dps_hubspot_product_type` + class (61 = One Time Charges, 60 = Freight). **8c-0 likely collapses from a four-part sub-step to a read-time lookup.**
- **Unmatched items block, never auto-create.** Melinda was explicit — inventory items carry GL accounts, costing, UoM, tax config.

content.text:
## 8a — Acceptance capture · **MERGED (#147)**

DB + HubSpot, zero NetSuite.

The PM transcribes what the customer said, picks the tier they named, records how it arrived (email/call/portal). One screen, one click. Writes `customer_accepted_tier_id` + `customer_response_channel`, plus a second review-feed row carrying the transcription. Pushes HubSpot stage → Won **and** amount in a single atomic PATCH. External-first: push fails, nothing is written, quote stays `sent`.

Migration 0042, additive-nullable. 43/43 smoke. Below-floor server guard patched in later via #148.

**Reversible.** Rollback and revise-from-accepted both work.

---

## 8b — Sales Order receipt UI · **HOLD (#148)**

All three visual states, **zero NetSuite calls**.

`SalesOrderTab` + `OrderReceipt` + `SendOrderModal`. Three states, one layout: **pending** (what's about to be sent), **failed** (order didn't reach NetSuite), **record** (the permanent post-lock record). Twelve dev-switcher variants.

Three structural locks so `complete` stays unreachable: no writer exists · a prebuild verifier fails the build on any `status: "complete"` write · the CTA is disabled with an honest caption.

**CB found 7 items.** P0 turned out to be a fixture defect, not product — CC hardcoded an approximate HubSpot amount in the provisioning script. But the trace surfaced a real production gap: after revise + cost edits, the pushed amount can diverge from the order total with no PM-visible signal. Shipping a divergence flag in 8b as a result.

Open: P1 (disabled CTA gives no reason), P2 (`complete` claims read-only, strip says REVISITABLE), P3–P5.

**What passed:** the failure states. CB confirmed both facts get equal weight and wouldn't walk away thinking everything failed. Highest-risk surface, independently verified.

---

## 8c — NetSuite push · **HELD** — the only irreversible step

**Architecture is still open.** Two candidates:

- **(a)** Nexus pushes the SO directly. Means reproducing everything the existing HubSpot→NetSuite workflow does — project auto-creation, SharePoint links, sales rep, PM, per-line class, ~94 populated fields.
- **(b)** Nexus creates the Item Group and writes the HubSpot line item; the existing workflow creates the SO. Much smaller, but the SO becomes asynchronous.

Evidence keeps pointing at (b). Not decided.

**What's settled:**
- **Item Groups are priceless templates.** Components at $0, no price field exists. Prices go on the SO line. Confirmed by API *and* by Aisha and Melinda after they initially disagreed.
- **Find-or-create keyed on composition.** Reuse when components match. One group, many lines.
- **Identity via `externalId`** — supported and queryable, but 0 of 33 existing groups have it. Nexus only ever finds its own; legacy groups need reconciliation at cutover.
- **NetSuite does not recompute totals.** `subtotal = total = Σ line amounts`. Reconciliation is safe end-to-end.
- **"Pending Fulfillment" verified live.** Terms are free text. Deal linkage goes in `custbody_dps_deal_id`.
- **OTC discrimination is bridged NetSuite-side** — `custitem_dps_hubspot_product_type` + class (61 = One Time Charges, 60 = Freight). **8c-0 likely collapses from a four-part sub-step to a read-time lookup.**
- **Unmatched items block, never auto-create.** Melinda was explicit — inventory items carry GL accounts, costing, UoM, tax config.

**Blockers:** architecture decision · workflow cutover (the auto-create SO workflow enrolls on the stage `markAccepted` sets — same-operation switch required) · two ops tasks (a first-class HubSpot company ID field on customers, and whether Nexus should suppress NetSuite's user events/emails).

content.text: but how do we associate the hubspot line items to the item group?

chat_messages.text:
You don't associate them — and that's the point. **The SKU is the association.**

Look at the DRSQ line: it carries `hs_sku = TCS-BAR-01`, and nothing else pointing at a group. NetSuite matches that SKU to its item record. That record *happens to be* an Item Group with three members configured. NetSuite expands it on the SO.

HubSpot has no concept of a group. It sends one SKU and a rate. The expansion is entirely NetSuite-side, driven by what type of item record that SKU resolves to.

**Which means the association happens at group-creation time, not at line-item time.** When Nexus creates the Item Group, the group's `itemId` *is* the SKU that HubSpot will later reference. Nexus writes one line item with that SKU. NetSuite does the rest.

**But this exposes something important:** the SKU has to be identical on both sides, and that's the actual coupling.

Which loops back to the naming question. We'd decided on a **generated unique SKU** for the group. But that generated SKU now has to be the SKU Nexus writes on the HubSpot line item, and it's what the customer sees on the invoice — `TCS-BAR-01` appears on the invoice line.

So the generated identifier isn't internal plumbing. It's customer-facing and cross-system. Three consequences:

1. It must be **stable** — the same composition must always produce the same SKU, or a requote creates a second group and a divergent line item
2. It must be **readable enough** for the invoice — a hash-suffixed code appearing on a customer document is a problem
3. It has to not **collide** with existing SKUs like `TCS-BAR-01`, which are hand-authored

**And a question I can't answer from here:** where does the group's SKU come from today? `TCS-BAR-01` is also the SKU of the physical inventory item inside the group (`inventoryitem/41350` was named `TCS-BAR-01 Dr. Squatch - Bar Soap Travel Case + UC`). So the group and its member component share a SKU prefix. Whether NetSuite permits an exact duplicate, or whether they differ in a way the screenshots don't show, matters for how Nexus generates the group's identifier.

That's worth one probe — compare the group's `itemId` against member `41350`'s `itemId` exactly.

**Design (b) is dead. My inference was wrong.**

Aisha is unambiguous: *"we have to remove the line item and add the group."* The workflow does **not** expand groups. It creates a flat SO from HubSpot line items, then Aisha manually deletes those lines and swaps in the Item Group. SO2454's grouped structure was hand-built after the fact.

So the SKU-as-association mechanism I described doesn't exist. NetSuite never resolved `TCS-BAR-01` to a group — Aisha put the group there.

**What this means:**

Writing HubSpot line items gets us a flat SO that still needs manual rework. It automates nothing that matters — the labor Nexus is meant to eliminate is exactly the step Aisha described, and (b) doesn't touch it.

**Where that leaves the architecture:**

- **(a) — Nexus pushes the SO directly**, with the group already on it. Back on the table, and it's now the only option that eliminates the manual step. Cost is reproducing what the workflow does: Project auto-creation, ~94 custbody fields, sales rep, PM, SharePoint, per-line class.
- **(c) — a hybrid I hadn't considered:** Nexus creates the Item Group *and* writes a HubSpot line item referencing the group's SKU. The workflow creates the SO from it. If the group's SKU is in NetSuite's item list — Aisha says *"groups are... inventory items in our NS product inv list"* — the workflow's item lookup may resolve it like any other item. The line would land already-grouped, no manual swap.

**(c) is worth checking before we commit to (a).** It's the difference between a small build and a large one. The question is narrow: **when the workflow looks up a SKU, does it search only inventory items, or all item types including groups?** If groups are searchable, (c) works. If the lookup is type-filtered, it doesn't.

Aisha's phrasing suggests groups *are* in the same list. That's suggestive, not proof.

**Two ways to test, both cheap:**
- CC probes whether the workflow's item-matching field exists on group records (it matched on something — likely SKU or name)
- Or: create a test HubSpot deal with a line item using a group's SKU, and see what the workflow produces. That's a real write, so it needs your call.

**My recommendation:** ask Aisha directly — *"if I put TCS-BAR-01 as the SKU on a HubSpot line item, would the sales order come over with the group already on it, or would it fail to match?"* She'll know from experience whether that's ever happened.

That's the missing piece, and it changes the naming picture.

**The group and the inventory item are separate records with separate SKUs:**
- `TCS-BAR-01` — the physical inventory item, the SKU HubSpot sends
- `TCS-BAR-01-G` — the Item Group, created in NetSuite, `-G` suffix

So Aisha's workflow is: HubSpot sends `TCS-BAR-01` → SO gets a flat line → she removes it and adds `TCS-BAR-01-G`.

**And it means there IS a convention after all** — `-G` for group. That's more programmable than the `-02` / `-I` / `-D` answer we got earlier, which was about *variants* of a group, not the group itself.

**But it still doesn't tell us whether the workflow can match `-G`.** Aisha's "it would come as a single line item" is still ambiguous — and now I suspect she was answering about `TCS-BAR-01`, the inventory item, not `TCS-BAR-01-G`.

**The question to ask, using the right SKU:**

> If a HubSpot line item had SKU `TCS-BAR-01-G` — the group, not the base item — would the sales order come over with the group already on it, or would the workflow fail to find a match?

That's the whole fork. If the workflow resolves `-G`, design (c) works: Nexus creates the group, writes one line with the `-G` SKU, and the manual swap disappears. If it can't match a group record, we're on design (a).

**Two things worth noting regardless of the answer:**

**The naming rule is now partly discovered, not invented.** Base SKU + `-G`. That's better than a generated hash — readable on the invoice, consistent with existing practice. What we still need is what happens when the *same* base SKU needs two groups with different compositions — that's where the earlier `-02` / `-I` / `-D` ad-hockery came in, and it's the part Nexus has to make deterministic.

**CC's probe should confirm this directly** — fetch `itemGroup/64026` and check whether its `itemId` is actually `TCS-BAR-01-G` rather than `TCS-BAR-01`. Round 1 reported `itemId: "TCS-BAR-01 DRSQ Bar Soap Travel Case w/ UC"`, with no `-G`. Either there are two group records, or the `-G` convention is newer than that record. Worth resolving — it's cheap and it's the actual field Nexus would write.

**Design (c) is dead. Design (b) is dead. We're on (a).**

The workflow can't match a group SKU. Nexus writing HubSpot line items produces a flat SO that Aisha still has to rework by hand — which automates nothing.

**So 8c is what the original brief said: Nexus pushes the Sales Order directly, with the Item Group already on it.**

That's the larger build, and now it's the only one that eliminates the manual step.

**What Nexus has to reproduce**, from SO2646's 94-field inventory:
- The SO itself — customer, subsidiary, location, class, currency, form, status, terms, ship date
- Line items with the group SKU, quantities, rates
- `custbody_dps_deal_id`, `custbody_sharepoint_link`, `custbody_dps_project_service_s`, `custbody_dps_project_source`, `custbody_dps_est_invoice_date`, `custbody_dps_transaction_hold`, and the rest
- Sales rep ← HubSpot deal owner · Project Manager ← HubSpot custom field · SharePoint ← HubSpot custom field
- **And the Project record**, which the workflow currently auto-creates (`custbody_dps_auto_generate_project: true` — so it may be a NetSuite-side trigger rather than something the workflow builds; worth confirming)

**Which means the deal-property pull you asked about earlier is now needed.** That's the HubSpot API work — deal owner, PM, SharePoint link, project source, project services, est. invoice date.

**And the workflow cutover comes back.** If Nexus creates the SO, the existing workflow must be disabled in the same operation or every accepted quote gets two SOs.

---

**One thing worth checking before we commit**, because it could still shrink this: does the workflow have a way to be *told* which item to use? It reads HubSpot line items — if the SKU field is what it matches on and groups aren't matchable, is there any other property on a HubSpot line item that maps to a NetSuite item reference? The line-item editor showed a "NetSuite information → NetSuite Subsidiary" section, which suggests some NetSuite-aware fields exist on line items. Worth expanding that section fully.

If there's a NetSuite item ID field on the HubSpot line item, (c) revives.

If not: 8c is design (a), and it's a bigger step than 8a or 8b. Worth updating the handover and re-scoping before CC opens it.

# CA → CC — 8c re-scope inputs (read-only, no build)

**Do not start 8c.** Two read-only questions whose answers shape the re-scope brief.

## 1. `custbody_dps_auto_generate_project` — who creates the Project?

SO2646 carries `custbody_dps_auto_generate_project: true`, and a NetSuite Project record exists (`174 Epicuren - Pro Masks`) with its own PM, SharePoint link, and Opportunity reference.

**Does the HubSpot workflow create that Project, or does NetSuite create it in response to the flag on the SO?**

If NetSuite-side, Nexus sets one boolean and gets the Project for free. If workflow-side, Nexus has to build the Project record too — a second create in an already-large step.

Answerable from the Project record's `createdDate` and source versus the SO's, or from SO2646's system notes. **This is the single biggest swing in 8c's scope** — it's either one field or a whole additional object.

## 2. HubSpot deal properties Nexus doesn't currently read

Under design (a), Nexus sources what the workflow currently reads. Report which of these Nexus already has versus needs to pull:

- Deal owner → SO Sales Rep
- Project Manager (custom property)
- Deal Folder Link / SharePoint
- Project Service(s), Project Category, Sourcing Location, Business Segment
- Client PO#, Invoice Date (est), Production Ship Date (est), Priority, Deal Type

Nexus already reads `hubspot_deal_id` on projects. **What else is already pulled, and what's net-new API surface?**

Answer from the codebase — no HubSpot calls needed.

---

## Context: architecture is now design (a)

Aisha confirmed the mechanism. **NetSuite does not expand Item Groups from a SKU reference.** The workflow creates a flat SO; Aisha then removes those lines and manually adds the group. A group SKU on a HubSpot line item **fails to match** — she confirmed directly.

So writing HubSpot line items automates nothing. **Nexus pushes the Sales Order itself, with the group already on it.**

**Banked from your `-G` probe:**
- **`externalId` is the identity, not the name.** Three eras of naming across one base SKU makes any name-based key unsafe.
- **Collision detection scans `itemid LIKE '<base>-G%'`**, not equality.
- Open: if a generated display name collides with an Era A/B record, what's the deterministic disambiguation? `itemId` uniqueness is likely enforced (0 duplicates across 33) but unconfirmed.

**Also still open, for the brief:** the workflow cutover — disabled in the same operation that ships `markComplete`, or every accepted quote gets two SOs.

Answer 1 and 2, then hold. #148 merges on CB's re-walk.

Service fees included under **both** allocation policies. 8c asserts the three consumers read the same primitive; it does not compare independently-derived figures.

- **Pattern 52 freeze at `complete`** — 27 columns, canonical list from Architect Q5. Includes both `pending_hubspot_from_stage_id` and `pending_hubspot_from_stage_version` (frozen at NULL to block repopulation by future revert/hotfix flows).
- **Conditional HubSpot amount patch** (§7.2 amendment) — override case only. NetSuite SO first (the irreversible act), amount patch after. **Patch failure must NOT block `complete`** — the SO exists; a stale amount is a reporting nit.
- **`customer_target_tier_label`** (text, 3 populated) is a DIFFERENT concept — captured at scenario creation, not acceptance. **DECIDED: no pre-highlight** on the chips. Stale scenario data must not bias the field the PM should read carefully.
- Below-floor gate — T4 disabled in both pickers, advance blocked, R5 admin-override path.
- NetSuite payload consumes the **Slice-11.5 ASY/LEAF adapter** (NOT deprecated `quote_skus`).
- **Turnkey totals depend on Slice-11 F1.5** (shipped).
- `.r8-proto` / `.r8-dn` are prototype-only — **strip in production.**

### Step 9 — Pricing CTA rewire + audit + Pattern 47 (small)
- Pricing "Send to customer" CTA → Quote > Preview Quote.
- Audit integration: distinct actions `quote_accepted`/`quote_completed`/`quote_reverted` (NOT generic `quote_advanced`).
- Pattern 47 on the tier picker + AddEntry input.

- Full CB smoke of the 5-sub-tab lifecycle.
- CD designer audit vs **R9.1** (not R8).
- Architect verification at impl completion.
- **CLAUDE.md close-out banks** (see §6).

Originally scoped as four pieces (schema field on `leaves` + mapper both directions + backfill + `AddProductModal` UI). **No longer needed.**

**The probe found the taxonomy is ALREADY BRIDGED on both sides:**
- **HubSpot line items carry `hs_product_type`** — verified on the Epicuren deal (`OTC-0016` → "One Time Charges"; `EPICURENMSK1` → "Filling and Packout Services").
- **Every NetSuite item carries `custitem_dps_hubspot_product_type`** with the same value, PLUS `class` (id 61 = "One Time Charges", id 60 = "Freight") PLUS `itemType` (`NonInvtPart` for OTC, `InvtPart` for physical).

Read at push time. No Nexus schema change, no backfill, no UI work. Confirm Nexus's `product_types` taxonomy maps 1:1 to HubSpot's enum and it's done.

#### 8c — NetSuite SO push — **RE-SCOPED to DESIGN (a)**. HELD.

### 🔴 THE ARCHITECTURE DECISION — read this before anything else

Three candidate designs were evaluated against live evidence. **Two are dead.**

| | Design | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Nexus pushes the Sales Order directly, with the Item Group already on it | ✅ **ADOPTED** — the only one that eliminates the manual step |
| **(b)** | Nexus writes HubSpot line items; the existing workflow creates the SO | ❌ **DEAD** — produces a flat SO that Aisha must still rework by hand |
| **(c)** | Nexus creates the group, then writes a HubSpot line item referencing the group's SKU | ❌ **DEAD** — Aisha: a group SKU on a HubSpot line item **"would fail to match"** |

**The mechanism CA initially inferred was WRONG, and it's worth recording why.** From SO2454 and the DRSQ invoice it looked as though HubSpot sent `TCS-BAR-01` and NetSuite auto-expanded it into the group. **It does not.** Aisha, verbatim:

> *"usually when i send items that are amortized over, i only add the line item of the component and then within ns i do the grouping"* · *"no we have to remove the line item and add the group"*

The workflow creates a **flat** SO from HubSpot line items. Aisha then **deletes those lines and adds the Item Group by hand**. SO2454's grouped structure was hand-built after the fact. **That manual swap IS the labor Nexus exists to eliminate** — and only design (a) touches it.

Also: the group and the physical item are **separate records with separate SKUs** — `TCS-BAR-01` (inventory item) vs `TCS-BAR-01-G` (the group).

### What 8c builds

1. **Item Group find-or-create** — see §4A for the full decision table
2. **Sales Order create**, with the group on it, mirroring SO2646's field surface
3. **~10 new HubSpot deal properties** + schema companion (see §4B)
4. **`markComplete`** — writes `accepted_tier_id`, `netsuite_so_id`, `netsuite_pushed_at`, `completed_by_user_id`, `completed_at`; flips `accepted` → `complete`
5. **Workflow cutover** — operational, see §4A

Auto-create fires for **turnkey segment only** (~60% attach rate), and Amy **manually reassigns** recurring turnkey orders to existing Projects. Melinda's reason — *"we track a lot of the raws inside the project since we are not using BOMs currently"* — points at the **post-v1 operations dashboard**, which is where this belongs. Nexus leaves `custbody_dps_auto_generate_project` at its default and does not touch Projects.
  - ⚠️ **Cutover check:** is the Project automation triggered by the DEAL or by the SO? If SO-triggered and owned by the workflow we disable, Project creation dies silently and Amy finds out the hard way. **Check HubSpot for a second, Project-related workflow before cutover.**
- Design (b) and (c) — dead, see above.
- `sales_order_finalized` as a cutover mechanism — **dropped.** A HubSpot deal boolean with an on-the-nose name, but nobody knows what writes it and it's empty on a deal that DID get an SO. Cheap to revisit: check the SO workflow's enrollment conditions for a reference to it. If the workflow self-guards on it, the cutover becomes a property read instead of a coordinated switch.

### Watch items

SuiteQL sweep of all 33 groups. Same base SKU, three conventions:

| Era | Period | Pattern | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | 2024 | `<base>-G` or numbered `-G1`…`-G5` | `TCS-BAR-01-G1` … `-G5` (ids 54280-54286), `Sarah Wragge Wellness - Pouches-G` |

| **C** | 2026 (current) | `<prefix>-<descriptive>-G` | `WFG842-Wild Adventure-G`, `WFL844-G` |

**Consequences:** a Nexus-generated `TCS-BAR-01-G` walks straight into a space already occupied by Era A's `-G1..G5` and Era B's bare `TCS-BAR-01`. Numbered variants exist because users **do** create multiple compositions per base SKU. This is why identity lives in `externalId` and the collision scan uses `LIKE`, not `=`.

### Setup COMPLETE (sandbox)

**Still 403:** Projects (`/job/*`) — not needed, Projects are out of scope. **Opportunity** — needed only if 8c links `custbody_dps_related_opportunity`.

**Keep `/api/dev/dump-deal-props`** until 8c closes.

**Nexus pushes the Sales Order directly, with the Item Group already on it.** The two HubSpot-line-item routes you may have been planning against are dead:

- **(b)** writing HubSpot line items produces a **flat** SO that Aisha reworks by hand — automates nothing

**The mechanism I inferred earlier was wrong.** NetSuite does not auto-expand an Item Group from a SKU reference. The workflow creates flat lines; Aisha deletes them and adds the group manually. SO2454's grouped structure was hand-built. **That manual swap is the labor we're eliminating.**

This is larger than 8a or 8b. **Come back with a proposed split before opening a branch.** My expectation is roughly:

- **8c-1** — NetSuite adapter + Item Group find-or-create, no SO
- **8c-2** — HubSpot deal-property expansion (§4B) + schema companion

## Item Group find-or-create

**Identity is `externalId`, NOT the name.** Supported and queryable; 0 of 33 existing groups populate it, so Nexus owns the field cleanly — and can only ever *find* its own groups. Legacy groups need reconciliation at cutover; that's known and accepted.

**Key on COMPOSITION** — which components. Not prices, not quantities, not destinations, not tiers. Same composition → reuse. Different composition → new group.

**Components carry NO price.** Verified against the live record: members are `{item ref, lineNumber, quantity, taxSchedule}`, quantity 1, and **the price field does not exist on the group**. Melinda: *"When setting up a group you do not have a field to add cost."* Prices go on the SO line.

**Display name:** `<base>-G`. Carries no identity. **Collision scan uses `itemid LIKE '<base>-G%'`, not equality** — Era A produced `-G1` through `-G5`, and Era B has a bare `TCS-BAR-01`. Three naming eras exist; see §4A.

**Open, and yours to propose:** what Nexus names the *second* group when one base SKU needs two compositions. No human convention exists. My inclination is continuing the numeric pattern (`-G`, `-G2`, `-G3`) since it's already recognisable in the account — but it's display-only, so argue if you see better.

**Description field:** human-readable prose describing the group. Aisha asked for it explicitly; it's blank on existing records.
