Mirror SO2646's field surface. CB walks before the lock merges. Non-negotiable on this one.

# Nexus v2 — Progress Update 7/28/26

**The vision:** Nexus is the assembly-aware layer between how PMs think about products and how NetSuite executes them. It owns the full quote lifecycle: inquiry → build → send → accept → NetSuite handoff. HubSpot seeds data, Nexus owns the flow, NetSuite receives the order.

## Where we are

Yesterday's update had the quote umbrella queued to build. It's now **~85% built** — eight of ten steps merged today, including the first production HubSpot writes.

**Shipped:**
- **Preview → Send → Client Review** — full sub-tab lifecycle, quote number continuity, versioning
- **Revise-in-place** — a sent or accepted quote reopens as a new version, same quote number. The customer never sees a different number.
- **Mark Accepted → HubSpot** — recording acceptance moves the deal to Won and pushes the amount. Live, and fully reversible.
- **Acceptance capture** — the PM transcribes what the customer actually said, picks the tier they named, records how it arrived. One screen, one click.
- **Sales Order screen** — the order summary a PM reads before sending, in all three states: pending, failed, and the permanent record.

**Remaining:** the NetSuite Sales Order push itself, then audit wiring and launch prep.

## The NetSuite work — what today changed

We spent the day scoping the NetSuite integration against the real system instead of building on assumptions. It changed the design substantially, and it was worth every hour.

**Thanks to Aisha, Melinda, and Amy** — their answers redirected the build several times, and one of them saved us from shipping something wrong.

**What we got wrong and caught:**

We had assumed NetSuite automatically expands an Item Group when it sees the SKU on an order. It doesn't. Aisha confirmed that the automation creates a flat order, and she then **removes those lines by hand and adds the Item Group herself.** That manual step is exactly the work Nexus is meant to eliminate — and two of the three designs we were considering wouldn't have touched it. One question changed the architecture.

**What we learned:**

- **Item Groups are templates, not priced records.** Components sit at zero; real prices go on the order. We initially had this backwards, and building on the wrong model would have had Nexus rewriting master data on every order.
- **Grouping reflects how the customer wants to be invoiced** — Dr. Squatch wants packaging and freight as one unit price, so it's amortized in and split into a group in NetSuite. Nexus already computes exactly that breakdown.
- **Group naming has drifted across three eras** — same product, three different conventions over two years. So Nexus will key on a system field rather than the name, and treat the name as display only.
- **One live conflict:** the existing "auto-create NetSuite sales order" automation fires on the same deal stage Nexus sets. It has to be switched over deliberately, not discovered in production. Now tracked.

**Deliberately left alone:** NetSuite Projects. They auto-create for turnkey orders today, nobody remaining knows how that was set up, and Amy manually reassigns recurring work. Rather than reverse-engineer it, we've scoped it out — it belongs with the operations dashboard and BOM work after v1.

**NetSuite sandbox is connected**, with the permissions needed to create Item Groups confirmed.

## Still to come

- **Sales Order push** — the one irreversible step. Building now, held to sandbox testing first.
- Audit integration, full lifecycle testing, design review
- **Before launch:** Microsoft SSO (pending IT), pre-launch cleanup, SPEC compliance audit, full automated test pass

## Timing

**Target v1: mid-August.** Later than the earlier late-July/early-August estimate. The NetSuite step grew once we understood what it actually has to do — Nexus now creates the sales order directly rather than handing off to the existing automation, because that's the only version that removes the manual work.

**After v1:** Operations dashboard (BOM generation, packing lists, freight/shipment tracking) → then v2 NetSuite-direct integration with native BOMs.

**Bottom line:** PMs can go Setup → Costs → Pricing end-to-end today, and the post-send lifecycle is nearly complete. What's left is the NetSuite handoff — and we now know exactly what it has to do, including the manual step it's replacing.

---

Two things to check before posting:

**The timing.** I moved it from "early-to-mid August" to "mid-August." 8c grew today — it's now creating the SO directly rather than delegating, plus ten new HubSpot properties and a schema migration. Your call whether to state that or hold the earlier number.

**Whether to name the mistake.** I kept the "what we got wrong" framing because it credits Aisha for catching it and shows the discovery had a concrete payoff. If that reads as too much self-flagellation for a status update, cut that paragraph and keep the findings list — the substance survives without it.

# Nexus v2 — Progress Update 7/28/26

**The vision:** Nexus is the assembly-aware layer between how PMs think about products and how NetSuite executes them. It owns the full quote lifecycle: inquiry → build → send → accept → NetSuite handoff. HubSpot seeds data, Nexus owns the flow, NetSuite receives the order.

## Where we are

Yesterday's update had the quote umbrella queued to build. It's now **~85% built** — eight of ten steps merged today, including the first production HubSpot writes.

**Shipped:**
- **Preview → Send → Client Review** — full sub-tab lifecycle, quote number continuity, versioning
- **Revise-in-place** — a sent or accepted quote reopens as a new version, same quote number. The customer never sees a different number.
- **Mark Accepted → HubSpot** — recording acceptance moves the deal to Won and pushes the amount. Live, and fully reversible.
- **Acceptance capture** — the PM transcribes what the customer actually said, picks the tier they named, records how it arrived. One screen, one click.
- **Sales Order screen** — the order summary a PM reads before sending, in all three states: pending, failed, and the permanent record.

**Remaining:** the NetSuite Sales Order push itself, then audit wiring and launch prep.

## The NetSuite work — what today changed

We spent the day scoping the NetSuite integration against the real system instead of building on assumptions. It changed the design substantially, and it was worth every hour.

**Thanks to Aisha, Melinda, and Amy** — their answers redirected the build several times, and one of them saved us from shipping something wrong.

**What we got wrong and caught:**

We had assumed NetSuite automatically expands an Item Group when it sees the SKU on an order. It doesn't. Aisha confirmed that the automation creates a flat order, and she then **removes those lines by hand and adds the Item Group herself.** That manual step is exactly the work Nexus is meant to eliminate — and two of the three designs we were considering wouldn't have touched it. One question changed the architecture.

**What we learned:**

- **Item Groups are templates, not priced records.** Components sit at zero; real prices go on the order. We initially had this backwards, and building on the wrong model would have had Nexus rewriting master data on every order.
- **Grouping reflects how the customer wants to be invoiced** — Dr. Squatch wants packaging and freight as one unit price, so it's amortized in and split into a group in NetSuite. Nexus already computes exactly that breakdown.
- **Group naming has drifted across three eras** — same product, three different conventions over two years. So Nexus will key on a system field rather than the name, and treat the name as display only.
- **One live conflict:** the existing "auto-create NetSuite sales order" automation fires on the same deal stage Nexus sets. It has to be switched over deliberately, not discovered in production. Now tracked.

**Deliberately left alone:** NetSuite Projects. They auto-create for turnkey orders today, nobody remaining knows how that was set up, and Amy manually reassigns recurring work. Rather than reverse-engineer it, we've scoped it out — it belongs with the operations dashboard and BOM work after v1.

**NetSuite sandbox is connected**, with the permissions needed to create Item Groups confirmed.

## Still to come

- **Sales Order push** — the one irreversible step. Building now, held to sandbox testing first.
- Audit integration, full lifecycle testing, design review
- **Before launch:** Microsoft SSO (pending IT), pre-launch cleanup, SPEC compliance audit, full automated test pass

## Timing

**Target v1: mid-August.** Later than the earlier late-July/early-August estimate. The NetSuite step grew once we understood what it actually has to do — Nexus now creates the sales order directly rather than handing off to the existing automation, because that's the only version that removes the manual work.

**After v1:** Operations dashboard (BOM generation, packing lists, freight/shipment tracking) → then v2 NetSuite-direct integration with native BOMs.

**Bottom line:** PMs can go Setup → Costs → Pricing end-to-end today, and the post-send lifecycle is nearly complete. What's left is the NetSuite handoff — and we now know exactly what it has to do, including the manual step it's replacing.

---

Two things to check before posting:

**The timing.** I moved it from "early-to-mid August" to "mid-August." 8c grew today — it's now creating the SO directly rather than delegating, plus ten new HubSpot properties and a schema migration. Your call whether to state that or hold the earlier number.

**Whether to name the mistake.** I kept the "what we got wrong" framing because it credits Aisha for catching it and shows the discovery had a concrete payoff. If that reads as too much self-flagellation for a status update, cut that paragraph and keep the findings list — the substance survives without it.

# CA → CC — Step 8c split: **APPROVED with two amendments**

Split is well-reasoned. `netsuite_item_groups` as an authoritative local cache keyed on composition hash is better than round-tripping SuiteQL on every push, and the three-layer lookup (cache → externalId → create) is right. D1 and D2 as throwaway diagnostics is the correct shape.

## Dispositions

**1. Split — take 4, not 3. Overruling your call.**

Your argument against is that a writer-only PR has no user-testable UI so a CB walk would be meaningless in isolation. That's true, and it's not the reason to split.

The reason is that **8c-3 as scoped contains the first NetSuite write, the first `status='complete'` write, the Pattern 52 freeze, the amount patch, and a UI replacement in one diff.** If a sandbox smoke fails, we won't know which of five surfaces caused it.

Split as: **8c-3 = (a) + (b) + (c)** — adapter wiring, SO push, guards. Verified by sandbox smoke, not CB. **8c-4 = (d)** — UI transition, copy sweep, prototype-class strip. CB walks 8c-4.

That gives the write path its own review under sandbox verification, and the UI its own under human eyes. Neither gate is doing double duty. Mid-slice checkpoints on a single branch aren't a substitute for a merge gate.

**2. Description format — don't guess. Ask Aisha.**

Your default is reasonable but she requested this field specifically and will read it daily. One message: *"When Nexus writes the group description, what would be most useful — the component list, the customer and product, the quote number, or something else?"* Cheap, and it's her field.

**3. `HUBSPOT_PM_PROPERTY`** — Edward set it; confirm scope with him. If preview is missing, add it — 8c-2's verification needs it.

**4. Run D1 now, D2 during 8c-2 prep.** D1 gates 8c-1 and could escalate. D2 only needs to land before 8c-3 merges.

## Amendments

**A. `markComplete` ordering — you have it as "external-first per §5.1", but this is a two-external-system flow.** Be explicit about the sequence and where the tx boundary sits:

1. Guards (below-floor, revisable-state) — before any external call
2. Item Group find-or-create — NetSuite write #1
3. SO create — NetSuite write #2, **the irreversible act**
4. DB tx: freeze + `status='complete'`
5. HubSpot amount patch — **after** the tx, failure never blocks

If step 4 fails after step 3 succeeds, the SO exists and the quote isn't `complete`. **What does retry do?** It must not create a second SO. Your `netsuite_so_pushes` unique key on `(quote_id, accepted_tier_id)` should cover it — confirm the retry path checks that table *before* attempting the push, not just relying on the constraint to reject.

This is the same class as #145's `from_stage` poisoning: the recovery path needs to be idempotent, not just the call.

**B. Below-floor guard evaluates against `accepted_tier_id`, not `customer_accepted_tier_id`** — you have this right and it's a good catch. Add one thing: **the override path is where below-floor becomes reachable at all.** R5 specifies an admin override for below-floor tiers. Confirm whether `markComplete` blocks unconditionally or admits an override token; if the latter, that's a separate authorization surface and I want to see it before it ships.

## Confirmations wanted

- `composition_hash` — what exactly is hashed? "Sorted `{leaf_id, quantity}` tuples per assembly" — does that include **which OTC codes** are in the group? Two compositions differing only by a customs line must hash differently.
- `netsuite_item_groups` — is `composition_hash` unique **globally** or per base SKU? Same composition under two different base SKUs must be two groups.

---

**Go on D1. Branch 8c-1 and 8c-2 once D1 is clean.** Hold 8c-3 until I've seen the ordering answer.

chat_messages.text:
Answered. **Description = customer + component list + SKU.**

Which raises one thing worth resolving before CC builds the generator: **if the description carries the customer, the group isn't reusable across customers.**

Composition keying says same components → same group. But a description reading "Dr. Squatch — Bar Soap Travel Case + Freight + Customs — TCS-BAR-01" is customer-specific. Two customers ordering an identical composition would share one group whose description names only the first.

Three possibilities, and Aisha's answer implies the second:

1. Compositions are effectively customer-specific anyway — components tied to a particular product build, so the question never arises in practice
2. The group **is** customer-scoped, and the composition key should include customer — which changes the identity rule
3. The description is just a label and nobody minds it naming one customer

Worth one clarifying message, because it affects the key rather than the copy:

> On the description — including the customer means a group is tied to one customer. If two customers ordered the exact same set of components, would you reuse one group, or build a separate group for each?

If she says separate, `composition_hash` needs the customer in it, and reuse becomes much narrower — closer to per-customer-per-product than per-composition. That's a real design change, not a formatting detail.

Pass the format to CC either way; just flag the key question as open.

# CA → CC — Item Group identity CHANGED. Read before 8c-1.

**Aisha's answer on the description surfaced a key change, not a formatting detail.**

**Groups are per CUSTOMER × composition, not composition alone.** Two customers ordering an identical component set get **separate groups**. Confirmed directly.

**`composition_hash` must therefore include the customer.** Your proposed hash — sorted `{leaf_id, quantity}` tuples — is insufficient on its own. Add the customer identifier, and be explicit about which one: NetSuite customer internal id, HubSpot company id, or the Nexus project's customer reference. Pick the one that's stable and available at push time, and state it.

**Consequences:**
- Reuse is narrower than we scoped — closer to per-customer-per-product than per-composition
- Group count grows with customers, not just compositions. Still bounded, but larger. Worth noting.
- The `-G` collision scan matters more: the same base SKU now legitimately produces multiple groups across customers, so `-G2`, `-G3` will be hit routinely rather than rarely

**Description format — Aisha's spec, verbatim:** customer + component list + SKU, **plus the HubSpot deal ID number.**

That last part is useful beyond the label: it makes the group traceable back to the deal that caused it, which is the only thread accounting would have to follow. Include it.

Draft one example against a real composition and run it past Aisha before generating at scale — she reads these daily and a format she finds awkward is one she'll work around.

**Also confirm:** if a group is customer-scoped and carries a specific deal ID in its description, but gets **reused** on a later order from that customer, the description now names a stale deal. Is that acceptable, or does reuse need a description refresh? Ask Aisha — it's her field and it affects whether the group is ever mutated after creation, which we'd otherwise ruled out entirely.

# CA → CC — Step 8c split: **APPROVED with amendments.** Plus one identity change — read that first.

Split is well-reasoned. `netsuite_item_groups` as an authoritative local cache keyed on composition is better than round-tripping SuiteQL on every push, and the three-layer lookup (cache → externalId → create) is right. D1/D2 as throwaway diagnostics is the correct shape.

---

## 🔴 IDENTITY CHANGE — groups are per CUSTOMER × composition

Aisha's answer on the description surfaced this, and it's a key change, not a formatting detail.

**Two customers ordering an identical component set get SEPARATE groups.** Confirmed directly.

**So `composition_hash` must include the customer.** Sorted `{leaf_id, quantity}` tuples alone is insufficient. Add the customer identifier — and state which one you're using: NetSuite customer internal id, HubSpot company id, or the Nexus project's customer reference. Pick whichever is stable and available at push time.

**Consequences:**
- Reuse is narrower than scoped — closer to per-customer-per-product than per-composition
- Group count grows with customers, not just compositions. Still bounded, but larger.
- The `-G` collision scan matters more: the same base SKU now legitimately produces multiple groups across customers, so `-G2`/`-G3` will be routine rather than rare

**Description format — Aisha's spec:** customer + component list + SKU + **the HubSpot deal ID**.

The deal ID is useful beyond labelling — it's the only thread accounting has back to the deal that caused the group. Include it. **Draft one example against a real composition and run it past Aisha before generating at scale.**

**And confirm with her:** if a customer-scoped group carries a specific deal ID and is later **reused** on a new order, the description names a stale deal. Acceptable, or does reuse need a description refresh? That matters — it's the difference between groups being immutable after creation (what we'd assumed) and being updated on reuse.

---

## Dispositions

**1. Split — take 4, not 3.** Overruling your call.

Your argument against is that a writer-only PR has no user-testable UI, so a CB walk would be meaningless in isolation. True, and not the reason to split.

The reason: **8c-3 as scoped contains the first NetSuite write, the first `status='complete'` write, the Pattern 52 freeze, the amount patch, and a UI replacement in one diff.** If a sandbox smoke fails, we won't know which of five surfaces caused it.

- **8c-3 = (a) + (b) + (c)** — adapter wiring, SO push, guards. Gated by sandbox smoke.
- **8c-4 = (d)** — UI transition, copy sweep, prototype-class strip. Gated by CB walk.

Each gate does one job. Mid-slice checkpoints on one branch aren't a substitute for a merge gate.

**2. Description format** — answered above. Aisha's spec, then validate one example with her.

**3. `HUBSPOT_PM_PROPERTY`** — Edward set it; confirm the scope covers preview. 8c-2's verification needs it there.

**4. D1 now, D2 during 8c-2 prep.** D1 gates 8c-1 and could escalate. D2 only needs to land before 8c-3 merges.

---

## Amendments

**A. `markComplete` ordering — this is a two-external-system flow.** Be explicit about the sequence and the tx boundary:

1. Guards (below-floor, revisable-state) — before any external call
2. Item Group find-or-create — NetSuite write #1
3. SO create — NetSuite write #2, **the irreversible act**
4. DB tx: freeze + `status='complete'`
5. HubSpot amount patch — **after** the tx; failure never blocks

**If step 4 fails after step 3 succeeds, the SO exists and the quote isn't `complete`. What does retry do?** It must not create a second SO. Your `netsuite_so_pushes` unique key on `(quote_id, accepted_tier_id)` should cover it — **confirm the retry path CHECKS that table before attempting the push**, rather than relying on the constraint to reject.

Same class as #145's `from_stage` poisoning: the recovery path has to be idempotent, not just the call.

**B. Below-floor guard against `accepted_tier_id`** — you have this right, good catch. One addition: **the override path is where below-floor becomes reachable at all.** R5 specifies an admin override. Does `markComplete` block unconditionally, or admit an override token? If the latter, that's a separate authorization surface and I want to see it before it ships.

---

## Confirmations wanted

- **`composition_hash`** — does it include **which OTC codes** are in the group? Two compositions differing only by a customs line must hash differently. (Plus the customer, per above.)
- **`netsuite_item_groups`** — is `composition_hash` unique globally or per base SKU? Same composition under two base SKUs must be two groups.

---

**Go on D1. Branch 8c-1 and 8c-2 once D1 is clean. Hold 8c-3** until the ordering and retry-idempotency answers are in.

🔴 D1 · NOT 1:1 — and a scope-changing gap on the resolution bridge

Ran D1 against production HubSpot + sandbox NetSuite. Two findings.

Finding 1 — Nexus product_types ≠ HubSpot hs_product_type. They're different taxonomies for different purposes:

- HubSpot hs_product_type — 15 enum values (Primary, Secondary, Cards Booklets, Design, Filling and Packout Services, Formulation, Freight, Labels, Third Party Logistics, One Time Charges, R&D / Testing, Raw ingredients, Soft Goods and Accessories, Finished Goods, Turnkey). Populated in NetSuite via custitem_dps_hubspot_product_type; 14 of 15 have live items (only Turnkey currently empty).
- Nexus product_types table — 17 rows across 2 orthogonal scopes: 9 ASY market-segment categories (Skincare / Supplement / Hair / etc.), 4 first-class LEAF types (Primary Packaging / Secondary Packaging / Tertiary Packaging / Soft goods), 4 hidden legacy types (Component / Assembly-sub / Service / Other). Loose overlap only on Primary/Secondary/Soft goods labels — not identity-of-values.

HubSpot has 11 first-class types Nexus doesn't have (Cards Booklets, Design, Filling & Packout, Formulation, Freight, Labels, 3PL, OTC, R&D, Raw ingredients, Turnkey). So there's no way to expand Nexus's taxonomy to "1:1 with HubSpot" — the taxonomies serve different jobs.

But this is fine: CA's premise is right that OTC discrimination doesn't need Nexus schema changes. The NetSuite item ALREADY knows what it is (custitem_dps_hubspot_product_type + class 60/61). At push time Nexus doesn't need to classify — it just references the NetSuite item and NetSuite carries the taxonomy for accounting.

Finding 2 — the actual blocker: leaf → NetSuite-item resolution has NO existing bridge. Sampled a NetSuite inventoryItem (Primary Packaging item id=1, custitem_dps_hubspot_product_type="Primary"). Its full custitem_* field surface:

custitem_311_asset_accntnum, custitem_311_cogs_accntnum, cust
custitem_bdc_lastupdatedbyimport, custitem_bdc_sync_exclude, custitem_bdc_updatedbyimport
custitem_dps_hubspot_product_type
custitem_order_delay_count, custitem_supply_allocation_count, custitem_supply_planning_count

Also queried customfield for any scriptid LIKE '%hubspot%' or label LIKE '%hubspot%': 0 matches. There is no custitem_dps_hubspot_product_id (or
equivalent) on NetSuite items.

Consequence: at SO push time, Nexus can't do SELECT id FROM i = <nexus_leaf.hubspot_product_id>. There is nothing to key on.

The bridge must be built OR fallback-matched. Options:

- (A) SKU-match — match nexus_leaf.sku (mirror of hubspot_proe_item.itemid. What Aisha does manually today. Fragile if thetwo SKU spaces diverge; historically they've been aligned (Aisha's workflow depends on it).
- (B) externalId convention for future items — Nexus writes N_id> when it CREATES items via API. Existing items (the entireback-catalog, thousands) weren't created by Nexus, so this doesn't help for the reuse case — only for future-created items. Not a working answer for MVP.
- (C) Bidirectional linkage field — add custitem_dps_hubspot_chema; Aisha (or an admin sync) backfills existing items. Realwork, but the only clean answer for durable identity. Post-v1.
- (D) Manual mapping table on Nexus side — Nexus persists net, netsuite_item_id, last_verified_at). Populated on first-pushper-leaf via SKU-match + PM confirmation. Cache-and-verify pattern.

My recommendation for 8c MVP: (A) SKU-match, with structured surface for mismatches. Every SO push resolves each leaf's NetSuite item via SELECT id,
itemid FROM item WHERE itemid = <nexus_leaf.sku>. If zero or D with a specific error tab: "Cannot resolve NetSuite item forSKU X — Y matches" and PM manually resolves (either fix the leaf SKU, or admin creates the NS item, or admin corrects the NS itemid). Same behavior
Aisha's manual process has today, just surfaced explicitly.

Escalation to CA: confirm option (A) is acceptable for MVP ORolution scheme. This is scope-critical for 8c-1'sfind-or-create (Item Group members need resolved NS item ids).

D1's Finding 2 is the important one and it's a genuine gap — worth catching before a branch existed.

# CA → CC — Q1–Q4 dispositions

## Q1 — Leaf → NetSuite item resolution: **(A) SKU-match, approved for MVP**

No linkage field exists (`0 matches` on any `%hubspot%` customfield), so there is nothing to key on but the SKU. Three supporting reasons:

- **It's what Aisha does today.** Her manual workflow already depends on the SKU spaces being aligned. We're not introducing fragility; we're surfacing an existing dependency.
- **The failure mode is already designed.** R9's `unmatched` flag exists for exactly this, and Melinda's §8 answer was unambiguous: missing items require human intervention because of GL accounts, costing, UoM, and tax config. **Block, never auto-create.**
- **Options B and C don't work for MVP.** B only helps items Nexus creates; C is a NetSuite schema change plus a backfill of thousands of records — post-v1, and worth proposing to Melinda separately as durable identity.

**Requirements on the implementation:**
- Zero matches **and** multiple matches both block with a specific, actionable message naming the SKU and the count
- Resolution happens **before** any NetSuite write — no half-created group with an unresolvable member
- **Track the hit rate.** CC's earlier sweep found 1 of 5, but four were R9 fixtures so the number is meaningless. If real coverage is low, `unmatched` becomes the common path and that changes 8c-4's UX prominence. Report it from the first sandbox smoke.

**Add option (D) as a follow-on, not MVP:** persist the resolved `leaf_id → netsuite_item_id` mapping with `last_verified_at`. Turns SKU-match into a cache-and-verify and gives us the linkage table (C) would have created, built up incrementally. Not now — but design the resolver so it can be added without rework.

## Q2 — Include per-member quantity in the hash. **You're right, I was wrong.**

My §4A phrasing "not quantities" meant tier and order quantities. **Per-member quantity within the group is structural** — "1 bottle + 1 pump" is a different product from "2 bottles + 1 pump," and the group members carry it. Include it.

No need to block on Aisha for the "2× X" case. Existing groups all show quantity 1, so if the multi-quantity case never arises the hash input is simply constant — harmless. If it does arise, we're already correct.

## Q3 — Description: send it to Aisha. **My read matches yours on staleness.**

Your two-line format looks right. Frame the reuse question to her as:

> When a group gets reused on a later order for the same customer, the description would still name the original deal it was created for. Is that fine, or would you want it updated to the current one?

**Argue for stale.** It names the deal that *caused* the group, which is honest and traceable. Refreshing makes groups mutable post-create, which contradicts the immutable-cache posture and adds an update path we'd otherwise never need. If she wants current-deal, propose append-style rather than overwrite — but push for stale first.

## Q4 — **Block unconditionally. Override deferred.**

Agreed, and your reasoning is right. An admin authorization surface needs its own audit action, permission model, approval semantics, and expiry rules. That's not a line in `markComplete`.

**One correction to your 8c-4 copy plan:** don't leave a "Contact admin" affordance implying a process that doesn't exist. Either state the block plainly — *"Blocked: tier is below the margin floor"* — or, if there's a real out-of-band path, name it concretely. A button or instruction pointing at nothing is the same class as the build-step leaks we're sweeping.

---

## On D1 Finding 1

Your conclusion is right and it strengthens the position: **Nexus doesn't need to classify at all.** The NetSuite item already carries `custitem_dps_hubspot_product_type` and its class. Nexus references the item; NetSuite owns the taxonomy for accounting. The two taxonomies serve different jobs and shouldn't be reconciled.

**8c-0 is formally cancelled.** No Nexus schema change, no mapper work, no backfill.

## Schema shape — approved

`composition_hash` as global PK is right, since the hash already includes customer and base SKU. NetSuite customer internal id as the customer identifier is the correct choice. The `(customer_netsuite_id, base_sku)` index for the `-G` collision scan is well-placed.

## Amendment A — approved as specified

CHECK-before-write at both layers, with the idempotency-key header as the belt for the create-succeeded-persist-failed window. The step-9 convergence path (retry sees the success row, jumps straight to the tx) is exactly right.

---

**Branch 8c-1 and 8c-2.** Hold 8c-3 until the Aisha answers on description are back — they affect the generator, not the adapter, so 8c-1 isn't blocked by them.

# CA → CC — Q1–Q4 dispositions

## Q1 — Leaf → NetSuite item resolution: **(A) SKU-match, approved for MVP**

No linkage field exists (`0 matches` on any `%hubspot%` customfield), so there is nothing to key on but the SKU. Three supporting reasons:

- **It's what Aisha does today.** Her manual workflow already depends on the SKU spaces being aligned. We're not introducing fragility; we're surfacing an existing dependency.
- **The failure mode is already designed.** R9's `unmatched` flag exists for exactly this, and Melinda's §8 answer was unambiguous: missing items require human intervention because of GL accounts, costing, UoM, and tax config. **Block, never auto-create.**
- **Options B and C don't work for MVP.** B only helps items Nexus creates; C is a NetSuite schema change plus a backfill of thousands of records — post-v1, and worth proposing to Melinda separately as durable identity.

**Requirements on the implementation:**
- Zero matches **and** multiple matches both block with a specific, actionable message naming the SKU and the count
- Resolution happens **before** any NetSuite write — no half-created group with an unresolvable member
- **Track the hit rate.** CC's earlier sweep found 1 of 5, but four were R9 fixtures so the number is meaningless. If real coverage is low, `unmatched` becomes the common path and that changes 8c-4's UX prominence. Report it from the first sandbox smoke.

**Add option (D) as a follow-on, not MVP:** persist the resolved `leaf_id → netsuite_item_id` mapping with `last_verified_at`. Turns SKU-match into a cache-and-verify and gives us the linkage table (C) would have created, built up incrementally. Not now — but design the resolver so it can be added without rework.

## Q2 — Include per-member quantity in the hash. **You're right, I was wrong.**

My §4A phrasing "not quantities" meant tier and order quantities. **Per-member quantity within the group is structural** — "1 bottle + 1 pump" is a different product from "2 bottles + 1 pump," and the group members carry it. Include it.

No need to block on Aisha for the "2× X" case. Existing groups all show quantity 1, so if the multi-quantity case never arises the hash input is simply constant — harmless. If it does arise, we're already correct.

## Q3 — Description: send it to Aisha. **My read matches yours on staleness.**

Your two-line format looks right. Frame the reuse question to her as:

> When a group gets reused on a later order for the same customer, the description would still name the original deal it was created for. Is that fine, or would you want it updated to the current one?

**Argue for stale.** It names the deal that *caused* the group, which is honest and traceable. Refreshing makes groups mutable post-create, which contradicts the immutable-cache posture and adds an update path we'd otherwise never need. If she wants current-deal, propose append-style rather than overwrite — but push for stale first.

## Q4 — **Block unconditionally. Override deferred.**

Agreed, and your reasoning is right. An admin authorization surface needs its own audit action, permission model, approval semantics, and expiry rules. That's not a line in `markComplete`.

**One correction to your 8c-4 copy plan:** don't leave a "Contact admin" affordance implying a process that doesn't exist. Either state the block plainly — *"Blocked: tier is below the margin floor"* — or, if there's a real out-of-band path, name it concretely. A button or instruction pointing at nothing is the same class as the build-step leaks we're sweeping.

---

## On D1 Finding 1

Your conclusion is right and it strengthens the position: **Nexus doesn't need to classify at all.** The NetSuite item already carries `custitem_dps_hubspot_product_type` and its class. Nexus references the item; NetSuite owns the taxonomy for accounting. The two taxonomies serve different jobs and shouldn't be reconciled.

**8c-0 is formally cancelled.** No Nexus schema change, no mapper work, no backfill.

## Schema shape — approved

`composition_hash` as global PK is right, since the hash already includes customer and base SKU. NetSuite customer internal id as the customer identifier is the correct choice. The `(customer_netsuite_id, base_sku)` index for the `-G` collision scan is well-placed.

## Amendment A — approved as specified

CHECK-before-write at both layers, with the idempotency-key header as the belt for the create-succeeded-persist-failed window. The step-9 convergence path (retry sees the success row, jumps straight to the tx) is exactly right.

p='SLICE-12-HANDOVER.md'
s=open(p).read()

# Update 8c section with what's built and what remains
s=s.replace(
"""### What 8c builds

1. **Item Group find-or-create** — see §4A for the full decision table
2. **Sales Order create**, with the group on it, mirroring SO2646's field surface
3. **~10 new HubSpot deal properties** + schema companion (see §4B)
4. **`markComplete`** — writes `accepted_tier_id`, `netsuite_so_id`, `netsuite_pushed_at`, `completed_by_user_id`, `completed_at`; flips `accepted` → `complete`
5. **Workflow cutover** — operational, see §4A""",
"""### Sub-step split — 4, and the first two are DONE

- ✅ **8c-1 (#149)** — adapter + Item Group find-or-create. No SO, no UI, not wired into any quote action.
- ✅ **8c-2 (#150)** — HubSpot deal-property expansion + schema companion.
- ⏭️ **8c-3** — adapter wiring into `quotes.ts` + SO push + guards. **Gated by SANDBOX SMOKE, not CB.**
- ⏭️ **8c-4** — UI transition, copy-leak sweep, prototype-class strip. **Gated by the CB walk.**

*(CC proposed 3 sub-steps; CA overruled to 4. Reason: 8c-3-as-proposed contained the first NetSuite write, the first `status='complete'` write, the Pattern 52 freeze, the amount patch, AND a UI replacement in one diff — a failed smoke wouldn't say which of five surfaces caused it. Each gate now does one job.)*

### 8c-1's two load-bearing findings

**1. The resolver MUST exclude `itemtype='Group'`.** `itemid="TCS-BAR-01"` exists twice in the catalogue — Group id 57232 (Era B, admin-authored) and InvtPart id 41350. Without the filter, **every group Nexus creates poisons the resolver for its own base SKU** — a failure that appears after the first successful push, not during smoke. NetSuite doesn't support nested groups, so groups were never valid members anyway.

**2. Leaf → NetSuite item resolution has NO linkage field.** A `customfield` sweep for `%hubspot%` returned **0 matches** — there is no `custitem_dps_hubspot_product_id`. **MVP resolves by SKU-match** (`itemid = nexus_leaf.sku`), which is what Aisha does manually today and what her workflow already depends on. Zero matches AND multiple matches both **block** with an actionable message; resolution happens **before** any NetSuite write. Real-leaf coverage in sandbox is 4/4, so `unmatched` is low-frequency, not the common path.
  - **Post-v1 (proposed to Melinda separately):** a first-class `custitem_dps_hubspot_product_id` on NetSuite items with a backfill — the only durable identity answer.
  - **Follow-on, designed-for-not-built:** persist `leaf_id → netsuite_item_id` with `last_verified_at`, turning SKU-match into cache-and-verify. The resolver is shaped to allow this without rework.

### 8c-3 — the remaining write path

`markComplete` ordering, locked (a two-external-system flow — CHECK-before-write at every layer, per #145's poisoning precedent):

1. Guards (below-floor against `accepted_tier_id`, revisable-state) — **before any external call**
2. **CHECK `netsuite_item_groups`** → cache hit reuses, miss falls to SuiteQL by `externalId`, miss again creates. NetSuite write #1
3. **CHECK `netsuite_so_pushes` on `(quote_id, accepted_tier_id)`** → success row skips create entirely
4. SO create — NetSuite write #2, **the irreversible act**. Idempotency-Key header as the belt for the create-succeeded-persist-failed window
5. Persist the `netsuite_so_pushes` row **before** touching quote state
6. DB tx: freeze Pattern 52's 27 columns; flip `accepted` → `complete`
7. **Post-tx:** conditional HubSpot amount patch. **Failure never blocks `complete`** — the SO exists; a stale amount is a reporting nit

**Convergence:** if step 6 fails after step 4 succeeds, retry re-reads step 3, finds the success row, and jumps straight to step 6. No second SO.

**Below-floor blocks UNCONDITIONALLY.** The R5 admin override is **deferred** — a real authorization surface needs its own audit action, permission model, approval semantics, and expiry rules. 8c-4's copy must NOT imply a "request unlock" process that doesn't exist; state the block plainly.

**`business_segment` label resolver** is an 8c-3 requirement, not a nice-to-have — NetSuite's SO field needs the label and we only store the enum id.

### Also in 8c
- **Workflow cutover** — operational, see §4A""")

open(p,'w').write(s)
print("ok")
PYEOF
cp /home/claude/SLICE-12-HANDOVER.md /mnt/user-data/outputs/SLICE-12-HANDOVER.md && wc -l /mnt/user-data/outputs/SLICE-12-HANDOVER.md

CC → CA — 8c-3 checkpoint: 6 pre-flight questions + sub-split proposal

Branch open (feat/slice-12-step-8c-3-so-create-markcomplete). Orientation done. Before code lands, six dispositions + a sub-split proposal — this scope has more surface area than 8c-1 or 8c-2, and asking now is cheaper than reshaping later.

D2 status — API-blocked

HubSpot Automation API v3 + v4 both returned 403 MISSING_SCOPES for Nexus's token (needs automation scope grant). Two paths:
- (a) Edward adds automation (read-only) scope to Nexus's HubSpot private app; I re-probe programmatically
- (b) Edward or Aisha eyeballs the HubSpot workflow list in the UI for a second Project-related workflow

D2 is still a pre-8c-3-merge gate, not a pre-code gate. Continue building the writer; land the D2 answer before merge.

Six pre-flight questions

Q1 — HubSpot company → NetSuite customer resolution (mirrors Q1-item pattern)

markComplete needs the NetSuite customer internal id for two things: the SO's entity field AND the composition_hash (per CA §4A). Options:

- (i) name-match on companyname in NS customer table (mirrors SKU-match; same fragility class — Epicuren-adjacent brand names could collide)
- (ii) match on a bespoke custentity_dps_hubspot_company_id if it exists (D1 pattern says probably doesn't — 0 matches on any %hubspot% custentity)
- (iii) manual mapping table on Nexus side, PM-populated at first-use
- (iv) probe NS to confirm

My recommendation: (i) with block-on-zero/multi surface — same discipline as SKU-match. Add a 8c-3 pre-code probe to check whether any custentity linkage exists (5-min SuiteQL grep against customfield for %hubspot_company%); if it exists, use (ii); otherwise (i).

Q2 — NetSuite SO orderStatus enum value ("Pending Fulfillment")

SO2646's REST GET returned status: "Pending Fulfillment". That's the read-side label; the write-side needs the internal enum value. NetSuite convention: orderStatus: "_pendingFulfillment" (underscored). Cheap sandbox probe to confirm the exact string; hardcode for MVP, add firm_settings.netsuite_so_order_status if firm needs configurability later.

Q3 — Subsidiary field on SO

SO2646 had a subsidiary field. Multi-subsidiary NetSuite accounts require it; single-subsidiary may auto-fill. Nexus sandbox = single-subsidiary presumably. Cheap probe — try creating a smoke SO without subsidiary, check if REST auto-fills or errors.

Q4 — Tax schedule at header vs per-line

Members of existing Item Group 57232 carry taxSchedule. Does the SO record itself require a tax schedule at header level, or does it inherit from lines/customer? Cheap probe on SO2646's REST response — check whether there's a header-level taxSchedule field populated.

Q5 — Memo mirror of custbody_dps_deal_id — do it?

chat_messages.text:
Good question, and my answer is **no — and we should be careful not to drift into it.**

The current architecture has Nexus as a **puller**: it reads HubSpot deals on demand, caches them, and writes back at specific moments (stage, amount, and soon line items). HubSpot doesn't know Nexus exists. That's a clean boundary and it's why today's discovery pass was possible at all — we could reason about the whole flow without an event graph in between.

**Where workflows would be tempting:**

- Auto-create a Nexus project when a deal reaches a certain stage
- Notify Nexus when a deal's properties change so the cache stays fresh
- Trigger something in Nexus when the customer replies

**Why I'd resist all three:**

Every workflow is **invisible logic owned by a different system**, and this slice just spent a day demonstrating the cost. The SO auto-create workflow nearly produced duplicate orders. The Project auto-create workflow runs in production and *nobody remaining knows how it works* — Melinda thought it was removed, Amy said "no idea, that was Diana and Vu." That's the steady state of workflow-driven integration: it works until the person who built it leaves.

Nexus pulling on demand means the logic lives in code, in version control, reviewable, testable, and attributable.

**The one case worth considering, and only after v1:** if deal properties change frequently and cache staleness becomes a real problem, a webhook is better than polling — but that's a **notification**, not a workflow. "Tell Nexus this deal changed" is different in kind from "when this happens, do that." The first keeps logic in Nexus; the second moves it into HubSpot.

**And there's a live decision this bears on.** The SO auto-create workflow gets disabled at 8c cutover. That's the right direction — moving logic *out* of HubSpot and into Nexus, where it's inspectable. Adding new workflows to feed Nexus would be moving in the opposite direction at the same moment.

**Worth doing regardless of the answer:** inventory the workflows currently touching deals. We know of two (SO creation, Project creation) and neither was documented. There may be others firing on stages Nexus now writes to — same class of surprise as the SO one, and cheaper to find now than at cutover. That's the same UI look D2 needs, so it's one task.

Then Q1 is settled: **no linkage exists in either direction.** Four avenues swept — NetSuite customfields, the customer record's `custentity_*` surface, the Ops Hub embed, and now the HubSpot company record. That's thorough enough to stop looking.

**Option (B), and it's the right answer for a reason beyond fallback:** it's the same shape as the leaf→item resolver, so 8c ends up with one consistent pattern for both unresolved-reference cases rather than two different ones.

**But it needs to be its own sub-step, not folded into 8c-3.** Three reasons:

1. **It inserts a human step into the irreversible action.** The PM hits "Send order to NetSuite" and, first time for a customer, has to pick the NetSuite account before anything proceeds. That's a design question — where the picker lives, what it shows, whether it blocks the modal or the tab — and it's CD's call, not CC's.
2. **It changes R9's `unmatched` flag from a rare blocker to a first-time-per-customer step.** With 4,594 customers and no map, *every* customer is unmatched on first push. That's not an edge case; it's the default path until the map fills.
3. **It's a new table plus a resolution surface plus PM training.** Materially larger than the 8c-3 scope we agreed.

**Proposed shape: 8c-3-pre.** Customer mapping table + resolver + the confirmation surface, CD-briefed, CB-walked. Then 8c-3 proper consumes a resolved id and stays the write path it was scoped as.

**One thing worth confirming before CD gets a brief:** how many *distinct customers* do the 57 quotes actually touch? If Nexus's real customer set is a few dozen rather than thousands, a one-time admin backfill — Aisha pairs them once — may beat a per-PM first-use flow entirely. That would make the resolver a lookup with no UI at all.

Worth asking CC to count it. Cheap, and it could remove the CD round.

# CA → CC — Q1 dispositioned: **(B'), fold into 8c-3.**

**Nine customers.** That number closes the question. A fuzzy-matching resolver against 4,594 NetSuite records to serve nine mappings would have been the wrong build by an order of magnitude.

**Sub-slice: (ii), fold in.** Your reasoning is right and it's the same principle as the earlier overrule — a resolver with no consumer has no verifiable behaviour, so shipping it separately buys a merge cycle and no gate. Your commit ordering (migration+resolver+admin → Aisha seeds → wire → smoke) is correct.

## Three requirements on the map

**1. Store the display name and treat it as advisory only.** `netsuite_customer_display_name` in your schema is right — but it's a human-legibility field, never a match key. Same rule as the Item Group description: written once, never used for resolution.

**2. No delete is correct. Add an audit row.** These mappings are historically anchored — an SO pushed against customer 131860 stays pushed. If a mapping is ever *edited*, that's a significant act and needs an audit trail, not just a `verified_at` bump. New audit action, `netsuite_customer_map_changed`, with before/after.

**3. Block-on-miss must name the customer.** Not "this customer isn't mapped" — *"Epicuren (HubSpot company 17586902316) has no NetSuite customer mapping. An admin can add one at /admin/netsuite-customer-map."* The PM should be able to forward that message and have someone act on it without a follow-up question.

## `netsuite_subsidiary` — flag it, don't chase it

Good catch. HubSpot has a deal property labelled "NetSuite Subsidiary" with a real description, and it's **empty**. Someone intended a NetSuite-aware integration that never landed values.

Doesn't help us — we hardcode subsidiary 2 — but **worth telling Edward** so it can go to whoever owns HubSpot admin. An empty NetSuite-aware property is either a broken workflow or an abandoned plan, and both are worth knowing before cutover. Not our scope.

## Everything else acknowledged

Q2–Q6 as dispositioned. `custcol_dps_sku` and `custcol_dps_unit_cost` both populated. `firm_settings.netsuite_default_tax_code_id` ships in 8c-3.

**One outstanding to Edward, not you:** whether any DPS customer is taxable. Hardcoded `-8` assumes none are — plausible for B2B contract manufacturing, inferred from one sandbox record. The firm_settings column is the escape hatch, but the answer should come from Melinda before a real SO goes out.

---

**Build 8c-3.** D2 still lands before merge.

**Sandbox smoke must cover the three failure paths explicitly:**
- Below-floor refusal **before** any NetSuite call — zero writes, no orphan group
- NetSuite 5xx on SO create — quote stays `accepted`, no orphaned Item Group, retry works, **no second SO**
- Tx failure after SO success — retry converges via the `netsuite_so_pushes` check and does **not** create a duplicate

That third one is the #145 poisoning case in a new costume. It's the one I'll look hardest at.

chat_messages.text:
That's useful and it tightens the design — the HubSpot side is guaranteed, but it doesn't close the gap we're solving.

**What your point guarantees:** every deal has an associated company. So Nexus always resolves deal → HubSpot company. That hop was never at risk, and it's now guaranteed by process rather than assumed.

**What's still unresolved:** HubSpot company → **NetSuite** customer. A company existing in HubSpot doesn't mean a corresponding customer record exists in NetSuite, and nothing on either side records the pairing. That's the map's whole job.

**Where your point does change something concrete:** the block-on-miss case is now narrower and better defined. It can only mean one thing — *this company exists in HubSpot but has no NetSuite mapping yet*. Never "no company at all." So the error copy can be specific, and the admin surface's "needs mapping" list is just: companies in `hubspot_deals_cache` with no map row.

**And it makes the nine-row seed durable.** New customers enter through a controlled process — contact, then company, then deal — so mapping additions arrive at a predictable moment rather than randomly. Worth noting for whoever maintains the map: a new company in HubSpot is the signal that a mapping may be needed.

**One question that follows:** when a new customer is created in HubSpot, does Ops Hub push a NetSuite customer automatically, or does someone create it there separately? If Ops Hub creates it, the NetSuite record exists by the time a quote is written and the mapping is purely a lookup someone records. If it's manual, there's a window where the HubSpot company exists and the NetSuite customer doesn't — and the block-on-miss would be correct but frequent for new customers.

Not blocking 8c-3. But it determines whether the map is maintained routinely or almost never touched after the initial nine.

chat_messages.text:
Amy's answer means **don't hardcode `-8`.** Two things in it rule that out:

**Some items are genuinely taxable** — file processing, tooling. Those are OTC codes, which is exactly what Nexus will be emitting. Hardcoding Not Taxable would write wrong tax onto the lines most likely to be taxable.

**And tax is jurisdictional** — out of state gets the OC rate, in state gets county rates. That's derived from ship-to, not a per-line constant. NetSuite's tax engine already handles this; a hardcoded code overrides it with a guess.

**Recommendation: omit `taxCode` from the payload entirely and let NetSuite apply its own default per item and customer.** That's the outcome I flagged as likely, and Amy's "leave it to NetSuite to decide" plus "we can do it manually" confirms both the primary and the fallback.

**Two things worth verifying before CC ships it:**

1. **Does NetSuite accept an SO line with no `taxCode`?** REST APIs sometimes require it even when the UI derives it. Cheap sandbox probe — create a line without it and see whether NetSuite fills it or errors.
2. **What does NetSuite actually apply?** On the sandbox smoke, check what tax code lands on each line unset. If it comes back `-8` on everything, we've lost nothing. If it applies a real rate on the tooling OTC, that's the engine working correctly and validates the decision.

**Keep `firm_settings.netsuite_default_tax_code_id`** — but as an **override that's null by default**, not a value we always send. If NetSuite's derivation ever misbehaves ("a weird quirk where it adds tax sometimes," per Amy), an admin can pin a code without a code change.

That's a design change to CC's Q4 disposition — worth sending now, since it's mid-build.

No — two different things, and only one is blocked.

**Creating Item Groups via REST works.** CC did it in 8c-1: created group NS id 74054, cache-hit on reuse, `-G2` on collision, full round-trip. That's proven and merged.

**Is it definitive?** Definitive for **REST**, yes — that's a thorough elimination. Not definitive overall, for three reasons:

1. **SOAP is untested** and already enabled on the account. It's an older, more permissive API surface, and this is exactly the kind of gap where it differs.
2. **A RESTlet** — a small SuiteScript endpoint — would run server-side inside NetSuite using the same internal APIs the UI uses. Aisha's UI workflow proves the operation is legal; a RESTlet is the standard way to reach it when REST won't. SuiteScript is enabled on your account.
3. **We haven't checked whether NetSuite documents this limitation**, which would tell us if there's a supported parameter we're missing rather than a hard wall.

**My read:** the operation is almost certainly achievable. The question is cost. SOAP might be one call. A RESTlet is a small script deployed into NetSuite — maybe half a day, but it's NetSuite-side code someone has to own.

**So the sequence is:** SOAP probe first, ten minutes. If SOAP works, we ship the full feature. If it doesn't, then it's a real decision — RESTlet now versus flat lines now and RESTlet later — and that's a scheduling call rather than a technical one.

Worth doing the probe before accepting the limitation.

new = """### 🔴 ITEM GROUPS ON A SALES ORDER ARE NOT AUTOMATABLE — exhaustively proven

**Creating an Item Group via API works** (8c-1, proven end to end). **Referencing one from an SO create does not.**

| Surface | Result |
|---|---|
| REST — 7 payload shapes (bare group, +rate, +amount, +grossAmount, +price level, amount:0, group+members inline) | **All rejected** at `item.items[0]`: *"Please enter a value for Amount"* |
| SOAP — `add` SalesOrder with group line | **Same error**, after auth was confirmed working (`getServerTime` → 200) |
| SOAP — group + member rates in one call | **Same error** |

Tested against group **64026** — the group on live SO2454 — and customer **131860**. Auth verified on both surfaces. **The limitation is NetSuite's server-side SO validator, not a config gap, and it is not REST-specific.**

Aisha's manual flow works because NetSuite's UI uses SuiteScript's `N/record` engine with interactive-save semantics — a different code path no external API reaches.

**SOAP required two enablements** that weren't obvious: the account-level feature (already on) **and** the `SOAP Web Services` permission on the role (separate from `REST Web Services`; we'd only granted the latter). There is no SOAP toggle on the integration record in this NetSuite version.

**DECISION: flat lines.** Nexus emits one SO line per leaf with correct prices. **What this delivers:** Aisha stops retyping prices between systems — the load-bearing time-drain. **What it does NOT deliver:** the group wrap, which is **customer-visible, not cosmetic** — the Item Group is why an invoice shows one turnkey line instead of freight/customs/setup as separate lines (INV2978 is the canonical example). Aisha's wrap step remains mandatory for anything invoiced. Finance signed off; Assemblies revisited at v1.5/2.0.

**Rejected: a SuiteScript RESTlet.** ~60 LOC of NetSuite-side script, 1–1.5 days plus a NetSuite-side ownership handoff, on an account with a documented history of orphaned automation — and obsoleted by the Assembly migration.

**NOT YET TESTED — the next probe:** a **three-step attachment** — POST the SO with flat lines, then **PATCH** to add or replace with a group line, then PATCH member rates. Every attempt so far put the group on at **create** time; PATCH on a **saved** record is a different validator path, and it mirrors what Aisha actually does. If it works, the grouped SO comes back with no RESTlet and no migration.

### 🔵 ASSEMBLIES WORK WHERE ITEM GROUPS DON'T — top v1.5/2.0 candidate

REST accepts an **Assembly** line on an SO cleanly (throwaway POST created + deleted). So NetSuite's API isn't hostile to bundled items — it's hostile to **Item Groups specifically**. Assemblies are first-class records with a build model and their own price; Item Groups are a presentation wrapper the API won't take responsibility for expanding.

**Four aligning points:**
1. NetSuite's API models Assemblies as first-class — proven
2. NetSuite's API refuses Item Groups on SOs at **both** REST and SOAP — proven
3. **Nexus's ASY/LEAF model is assembly-shaped**, not group-shaped — parent, children, `qty_per_parent`, roll-up pricing
4. The v2 roadmap already targets NetSuite-direct with native BOMs

**And DPS already has 9 Assembly items in the catalog** — expansion, not greenfield. Finance is aware and has parked it for v1.5/2.0.

### ✅ D2 ANSWERED — Project creation survives the cutover

Vu Nguyen (NetSuite analyst, built it with Diana): **Project creation is a NetSuite-side script triggered by the `custbody_dps_auto_generate_project` checkbox on the SO** — not by HubSpot, not by the workflow we disable at cutover. *"A project can be created from any sales order source as long as the box is checked."* Also: *"if the project field is not empty, the script will not create a project"* — the find-or-create behaviour behind the ~60% attach rate and Amy's manual reassignment.

**⚠️ Vu UNCHECKED the field's default on 2026-07-28** while answering. It now defaults to **false** and must be set explicitly. **CA's earlier direction — "leave it at its default" — would now mean Nexus never creates Projects, silently.** Outstanding question to Vu: should Nexus set it always, conditionally on business segment, or never? One line either way; ship what they want.

"""
s = s.replace(anchor, new + anchor, 1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("ok")

**What makes me think it's genuine:** CC sent `amount` explicitly. And `rate`. And `grossAmount`. And a price level. And `amount: 0`. Every one returned the same error. If the validator wanted an amount on the group line, one of those should have satisfied it.

**Subject: Question about item prices in NetSuite**

Hi Melinda — one question that came out of the Nexus sales order work. Some background so it makes sense.

When Nexus creates a sales order automatically, we'd like it to add the Item Group the same way Aisha does by hand — so the customer sees one turnkey line on the invoice instead of the components listed separately.

We couldn't get that working at first, and we've now worked out why. When you add an Item Group to a sales order through the NetSuite interface, NetSuite lets you type the prices onto the component lines afterwards — which is exactly what Aisha does. When something adds it *automatically*, NetSuite instead looks up a price on each component's item record. Our items don't have prices on them, so it stops and won't create the order.

To be clear, we're not proposing that Nexus set or change any prices. This would be item setup on your side, like GL accounts or units of measure — set once when an item is created, not touched per order.

Happy to walk through what we found if useful.

---

That's the finding, and it validates your instinct completely. We were one probe from closing something that works.

**The sequence works: POST bare group → GET expanded lines → PATCH each member with the real rate.** Single-line PATCH updates in place — no duplication, no atomicity error. That's the mechanism, and it's REST-only.

**And `$0.00` satisfies the validator.** Which resolves your objection precisely: freight and customs carry a structural zero meaning "no standing price," and every SO carries the actual amount. Nothing false is asserted anywhere.

**Two things in 7d are worth pausing on before we commit.**

**1. The duplication failure mode is dangerous.** Sublist PATCH returns **204 — success** — while silently appending a second full group expansion. Twelve transaction lines, rollup doubled, no error. If 8c's implementation ever reaches for the sublist PATCH instead of single-line, it produces a wrong Sales Order that reports as successful. That needs to be structurally impossible in the code, not just avoided by convention.

**2. Per-SO call count goes from 1 to 8–12**, each a potential failure point mid-sequence. The partial-failure state is new: SO created, group expanded, some members priced, some at zero. That's a **valid-looking order with wrong amounts** — worse than a clean failure, because nothing flags it.

Both are solvable. Neither is trivial.

That's the question I'd put to Melinda now — and it's a much better question than the one I drafted earlier. Not "why don't items have prices" but: *"we need a zero price on these items as a structural placeholder; is that acceptable and who sets it?"*

**And the scheduling question is yours:** this is real additional work on the irreversible step, at the end of a slice, with a new partial-failure mode. Flat lines ship now and this becomes 8c-5 or v1.1. Or we hold 8c-4 and build it.

My lean is **ship flat lines, build grouped as the immediate next step** — but that's a call about your August date, not a technical one.

# CA → CC — Probe 8: scope the price prerequisite

Probe 7 reopened the grouped-SO path and that's the most valuable finding of the day. Before anyone touches the catalogue, we need to know exactly what "populate `price`" means and how many records it touches.

**Context:** Edward can have Vu (NetSuite analyst) run a bulk update. He needs one precise instruction, not three revisions — and this is a **production master-data change**, so it gets scoped properly first.

## 8a — The exact `price` payload shape

Your throwaway items got a `price` set, but the report doesn't say how. NetSuite's pricing sub-collection usually has structure — price level, currency, quantity break.

Report the **complete shape** of a populated `price` sub-collection on a real item. Use `inventoryitem/2769` (which has one). Specifically:
- Every field on each price row
- How many rows exist and what distinguishes them
- Which price level(s) — Base Price, Custom, others?
- Currency handling
- **The minimal payload that satisfied the validator on your throwaway** — verbatim

Vu writes his query from this. If a bare `0.00` isn't sufficient and it needs a price-level row, that changes the instruction.

## 8b — How many items are unpriced?

Across the catalogue:
- Total items, and how many have `price` populated vs empty
- Broken down by `itemtype` — InvtPart, NonInvtPart, Assembly, Group, Service, OtherCharge
- Broken down by `class` where it clarifies — particularly the OTC clusters (60 Freight, 61 One Time Charges)

## 8c — How many does Nexus actually touch?

**This is the number that scopes the ask.**

Take the leaf SKUs referenced by real quotes across the nine mapped customers. Resolve them to NetSuite items. Report:
- How many distinct items
- How many are unpriced
- Which OTC codes appear in real quotes

If Nexus touches 40 items and 35 need a price, that's a targeted update. If it needs the whole catalogue, that's a different conversation.

## 8d — What breaks if a null becomes zero?

**Read-only, and this is the one that protects us.** Setting `$0.00` where `price` is currently empty is a production master-data change. A null and a zero are not the same value to anything reading it.

Report anything you can see that references item price — saved searches, workflows, other integrations, reports. **You won't see everything from the API**, so flag the limits of what you checked. Vu confirms the rest from inside NetSuite.

---

## Also — two hazards from Probe 7 to bank now

**1. Sublist PATCH returns 204 while silently duplicating.** Twelve transaction lines, rollup doubled, **no error**. If any future implementation reaches for sublist PATCH instead of single-line PATCH, it produces a wrong Sales Order that reports as successful. When grouped-SO gets built, that must be **structurally impossible** — not avoided by convention. Bank it as a watch item now, while the evidence is fresh.

**2. Partial-failure mid-sequence is a new state.** POST + GET + N PATCHes means the SO can exist with the group expanded, some members priced, some at zero. That's a **valid-looking order with wrong amounts** — worse than a clean failure, because nothing flags it. The recovery design needs to handle it explicitly.

---

**Read-only. No writes to any real catalogue item. Report numbers and shapes, not conclusions.**

**8c first** — it's the number that determines whether this is a small targeted update or a catalogue-wide policy question.

We've found the mechanism: NetSuite's API needs a price on each component's item record before it will expand a group onto an order. Once that's there, the order gets created and we then set the real rates on each line — same end result as adding the group in the UI.

The catch is that a lot of our items have no price on the record. Freight and customs especially, and that's correct — those aren't known until the shipment happens.

We'd want it in the sandbox first so we can verify the whole flow works against real items, then production once it's proven.

Same opening, then:

Hi Vu — following up on the Nexus sales order work. Two asks and some things I'd want your read on first.

## What we found

We've worked out how to have Nexus create a Sales Order with the Item Group already on it, so the customer sees one turnkey line instead of the components listed separately — the step Aisha does by hand today.

NetSuite's API needs a price on each component's item record before it will expand a group onto an order. Most of our items don't have one. We tested it: **a price of `$0.00` is enough** — it doesn't need to be a real number. The actual amounts still come from the order, exactly as they do now. We verified this in the sandbox end to end.

## The two asks

**1. Set base price to `$0.00` on 937 items** — the ones Nexus references that are currently unpriced. I have the full list of internal IDs ready to send.

Sandbox first, so we can prove the whole flow against real items before anything touches production.

The shape is one row per item: price level **Base Price (1)**, currency page **1**, price **0**.

**2. Set `$0.00` as the default when a new item is created.** Otherwise this comes back — new products flow in from HubSpot without a price, and we'd be asking you to run the same update again in a few months. Whether that's best done in the HubSpot sync config or NetSuite-side, you'd know better than I would.

## Before you run anything — three things I'd want your view on

**1. Does anything read base price where an empty value and a zero behave differently?** Saved searches filtering on price being null, user event scripts branching on a zero rate, client scripts on the item form, workflow conditions. **2. This changes what Aisha sees when she enters an order.** Right now a blank price gives her an empty field to fill in. Afterwards, lines would pre-fill with `$0.00` — which *looks* filled. If she tabs past one, an order could ship at zero. Worth thinking about whether that needs a guard, or whether it's fine because she reviews every line anyway.

**3. Is there a reason items don't carry a base price today** — a deliberate setup decision, or just never needed? 93% of the catalogue is unpriced, so I assume it's the former and I'd rather ask than find out afterwards.

## Context

If the answer to any of this is "this is more trouble than it's worth," that's fine. Nexus can create the order with the components as separate lines and someone adds the group afterwards — which is what happens today. Not ideal, but not blocking us.

Happy to walk through what we tested, or show you the sandbox order we created.

---

input.file_text:
# Slice 13 — NetSuite Readiness & Cutover

**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-07-28
**Author:** CA

---

## Why this exists

Slice 12 delivers the **mechanism**: a PM accepts a quote, presses Send, and a NetSuite Sales Order is created with correct line items, prices, terms, customer, and deal reference. Proven end to end (SO 360441).

It does **not** deliver a process a PM can run unaided.

Five items stand between the two, and they accumulated as findings in the handover rather than as scope. Each is individually small and defensible. Together they mean a PM cannot reliably go from accepted quote to correct Sales Order without someone intervening.

**The test for "done" is one sentence:** *a PM accepts a quote, presses Send, and a correct Sales Order exists in NetSuite with no one else touching anything.*

Against that test, Slice 12 does not close.

---

## Recommendation: a dedicated slice, not an expansion of 12

Three reasons:

1. **Different work.** Slice 12 is application code. This is operational cutover, external-system configuration, and data remediation. Different verification, different owners, different failure modes.
2. **Different people.** Three of five items depend on Vu, Melinda, Aisha, or Amy. Slice 12's cadence (CC builds, CA reviews, CB walks) doesn't fit work that waits on other teams.
3. **Slice 12 has a clean close.** Steps 9 and 10 are scoped, small, and code-only. Extending 12 to absorb operational work muddies a slice that is otherwise ready to finish.

**Slice 12 closes as scoped. Slice 13 makes it usable.**

---

## R1 — Workflow cutover · BLOCKER · owner: Edward + Vu

The HubSpot workflow **"NETSUITE: Auto create NetSuite sales order from won deal"** is ON and enrolls on `Won - In production (Sales)` — the same stage `markAccepted` sets.

**Until it is disabled, every accepted quote gets TWO Sales Orders.**

- Disable early → orders stop reaching NetSuite with nothing replacing them
- Disable late → duplicates on every accepted quote

**Required:** a same-operation switch — the workflow is disabled in the same window Nexus goes live, with a verified path back if the Nexus push fails.

**Sub-tasks:**
- Written cutover runbook: sequence, who does what, rollback trigger, rollback steps
- Confirm no other deal workflow fires on `Won - In production` (partially checked; not exhaustive)
- Verify Project auto-creation is unaffected — **confirmed safe** (Vu: NetSuite-side script on the `custbody_dps_auto_generate_project` checkbox, source-agnostic)
- A defined observation window post-cutover with someone watching for duplicates

**Cannot be a to-do. It is a planned operation with a named owner and a date.**

---

## R2 — Item Groups · IN FLIGHT · owner: CC + Vu

Currently **manual**. Nexus emits flat lines with correct prices; Aisha wraps them in an Item Group by hand for anything customer-facing.

**This is customer-visible, not cosmetic** — the group is why an invoice shows one turnkey line instead of freight, customs, and setup as separate lines.

**Reopened by Probe 7.** The sequence `POST bare group → GET expanded lines → PATCH each member rate` works. Prerequisite: every group member needs an item-level `price`, and `$0.00` satisfies the validator.

**Vu's finding relocated the fix:** NetSuite items are unpriced because the **HubSpot products** are unpriced. The sync carries what exists upstream.

**Open path:**
1. CC Stages 1–2 (assess + rollback capture) — in flight
2. **Five-row test** — set `hs_price = 0` on five products, verify propagation to NetSuite, create a grouped SO against a real item
3. **The load-bearing unknown:** does the sync update *existing* items, or only on create? If create-only, HubSpot-side backfill never reaches the 937 existing items and Vu's NetSuite-side update is needed as well
4. Full backfill (~hundreds of products)
5. `mapLeafToHubspotCreate` writes `hs_price: 0` — stops the trickle at source
6. Products created directly in HubSpot outside Nexus — needs a HubSpot-side default, or confirmation it doesn't happen
7. Rebuild the grouped-SO payload in `sales-orders.ts`

**Two hazards already identified, must be designed against:**
- **Sublist PATCH returns 204 while silently duplicating** the group expansion. Doubled rollup, no error. Must be structurally impossible in the implementation, not avoided by convention. Only `PATCH /salesOrder/{id}/item/{lineIdx}` is safe.
- **Partial failure mid-sequence** leaves a valid-looking SO with some members at $0. Needs either a transactional wrapper with SO-delete rollback, or a read-back verification pass before marking the push succeeded.

**If this doesn't resolve:** the manual wrap is a permanent stated limitation someone signs off on knowingly — not a footnote.

---

## R3 — Unresolved leaves · owner: TBD

**59 of 1020 leaves (6%) do not resolve to a NetSuite item.** A quote containing one blocks at send with a clear, actionable message — but someone has to create the item.

CC's breakdown:
- **~35 real customer items** absent from NetSuite by exact SKU match
- **~10 sample-seed placeholders** (`LIB-`, `LEAF-GLW-`, `Nexus-Smoke-Test-1`, `TEST-LFC2-*`) — won't reach production
- **Data-entry defects** — leading-tab SKUs on `Cirqadian-*`, likely fixable in Nexus
- **`TCS-BAR-01`** — exists, but flagged ambiguous by the Group/InvtPart itemid collision. Already handled by the 8c-1 resolver filter; verify it clears.

**Required:**
- Triage all 59 into: create in NetSuite / fix in Nexus / ignore (sample data)
- Create the real ones — Melinda's rule applies: items carry GL accounts, costing, UoM, tax config, so **a human creates them, never Nexus**
- Fix the Nexus-side data defects
- **Decide the steady-state policy:** new leaves will keep arriving unmatched. Is blocking-at-send acceptable as the permanent behaviour, or does a PM need a pre-send readiness check?

---

## R4 — Customer map maintenance · owner: CC

Nine rows seeded, covering every customer with an active project. **Verified: all nine NetSuite `companyName` values match their HubSpot names exactly.**

**But there is no maintenance surface.** A new customer blocks at send until someone writes a row directly to the database.

**Required:**
- Admin UI: list, add, edit. **No delete** — mappings are historically anchored to pushed Sales Orders
- Audit on edit (`netsuite_customer_map_changed`, before/after) — a mapping change is significant
- A "needs mapping" view: companies in `hubspot_deals_cache` with no map row
- Block-on-miss copy names the customer and the HubSpot company id so it can be forwarded and acted on

**Note:** Ops Hub creates the NetSuite customer when the HubSpot company is created, so the pairing always *exists* — recording it is a lookup, not a creation task. Genuinely low-effort admin work.

---

## R5 — Taxability confirmation · owner: Edward + Melinda

**Outstanding since 2026-07-28 morning.**

Nexus omits `taxCode` and lets NetSuite derive it. The sandbox smoke returned `-8` (Not Taxable) on a real customer, which is the evidence.

**But Amy flagged that some items ARE taxable** — file processing, tooling — and tax is jurisdictional (out-of-state OC rate, in-state county rates). Those are OTC codes, which is exactly what Nexus emits.

**Required:** Melinda confirms NetSuite's derivation is correct for automated orders, or names the cases where it isn't. `firm_settings.netsuite_default_tax_code_id` exists as a nullable override.

**Gates the first production Sales Order.**

---

## Also in scope

| Item | Note |
|---|---|
| **Production credentials** | NetSuite integration record, role, and tokens exist in **sandbox only**. Production setup is a repeat of §4A steps 2–6, plus Vercel env at production scope. |
| **Production smoke** | Controlled test orders, per-order Edward confirmation, void-or-close path established **before** any create. |
| **Pattern 52 freeze verification** | Implemented but never smoke-verified — Clerk blocked the mutation attempt, not the freeze. Needs an in-request-scope harness. |
| **Customer PDF defects** | Tier 2 unit prices render as em dash; inconsistent money formatting; header overflow. Slice 11 workstream, but on the v1 path. |
| **`business_segment` label** | Enum id only; resolver deferred. Needed if the SO's segment field is ever populated. |
| **MS OAuth** | Pending IT. Blocks team sign-in and CB self-authentication. |

---

## Sequencing

**R5 and R1 gate the first production order.** R2 is in flight and may resolve favourably. R3 and R4 are parallel work with no external dependency once triaged.

**Suggested order:**
1. R5 (one answer) · R2 five-row test (in flight)
2. R3 triage · R4 admin surface — parallel, no blockers
3. R2 full backfill + grouped-SO rebuild, if the test confirms
4. R1 cutover runbook, then execute
5. Production credentials + controlled production smoke

---

## The honest framing

Slice 12 was reviewed against its brief and every step passed. The brief described the mechanism, and the mechanism works.

The gap opened when the architecture changed mid-slice and "what done requires" was not re-derived. Items accumulated as findings in the handover rather than as scope with owners.

**Slice 13 exists so that gap is closed deliberately rather than discovered at launch.**
