## Introduction

### This is an early prediction covering the known information for each class. For all the latest information once the Season launches, make sure to check our [Tier List](https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/tier-list) for the best builds and the [Leveling Guides](https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/leveling-builds) to help blast through Season 14.

## Video

## Warlock

#### [Warlock Class Lead - Ace](https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/profile/ace)

For Warlock in Season 14, the top build has seen some big changes since ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/apocalypse.png)Apocalypse is no longer the go to. This might worry some people at first, especially since Warlock didn’t get any huge buffs this season. That said, a lot of major ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/profane-sentinel.png)Profane Sentinel bugs getting fixed, the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/command-fallen.png)Mega Lunatic Command Fallen build is still really strong, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/dread-claws.png)Dread Claws is performing well too. So overall, Warlock is still in a solid spot. We probably won’t miss ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/apocalypse.png)Apocalypse as much as it seems. If anything, the fix to the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/nether-step.png)Nether Step bug on controller might be one of the bigger buffs for the class this season.

My top top 3 builds for the season are ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/dread-claws.png)Dread Claws, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/command-fallen.png)Mega Lunatic Command Fallen and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/profane-sentinel.png)Profane Sentinel.




**For more** ***Warlock*** **content, check out** ***Ace*** **on** [**YouTube**](https://www.youtube.com/@Goblin-Inc) **and** [**Twitch.**](https://twitch.tv/aceofspadeshots)

## Barbarian

#### [Barbarian Class Lead - Cliptis](https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/profile/cliptis)

The Barbarian is looking to be one of the most well rounded classes heading into Season 14. It will compete for the highest levels of the Tower, have some of the tankiest builds and still be one of the fastest classes for farming out there. All your favorite builds will still be there in Season 14 with some new exciting ones jumping up the ranks a little.   Let's start with the strongest build for pushing the Pits and the Towers, the[Ancient Bro'barian build](https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/builds/barbarian-ancients-leap-endgame). It will be very similar to season 13 but due to bug fixes, we can now run ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/ramaladnis-magnum-opus.png)Ramaladni's Magnum Opus and the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/melted-heart-of-selig.png)Melted Heart of Selig increasing it's damage siginificantly from the PTR testing. Your bro'barian build does have an insanely fast speed variant but compared to the ease of play and gearing from Whirlwind, this takes the top slot for the ultimate farmer. It will be strong and will push high into the Pits but with the nerf to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/signet-of-pelghain.png)Signet of Pelghain the Freeze variant is no longer a thing for the Barbarians reducing some of that top end damage. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/leap.png)Leap will be making a return in season 14, along with a weapon swap, auto-cast whirlwind variant that spams ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/steel-grasp.png)Steel Grasp. There are so many more options with the changes that were made to Uniques that I'm really excited to bring to everyone this season.  


**For more Barbarian content, check out** ***Cliptis*** **on** [**YouTube**](https://www.youtube.com/@cliptis86) **and** [**Twitch**](https://www.twitch.tv/cliptis)**.**

## Druid

#### [Druid Class Lead - Zaior](https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/profile/zaior/builds)

Hey everyone, Zaior from Mobalytics here, and first of all, I want to say that the Druid is in a great spot for Season 14r. Last season, Companions was the best build for pushing both the Tower and the Pit. Well, this season it has been heavily nerfed, leaving it practically out of the meta. Even so, it will probably still be able to clear Torment 12 without any issues. Now, let's move on to what I think will be the best Druid builds. First, we have the Storm and Werewolf builds, which will really shine this season thanks to the buffs received by the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/charms/storm-shepherds-call.png)Berú of the Storm Shepherd set. Builds like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/shred.png)Shred and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/tornado.png)Tornado will be at the top. And not just for pushing—they're also incredibly strong for farming content, which is where we spend most of our time improving our characters. Right behind them, we'll have some very strong contenders that are just a bit lower in terms of DPS. Those builds are ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/landslide.png)Landslide and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/boulder.png)Boulder. Last season, the Resolve mechanic was extremely powerful. This season, it has been nerfed to better balance Werebear and Werewolf builds, leaving them much closer in overall damage. On top of that, our Earth builds gain access to the new ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/the-basilisk.png)The Basilisk, which guarantees Critical Strikes whenever we Petrify enemies. This synergizes perfectly with the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/charms/song-of-the-old-mountain.png)Berú of the Old Mountain set, as well as the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/locrans-talisman.png)Locran's Talisman, which increases the damage of our Critical Strikes. Without a doubt, the Bear will also be very strong this season, but still one step below ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/shred.png)Shred and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/tornado.png)Tornado. To get the most out of these four builds, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/grizzly-rage.png)Grizzly Rage will be the Ultimate that allows us to further amplify and scale our damage.

Overall, the Druid will have a lot of variety in the endgame. Fast builds, tankier builds, and high-DPS builds capable of climbing the Tower. My favorite build this season will be ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/shred.png)Shred, because it's by far the most complete. It's fast, making it perfect for farming for hours, and it will also have one of the highest DPS outputs this season. So, if you want to enjoy all of these Druid builds this season, don't forget to visit my Mobalytics profile, where you'll find all of these builds to destroy Sanctuary. Good luck, my fellow Druids!

**For more Druid content, check out** ***Zaior*** **on** [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@zaiorofficial) **and** [Twitch](https://www.twitch.tv/zaiorttv)**.**

## Necromancer

#### [Necromancer Class Lead - kay](https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/profile/kay)

The Necromancer has seen a lot of nerfs coming into Season 14, with the Overpower nerfs hitting necro the hardest. Multiple uniques, aspects, and glyphs related to overpower have gotten heavily nerfed such a ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/red-blessing.png)Red Blessing, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/aspects/utility.png)Tidal Aspect, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/paragon/glyphs/necromancer-dominate.png)Dominate which were all core things the class has heavily relied on for damage. And with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/aspects/defensive.png)Aspect of Glynn's Anvil going from Uncapped damage reduction to getting capped at just 40%, it means the Necromancer has also lost a core part of its survivability too this season.   And on top of that, the meta will look largely the same as season 13, with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/blood-wave.png)Blood Wave on top as the best build, and Minions not being too far behind. However there are two pretty relevant buffs the class has seen going into this season, with the first being a bug fix to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/lidless-wall.png)Lidless Wall which enables a resolve/ block stacking engine with the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/aspects/utility.png)Aspect of Interdiction and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/aspects/offensive.png)Aspect of Redirected Force aspects, which will help some builds like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/bone-spirit-astral-projection.png)Astral Projection Bone Spirit close the gap Overpower once filled. And the other relevant buff was to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/bloodless-scream.png)Bloodless Scream, with it getting ranks to darkness skills back which will really helps Darkness based Minion builds, with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/golem.png)Golem being a stand out for the season thanks to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/golems-iron.png)Golems Iron being a darkness skill to leverage the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/bloodless-scream.png)Bloodless Scream buffs as well as utilize the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/charms/peace-of-the-black-shroud.png)Berú of the Black Shroud set. Overall it'll be a pretty rough season for the Necromancer with not a lot of changes, but we'll still have some cool builds this season to look forward to

**For more Necromancer content, check out** ***kay*** **on** [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/c/mobalytics)**.**

## Rogue

#### [Mobalytics Team Lead - M1PY](https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/profile/m1py)

For Rogue the buffs to Uniques in the form of Mythic Upgrades really benefit the top builds quite a lot. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/death-trap.png)Death Trap for example was already running a decent amount of uniques and having them be stronger is a huge boon. The nerf to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/heir-of-perdition.png)Heir of Perdition does hurt for pushing, but for overall gameplay, there are ample solutions in the Helmet slot. The uniques for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/death-trap.png)Death Trap also gain a lot of useful stats by default, such as Maximum Resource and Cooldown Reduction, which allows the build to come fully online much earlier. Overall, Death Trap appears to be the best overall choice again for Rogue in Season 14, as its crazy mobility is also left untouched.  

Leveling with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/dance-of-knives.png)Dance of Knives took a bit of a hit with the nerf to it's base damage, but that nerf is quite minor and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/dance-of-knives.png)Dance of Knives is still a great choice regardless. In the endgame stages ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/dance-of-knives.png)Dance of Knives performance will take a much bigger hit compared to other builds, as it does not have many good Uniques available to slot in.  

The bow builds look quite promising and especially ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rain-of-arrows.png)Rain of Arrows with it's (hopefully) now fixed interaction with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/beastfall-boots.png)Beastfall Boots looks like a very strong contender to take ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/death-trap.png)Death Trap's crown.  

The buffs to the melee builds are quite underwhelming and there is little hope to boost them into top tier territory. However, the silver lining for these might be the easy access to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/signet-of-pelghain.png)Signet of Pelghain and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/azurewrath.png)Azurewrath for the cold explosion interaction for pushing, albeit that might be much better executed by ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/penetrating-shot.png)Penetrating Shot or even ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rain-of-arrows.png)Rain of Arrows.  

Ultimately, as long as the crazy Rogue bugs we have seen in S13 are truly fixed, the class has a lot of options to choose from and looks to be in an excellent spot for Season 14.

**For more Rogue content, check out** ***M1PY*** **on** [**YouTube**](https://www.youtube.com/@m1py) **and** [**Twitch**](https://www.twitch.tv/m1py)**.**

## Paladin

#### [Paladin Class Lead - Sanctum](https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/profile/sanctum)

Season 14 is here and things have gotten better for Paladin, but not too much so. Although many builds have gotten buffs and the most powerful builds from other classes have gotten nerfed, it is not enough and Paladin still does not have an S-tier build currently.  

![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/clash.png)Clash was the only build that could somewhat compete in overall damage output against other classes last season and it has gotten nerfed considerably; 5-10 Pit tiers.  

Tankiness has gone down a lot as ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/aspects/defensive.png)Aspect of Glynn's Anvil is now capped at 40% Damage Reduction, where previously it could get up to 95% Damage Reduction.  

On a brighter note, Wing Strike, Auradin, Zeal and Divine Lance have gotten considerably buffed and will be quite good.  

Overall, Paladin’s balance within the class has gotten a lot better. Many builds have a similar power level and level of viability, which is great. The class is no longer immortal, but tanky enough. Speedfarming capabilities with Hammerdin, Wing Strikes or Auradin should be great when stacking enough Movement Speed. If Paladin gets more love on their lackluster Talisman Sets or other Classes get nerfed further, we will finally be in a great spot again.  


**For more Paladin content, check out** ***Sanctum*** **on** [**YouTube**](https://www.youtube.com/@Goblin-Inc) **and** [**Twitch**](https://www.twitch.tv/sanctum_ttv)**.**

## Sorcerer

#### [Sorcerer Class Lead - OperatorOtter](https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/profile/745fb9b8-9460-4870-bb21-fad62eaeaedf)

The meta is getting flipped due to nerfs to how ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/unstable-currents.png)Unstable Currents is interacting. It now only affects crackling energy damage, and you cannot gain charges when at maximum crackling energy stacks. This now forces us to use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/esadoras-overflowing-cameo.png)Esadora's Overflowing Cameo to receive the stacks. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/aspects/offensive.png)Aspect of Overwhelming Currents now gives stacks "frequently" which means it's tied to a pseudo-like lucky hit chance affect being that 50-75% of the crits will grant a stack that increases our shock damage instead.   So where does this put shock builds? Well the short version is that the only top-tier shock build will be crackling energy. But even with the lightning build nerfs, many of them remain in A-Tier with "Crackling Energy" being probably the most well-rounded S-Tier Sorc build in Season 14 in terms of Pushing and Speed-Farming. The changes in Season 14 to allow any unique to be upgraded into a mythic will be utilized heavily by the sorc due to most builds revolving around many uniques with maybe 2-3 standard legendaries. This change combined with many of the redesigned and buffed aspects for fire and cold builds, allows them to rise from the ashes of Season 13 to be viable and powerful builds for Season 14.  

Three non-lightning builds to look out for in Season 14 are going to be ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/firewall.png)Firewall, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/hydra.png)Hydra Burn, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/blizzard.png)Blizzard Ice Spikes. The changes to made to Fundamental Release Paragon Legendary Node allows burn builds to really shine; and the two burn builds that are standing out are ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/firewall.png)Firewall and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/hydra.png)Hydra.   ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/firewall.png)Firewall is looking to be the best Pit Pushing build for Sorcs with a recorded clear of Pit 135 in the PTR. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/hydra.png)Hydra isn't necessarily as strong for pushing, but the buffs to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/ophidian-iris.png)Ophidian Iris and the fact it can be upgraded to Mythic in tandem with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/classes/sorcerer.svg)Fundamental Release buffs means the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/hydra.png)Hydra can instantly burn targets in T12 with a decent damage profile.  

Lastly we have ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/blizzard.png)Blizzard Ice Spikes. There are no nerfs whatsoever for this build and it was already preforming decently in Season 13, but now that things like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/blue-rose.png)Blue Rose and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/azurewrath.png)Azurewrath can become Mythics means that the overall power the build is going to increase by a further 5-10 pit tiers when it was already completing Pit 115 in Season 14.   Other non-lightning builds such as: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/ice-shards.png)Ice Shards, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/frozen-orb.png)Frozen Orb, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/fireball.png)Fireball and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/meteor.png)Meteor are all getting general buffs bringing them closer in line with lightning based-builds meaning the sorc will have a wide variety of builds that are capable of clearing T12 content.

**For more Sorcerer content, check out** ***OperatorOtter*** **on** [**YouTube**](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCrq_obHVkqLoDkWASXWNF-Q) **and** [**Twitch**](https://www.twitch.tv/operatorotter)**.**

## Spiritborn

#### [Spiritborn Class Lead - Imortilize](https://mobalytics.gg/diablo-4/profile/imortilize)

Spiritborn is looking to be as solid as ever in Season 14, falling somewhere between the top and the middle of the pack with a range of builds that will clear all the games content without the need to use any Transfigurations.  

The ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/touch-of-death-erupting-swarm.png)Erupting Swarm Touch of Death build we have all come to love is again going to top the list even after having both it's Aspects nerfed, but this time round it will be much closer between this and the other builds topping the Spiritborn list.   The ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/rod-of-kepeleke.png)Rod of Kepeleke is once again flying high with a range of builds that will all be more than capable of destroying any endgame content thrown there way. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/stinger.png)Stinger, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/crushing-hand.png)Crushing Hand, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rake.png)Rake, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/quill-volley.png)Quill Volley, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/payback.png)Payback are all going to be able to crush T12 content with a special mention going to Poison ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/stinger.png)Stinger for pushing Pits and Lightning ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/quill-volley.png)Quill Volley for pushing the Tower.  

Speed wise we took a huge hit with the gutting of ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rushing-claw-evasive-swipe.png)Evasive Swipe Rushing Claw, but that doesn't mean we haven't got other options available to us. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/sunbirds-gorget.png)Sunbird's Gorget and Evade ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/the-seeker-storm-feathers.png)Storm Feathers The Seeker will both easily farm T12 and be able to reach up to 300% Movement Speed as well as either incorporating the new Perma-Evade tech or switching to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rushing-claw-evolving-claws.png)Evolving Claws Rushing Claw in order to grant enemy lock-on mobility.   A new build on the block is Fire ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/soar.png)Soar which is getting a juicy buff in Season 14 with the new Mythics boosting the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/scorn-of-the-earth.png)Scorn of the Earth, offering a new unique way to play Spiritborn. Although not the fastest or strongest, this build will be able to reach decent Movement Speed as well as handle all T12 content thrown it's way, being especially good at bosses!  

With the new Mythic setup the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/sepazontec.png)Sepazontec is not only receiving a buff to itself but also through the mythic boosts, meaning both Fire ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rock-splitter.png)Rock Splitter and Thorns ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rock-splitter.png)Rock Splitter will be stronger than they were in Season 13. Though these builds have there struggles in certain areas of the game due to lack of damage scaling or clunky mechanics, they both offer unique build setups and will go to T12 and beyond.

Finally, at the bottom of the pack is ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/touch-of-death.png)Touch of Death which is by far our tankiest build but lacks the damage scaling to be useful beyond T12. This would be particularly good for Hardcore early on however whilst farming for gear for stronger pushing builds. Overall Spiritborn is looking pretty good in Season 14 more builds closer in power at the top and a range of builds to play for all content.

**For more Spiritborn content, check out** ***Imortilize*** **on** [**YouTube**](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCl9pV-eFiZJObvxtImD8_Eg) **and** [**Twitch**](https://www.twitch.tv/imortilize)**.**

content.text:

Diablo 4 Season 14 patch PTR 3.1 focuses on balance changes. Overpowered builds are nerfed, weaker ones buffed. Paladin, Druid, Rogue gain strength; Barbarian, Sorcerer, Spiritborn face significant nerfs. Overall, class diversity and build viability improve across the game. ... Roughly 70% of the patch notes consist of balance adjustments. The strongest builds will be nerfed, while most other archetypes receive buffs, steering the overall environment toward greater equilibrium. Currently S-tier builds are expected to drop to A or B tier, whereas bottom-tier builds will move closer to B tier. 

Zenith's base damage and Weaken Upgrade have both received enhancements. Clash's Crusader's March now offers a higher block chance.

Spiritborn has been substantially weakened overall, especially in terms of fast farming efficiency, but build diversity is expected to increase. Fiend of Abaddon receives another notable buff. Nether Step's Gloomwalker variant now properly benefits from movement speed bonuses. Wall of Agony gets a major buff, making its Encircle variant a viable survival tool. Terror Swarm's Nightmare variant is significantly improved, making this ultimate skill more usable. Wrath generation from Command Fallen has been reduced. The soul fragment demon skill of Command Valick is partially nerfed. Apocalypse Warlock build's damage bonus against surviving enemies is reduced by 90%, and even though the effect's duration is extended to 3 seconds, the loss remains huge. 

Additionally, its Evasive Swipe variant no longer counts toward Evade, preventing Spiritborn from achieving infinite mobility.

content.text:
Here's the current state of play, and one framing correction up front: **Lord of Hatred** is the expansion (released April 28, 2026 — Skovos, Paladin + Warlock, skill-tree reworks, War Plans). **3.1.0** is the patch that launched **Season 14: Death Awakening** on June 30, 2026. So you're theorycrafting on 3.1.x, not on a "3.1 LoH" patch per se. Also relevant: **3.1.1 drops tomorrow, July 14**, and it touches Spiritborn.

## Where the patch sits right now

S14 launched on 3.1.0 (Build #72578) with the Pandemonium Ruptures seasonal mechanic, the Mythic Unique 3.0 itemization rework, Solo Self-Found mode, the Tower & Leaderboards, and the Corrupted Reaper seasonal Lair Boss. The single biggest theorycrafting lever is Mythic Unique 3.0: Mythic is now a *quality* any Unique can reach, every Unique gets two guaranteed affixes, and Mythics can be enchanted with always-max-roll affixes — crafted with Pandemonium Fragments in the Horadric Cube at level 70.

That reframes the whole season. Class balance this season is driven by itemization access rather than skill tuning, so a build that reads mid-pack on paper can clear the same content as a top-ranked one once its Mythic pieces are in hand.

**3.1.1 (July 14)** mostly fixes the Mythic economy that was gating all of this: a bug that blocked Mythic drops entirely from Lair Bosses and certain other Unique sources gets fixed, Iconic Mythic roll odds go up, the Horadric Cube recipe drops from 5 Pandemonium Fragments to 4, and El'druin is added to the Blacksmith's Mythic Cache. Fragments also get easier — Corrupted Reaper drops up to two (scaling with Torment) and the repeatable Glints of Hope reward guarantees one. Superior Lair Keys get more available too.

**Spiritborn-specific in 3.1.1:** Stinger is being fixed for occasionally dealing more damage than intended (i.e. a de facto nerf), plus a Fiery Soul VFX fix and a Wyrdskin gloves fix. If you're planning to build Poison Stinger, budget for that hit.

## Spiritborn state of the class

Broad read: Spiritborn sits between the top and the middle of the pack, with a range of builds that clear all content without needing Transfigurations.

**Top / Pit push**
- Erupting Swarm Touch of Death still tops the class list even after both its Aspects were nerfed — but the gap to the rest is much narrower this season.
- Rod of Kepeleke builds (Stinger, Crushing Hand, Rake, Quill Volley, Payback) all crush T12; Poison Stinger is the standout for Pit pushing and Lightning Quill Volley for the Tower. Caveat: Stinger eats the 3.1.1 fix, and there were Quill Volley bugs where excessive movement speed got you stuck in the ground.

**Speed farming — this is where you took the damage**
- Evasive Swipe Rushing Claw got gutted; specifically, its Evasive Swipe variant no longer counts toward Evade, killing infinite mobility.
- Replacements: Sunbird's Gorget and Evade Storm Feathers "The Seeker" both farm T12 easily and hit ~300% movement speed, using the new perma-Evade tech or swapping to Evolving Claws Rushing Claw for enemy lock-on mobility.
- **Evade Counterswarm** is the one to watch — Maxroll moved Spiritborn Counterswarm up to S Tier based on performance, and it remains one of the top speedfarmers despite the S13 nerfs, using Ring of Writhing Moon (Lord Zir) to keep swarms circling and Loyalty's Mantle as your crafted Mythic for the CDR to spam Rushing Claw. With 30+ ranks in Ravager you can swap to Evolving Claws for permanent charge refill via Ferocity.

**Newly viable / off-meta**
- Fire Soar is the new build on the block, buffed via Mythic-boosted Scorn of the Earth — not the fastest or strongest, but handles all T12 and is especially good at bosses.
- Sepazontec got both a direct buff and Mythic scaling, making both Fire Rock Splitter and Thorns Rock Splitter stronger than S13, though both have scaling/clunkiness problems. Rock Splitter Thorns is still the standard fresh-character leveling shell.
- Plain Touch of Death is bottom of the pack — tankiest build in the class but lacks scaling past T12; good early Hardcore choice.

**Stat priorities:** Resource Generation and Cooldown Reduction pay off across most of the class this season.

## What I'd actually theorycraft around

Given 3.1.1's Fragment economy loosening tomorrow, the Mythic checklist stops being the bottleneck it was for the first two weeks — which favors the multi-Unique builds (Kepeleke + Ring of the Midnight Sun cores) over the ones that were "cheap to gear." If you want, tell me which direction you're leaning (Pit push, Tower, speedfarm, SSF/HC) and I'll dig into the specific skill/aspect/Paragon numbers and stress-test the build math with you.

## Build Overview

Welcome to **Allie's** guide on **Poison Swarm Spiritborn**! This was a build I fell in love with in **Season 13** and I am running it back again for **Season 14**! This build is, as far as we are aware, is going to be the top build for pushing **Tower** and the **Leaderboards** in **Season 14** on a **Spiritborn** and I plan to min-max it to the extreme!

In **S13** I held **Top 10** on the **Spiritborn Ladde**r and with **SSF**, I am looking to do it all over again while going for **Rank 1** and this build is what I will be choosing to do that with!  

In this guide we will cover all of the basics of leveling a **Spiritborn** from **1-70** as well as all of the different progression points through ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rock-splitter-shattered-stone.png)Shattered Stone Rock Splitter and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rock-splitter-inner-ferocity.png)Inner Ferocity Rock Splitter. This will be used to farm out the gear we need to swap over to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/counterattack-counterattack-of-the-swarm.png)Counterattack of the Swarm Counterattack with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/ring-of-writhing-moon.png)Ring of Writhing Moon where we will settle into our **Endgame** build!  

**---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------**  
***If you have any questions, I stream every day on*** [***Twitch***](https://www.twitch.tv/Allliee_)***and would be more than happy to help you out!***

***You are also more than free to join our*** [***Discord***](https://discord.gg/Awiee)***! We have a lot of amazing and helpful cuties there!***  
**---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------**

Swarm will be a fully automatic build where you simply just need to move forward! ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/counterattack-counterattack-of-the-swarm.png)Counterattack of the Swarm Counterattack will constantly trigger **Pestilant Swarms** which with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/uniques/ring-of-writhing-moon.png)Ring of Writhing Moon will spin around you, **Poisoning** enemies. This will be combined with many massive multipliers to cause each **Poison** you apply to be so strong that it will instantly kill any enemy you come across.

***Note - This build does require you to NumLock 4 abilities to get the most out of. At a bare minimum you will need to NumLock*** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/counterattack.png)Counterattack ***and without doing so this build is VERY APM intensive. NumLocking is easy to set-up and will be explained in the Skills Section.***

When paired up with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rushing-claw.png)Rushing Claw, we have amazing mobility at our fingertips even through the nerf that happened to it in **Season 14**.

Overall, you can expect a very fast and satisfying build that has a smooth progression curve all the way to the top and one of the most fun playstyles in the game!

## Strengths and Weaknesses

- Top Spiritborn Pushing Build.
- Automatic build if NumLocked.
- Some of the highest mobility in the game.
- Very tanky at all points in the build Post-70.

- Swarm requires gear to begin, until then we will be playing ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rock-splitter.png)Rock Splitter.
- Requires NumLocking.

For **Levels 1-15** simply focus on finding a **Weapon** that has a higher **DPS** number. You should equip any **Blue** items as you come across them and to then upgrade into **Rare** gear as it drops.

Ideally look for **Dexterity** and **Maximum Life** on your **Helmet**, **Body Armour** and **Pants**.

Try to find a pair of **Boots** with **Movement Speed** on them and never take them off unless you are upgrading to another pair with **Movement Speed**.

Finding a bit of **Life on Hit** helps with the first few levels quite a bit but will very quickly fall off as you start swapping to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/diablo-4/images/skills/rock-splitter.png)Rock Splitter.

Lastly, if you can find **Attack Speed** on your **Gloves**, **Amulet** or **Rings**, that will make everything feel much smoother. **Damage over Time**, **Vulnerable Damage** and **Poison Damage** are all solid stats too and equip any items with those as you get them. Anything **Crit** related is ok but not as strong as the other options.

content.text:
## First: your premise is wrong, and that's good news

Counterswarm is not the only Spiritborn build that reaches Pit 130+. Current data on the season says the strongest builds in the game land around Pit 140–145, a deep field clusters at 128–135, and even B-tier builds handle roughly Pit 130. And every class has at least one build capable of Pit 130+. Within Spiritborn specifically, Pestilence/Counterswarm, Stinger, and Quill Volley are all quoted at a 135+ range.

So the real question isn't "what else is viable at 130+." It's **"what has the highest ceiling above 135, and what's actually gating me right now."** Those are different problems and they have different answers.

## The genuine candidate space (mechanical cores, current patch)

**Counterswarm / Pestilence Swarm (what you're on).** Still the best overall class package post-nerf. Counterattack of the Swarm + Ring of Writhing Moon keeps swarms orbiting you, stacked with large poison multipliers. Key ceiling fact: DoT can't crit, so crit chance is worthless to you — Reaper's/Ruthless-style crit engines are dead weight in this shell. Your damage comes from DoT multipliers, Resolve, and uptime, not crit.

**Stinger (the actual Pit-depth specialist).** This is the one to look at hardest. It's the class's Poison Bomb: Withering Fist spreads poison, Stinger consumes Vigor and detonates every poisoned enemy at once, and it's widely treated as the sharper pick for pushing Pit depth specifically. The push variant swaps to the Berú of the Multitude 3pc with Seal of the Golden Epiphany, Ring of the Midnight Sun, Locran's Talisman, and Protean Heart — explicitly a push-oriented Talisman config, with Harmony of Ebewaka and Rod of Kepeleke both as Mythics. **Caveat you must price in: 3.1.1 (tomorrow) fixes Stinger dealing more damage than intended.** Nobody has clean post-fix Pit numbers yet. That's a real risk, but it also means the *current* published Stinger numbers are inflated and post-patch you'll want to re-benchmark, not re-roll blind.

**Quill Volley.** Harmony of Ebewaka + Berú of the Multitude 2pc gives it multiple Spirit tags simultaneously; Rod of Kepeleke gives it the Basic tag and strips the Vigor cost so you can spam it. Reaper's + Ruthless together get you to 100% crit since QV is both Eagle and Jaguar, with Scourge used to poison and enable Reaper's. It's the Tower pick more than the Pit pick — but note it's a *crit* build, which means it scales off a completely different multiplier stack than your Counterswarm. That makes it a real hedge, not a sidegrade.

**Erupting Swarm Touch of Death.** Still tops the class list even after both its Aspects were nerfed, but the field is much tighter behind it now. It's the delayed-payoff poison spread rather than a clean instant hit — which is exactly why it absorbed the itemization changes better than mobility-dependent lines.

**Crushing Hand.** The Gorilla shell. Path of the Emissary auto-casting Quill Volley as you move feeds extra hits into the Berú of Rezoka's Rage 2pc, and Prodigy's Tempo handles cooldowns. Its selling point is that it needs almost no Mythic investment to feel complete — which is a *floor* advantage, not a ceiling advantage. Probably not your 140 build.

**Fringe with an argument:** Fire Soar (Mythic-boosted Scorn of the Earth, weak clear but explicitly strong at bosses) and Sepazontec Fire/Thorns Rock Splitter (buffed directly *and* through Mythic scaling, stronger than S13, but with real scaling and clunkiness problems).

## Where the 135→145 ceiling actually comes from this season

This is the part I'd focus your effort on, because it's build-agnostic:

1. **Mythic Unique 3.0 is the multiplier this season, not skills.** Class balance is being driven by itemization access rather than skill tuning — a build that reads mid-pack can clear the same content as a top-ranked one once its Mythic pieces are in hand. Every Unique can reach Mythic quality, gets two guaranteed affixes, and Mythics enchant with always-max-roll affixes. If you're at 130 and stuck, the question is almost certainly *which Uniques haven't you Mythic'd yet*, not *which skill should I swap to*.
2. **Tomorrow's patch materially loosens that.** Lair Bosses were bugged to drop zero Mythics; that's fixed. Cube recipe goes 5 → 4 Fragments. Corrupted Reaper drops up to 2 Fragments scaling with Torment, and Glints of Hope guarantees one. Your Mythic acquisition rate is about to jump, which changes the calculus on any build with a long Mythic checklist (Stinger, Erupting Swarm) versus a short one (Crushing Hand).
3. **Glyphs and War Plans.** Finish War Plans progress for The Pit to allocate Choron's Haste and Choron's Wager — extra glyph upgrade chances per run. At 130+ glyph ranks are a huge chunk of your remaining multiplier.
4. **Resistances, not damage.** Monsters from Pit 130 onward deal so much damage that resistances should be a top priority. Most people stuck at 130 are dying, not failing DPS checks.
5. **Defensive nerf you're eating:** Armored Hide lost Unstoppable, which is a real defensive nerf that has to be offset through gear — though Evade Counterswarm doesn't primarily rely on it for survivability.

## What I need from you to do this properly

Here's my honest constraint: I can pull the meta layer and the mechanical cores, but the exact aspect multiplier values, skill-node numbers, and paragon glyph scaling for the post-Lord-of-Hatred skill trees aren't something I can reliably retrieve — the build planners are JS-rendered and my own knowledge predates the LoH rework. I'm not going to invent multiplier numbers and hand you fake math; that would waste days of your farming.

**So paste me your actual setup and I'll do real optimization on it:** your current gear with affixes/tempers/masterwork, your Talisman + Seal + Charms, your skill tree allocation, your paragon boards/glyphs and glyph ranks, your current Pit clear tier + roughly where you're failing (timer or deaths), and which Mythics you already have vs. which you're missing.

With that I can (a) tell you whether you're DPS-gated or defense-gated at 130, (b) find the dead multipliers in your sheet — crit stats on a DoT build being the classic one, (c) build a Stinger-vs-Counterswarm decision tree that accounts for tomorrow's Stinger fix, and (d) sequence your Mythic crafting against the new 4-Fragment cost so you're not burning Pandemonium on the wrong slot.

I'm seeing there's actually two different things called "Multitude" here — Berú of the Multitude is a specific charm that appears in different set configurations, with the two-piece giving damage bonuses and enabling certain abilities, while the three-piece version provides passive effects like Armored Hide.

The full set is called Bliss of the Multitude, and its individual charms are named after different spirits (Phoba, Fer, Mlor, Linta, and Berú). The set bonuses work by having your Ultimate Skill active grant all your skills that spirit type, which then stacks damage bonuses based on how many spirit types you have. Higher piece counts add resistance and passive effects from those spirits, plus a chance to invoke the Ultimate Spirit itself for increased damage.

Now looking at Wumba's Embrace Set, which starts with a two-piece bonus of 7000 Thorns.

The blocking mechanic pulses Thorns around you with a 20% chance, and this damage counts as a Gorilla Skill. The three-piece adds 30% Block Chance and 20% Damage Reduction, while the five-piece makes Gorilla Skills deal 125% more damage and grants the Gorilla Primary Spirit Hall bonus for free at 250% potency.

There's an important caveat about Multitude's five-piece — it automatically invokes ultimates, which conflicts with ultimate aspects like Supremacy and Vehement Brawler, putting them on cooldown and preventing stacking. That's why the top guides use Multitude as a partial set (2pc with Rezoka's Rage, or 3pc with Crushing Hand and Stinger push) rather than going all the way to five pieces.

Wumba's five-piece is more interesting for new builds because freeing up your Primary Spirit Hall slot at 250% potency means you can choose a different Primary Spirit instead of being locked into Gorilla.

I'm also noting that Balazan's Maxtlatl converts Thorns to poison with 150% Thorns damage plus poison scaling up to 300%, which pairs naturally with Wumba's 7000 Thorns and the pulse mechanic — creating a real Thorns-poison engine. And Hesha e Kesungi gives massive damage bonuses when skills are Gorilla-tagged, which synergizes with both Multitude's two-piece (Protector gets the Gorilla tag) and Wumba's setup. I should note this data is from Season 9, so the numbers might have shifted since then.

Now I'm mapping out two concrete build paths. The first direction leverages Wumba's five-piece for the Gorilla/Thorns engine with a free Spirit Hall at 250% potency — the key insight being that getting Spirit Hall for free opens up your Primary Spirit Hall slot for a second spirit tag without sacrificing the slot itself. Combined with Harmony of Ebewaka's spirit tag damage scaling and Hesha e Kesungi's Gorilla bonuses, this creates a powerful multi-tag synergy.

The critical detail I'm verifying: Wumba's free Gorilla Primary bonus applies the Gorilla tag to all skills at 250% potency, which means every skill in your rotation becomes a Gorilla skill while freeing up your actual Primary slot for additional spirit stacking — essentially the same multi-tag engine Quill Volley builds around, but achieved through Wumba's instead of relying on The Protector uptime.

However, there's a constraint I need to work through: a 5-piece Wumba set consumes all five charm slots, leaving only one slot for a unique charm, which means you can't also run Multitude's 2-piece bonus for the 15% per-tag damage scaling. So while the free Gorilla tag is valuable, you're trading off the multiplicative per-tag damage that makes other spirit stacking builds so potent.

The real scaling comes from Harmony of Ebewaka, which provides per-tag damage scaling in the 25-39% range. Block chance becomes your proc rate driver here—30% from the 3-piece plus Gorilla block synergies like Counterattack and Armored Hide. Your existing poison and DoT paragon choices transfer over since you're already in that design space. The main risk is that Thorns scaling historically struggles at very high Pit tiers because it's flat damage that doesn't multiply well, though the recent Sepazontec buffs and Mythic boosts have made Thorns Rock Splitter more viable than it was in Season 13.

For a Multitude-based approach, the core engine is already built into Quill Volley and Crushing Hand, so the strategy becomes finding an underutilized skill to feed through that tag-stacking system. Candidates include Payback, Rake, Crushing Hand variants, Soar, or Touch of Death—you activate The Protector's Gorilla ultimate to tag all skills, which triggers the Harmony of Ebewaka multipliers and unlocks Hesha e Kesungi. The catch is that the 5-piece Multitude auto-invoke has reported issues with ultimate aspects like Supremacy and Vehement Brawler, so there's a compatibility problem to work around.

## What each set actually does

**Bliss of the Multitude** (charms: Phoba / Fer / Mlor / Linta / Berú of the Multitude):
- **2pc** — While an Ultimate is active, your skills gain that Ultimate's Spirit type. Skills deal 15% increased damage per Spirit type they have.
- **3pc** — Casting a Skill grants 35% Resistance to its Spirit's primary damage type and the Passive effect of that Spirit's Incarnate Skill for 10s.
- **5pc** — Casting a Skill has a 5% chance to invoke the Ultimate Spirit of that Skill's type and increase damage from that Spirit by 50% for 10s.

**Wumba's Embrace:**
- **2pc** — Gain 7000 Thorns. Blocking has a 20% chance to pulse your Thorns around you. **This damage counts as a Gorilla Skill.**
- **3pc** — 30% Block Chance and 20% Damage Reduction.
- **5pc** — Gorilla Skills deal 125% increased damage. **Gain the Gorilla Primary Spirit Hall bonus for free with 250% potency.**

## The honest read: Multitude isn't "new"

Multitude is already the backbone of half the class. Quill Volley is *built* around the 2pc: The Protector active → all skills become Gorilla → +20% from Multitude, +25–39% from Harmony of Ebewaka, and it unlocks Hesha e Kesungi as a massive bonus since your skills now count as Gorilla. Crushing Hand runs a 6-slot Seal to hold Berú of Rezoka's Rage 2p *and* Berú of the Multitude 3p simultaneously, plus Protean Heart. Stinger's push variant runs Multitude 3p with Seal of the Golden Epiphany, Ring of the Midnight Sun, Locran's, Protean Heart.

So if you want Multitude, you're not finding a new set — you're finding a **new skill to run through the existing Multitude tag-stack engine.** That's legitimate, but understand what you're doing.

**And do not chase the 5pc.** There's a known anti-synergy: the auto-invoked Ultimates don't work with Ultimate aspects like Supremacy, and because the set casts the Ultimate for you it goes on cooldown, so you can't cast it yourself to stack Supremacy / Vehement Brawler. Multitude is a 2pc/3pc partial, full stop.

## Wumba's 5pc is the actually unexplored lever

Here's why it interests me far more, and it's the "free Spirit Hall slot" clause.

Primary Spirit Hall grants that Spirit's tag to *all* your skills — that's the mechanic every tag-stacking build exploits (Quill Volley takes Centipede Primary for DR and Jaguar Secondary, then borrows Gorilla via The Protector). Wumba's 5pc hands you **the Gorilla Primary bonus for free, at 250% potency**, without spending your Primary slot.

If that resolves the way the text reads, you get:
- Gorilla tag on everything, permanently, with **no Protector uptime requirement** — Quill Volley's whole engine is conditional on The Protector being active; yours wouldn't be.
- Your actual Primary Spirit Hall slot freed for a second spirit → more tags → more Harmony of Ebewaka scaling (which pays per tag) → **Hesha e Kesungi live at all times.**

**The poison bridge, which is the part you already know how to play:** Balazan's Maxtlatl converts each Thorns retaliation into Poisoning, ramping the poison damage the more you retaliate. Thorns doesn't crit and DoT doesn't crit — which is *the same design space as your Counterswarm*. Your poison/DoT paragon, glyphs, and DoT multiplier instincts largely transfer. 1. **Thorns scaling is the class's known weak point.** The Spiritborn class lead flagged Thorns/Fire Rock Splitter as struggling from lack of damage scaling and clunky mechanics — good to T12 and beyond, but that's not a 135+ endorsement. The 125%[x] Gorilla multiplier and 250%-potency Hall bonus are exactly what a thorns build has historically lacked, which is why this is worth testing — but it's a hypothesis, not a proven Pit 140 build.
2. **Sepazontec got buffed directly and through Mythic scaling, making Thorns Rock Splitter stronger than S13** — so the thorns shell is at least trending up, not down.
3. **5 charm slots are consumed by the set**, leaving you ~1 unique charm slot on a 6-slot Seal. You give up the Rezoka's Rage 2pc (+50% Crit Damage, 25% Cast Speed) — but you don't want crit damage on a Thorns/DoT build anyway. That's a *clean* tradeoff, which is a good sign.
4. Some of the item numbers I'm working from (Balazan's Maxtlatl's thorns→poison conversion, Razorplate) predate the current patch's item pass and need re-verification in-game before you commit Pandemonium Fragments.

## What I need to take this from theory to a spec

I'm not going to hand you a full Pit-140 skill tree and paragon board built on multipliers I can't verify — the planners are JS-rendered and I'd be guessing at post-Lord-of-Hatred node values, which would cost you days of farming.

**Two things and I can build the whole thing out:**
1. Go into the game and check the *current* tooltips for: Wumba's 5pc exact wording (specifically whether the free Gorilla Hall bonus applies the Gorilla **tag** to all skills or only the passive damage bonus — the entire build hinges on this), Balazan's Maxtlatl, Hesha e Kesungi, and Harmony of Ebewaka. Paste them to me verbatim.
2. Tell me which Gorilla skill you'd want as the payload — Crushing Hand, Rock Splitter, Counterattack, or "let the Thorns pulse *be* the build."

With those, I'll spec the Spirit Hall pairing, block-stacking, aspect list, and paragon/glyph priorities, and give you an honest go/no-go on whether it can beat your Counterswarm at 130+ before you spend a single Fragment.

The Spiritborn is the new class that will be added in the expansion for Diablo 4, Vessel of Hatred to be released on 8th October 2024. [1] Spiritborn are native to the jungles of Nahantu, where Vessel of Hatred takes place, and they are deeply rooted in the elements of nature and the spiritual realm. They are the children of the wild, born from the spirit of the plains, sky, soil, and forest. Their souls are intertwined with the world around them, drawing strength from the very essence of life and nature. They are connected to four Spirit Guardians: Rezoka (Jaguar), Balazan (Centipede), Kwatli (Eagle), and Wumba (Gorilla), each representing different aspects like courage, balance, awareness, and protection. Spiritborn are versatile warriors who fuse three-hit-combo attacks and acrobatic fluidity. 

Its movement speed and amplified Evade, combined with extendable mid-ranged attacks and a control of Lightning, come together to deliver a concentrated burst of pain upon your foes. Gorilla (Wumba) - The embodiment of resilience and retaliation, the Gorilla not only shrugs off incom

Once you’ve reached Level 15 as a Spiritborn, seek out Tarka, a Spiritborn emissary in Gea Kul. Together, you’ll embark on a quest for your destiny, becoming more attuned to the ways of the Spirit Guardians. Completing the Sacred Hunt quest unlocks the Spirit Hall, the Spiritborn’s Class Mechanic. Using the Spirit Hall, Spiritborn can enhance their connection to the Spirit Guardians. Select one of the 4 Guardian Spirits as your Primary Spirit. Doing so will grant you a special passive bonus, but it also adds that Spirit’s Skill Tag to all your Skills, allowing its Spirit-based bonuses to carry to each of your Skills.

content.thinking:
I'm seeing there's actually two different things called "Multitude" here — Berú of the Multitude is a specific charm that appears in different set configurations, with the two-piece giving damage bonuses and enabling certain abilities, while the three-piece version provides passive effects like Armored Hide.

The full set is called Bliss of the Multitude, and its individual charms are named after different spirits (Phoba, Fer, Mlor, Linta, and Berú). The set bonuses work by having your Ultimate Skill active grant all your skills that spirit type, which then stacks damage bonuses based on how many spirit types you have. Higher piece counts add resistance and passive effects from those spirits, plus a chance to invoke the Ultimate Spirit itself for increased damage.

Now looking at Wumba's Embrace Set, which starts with a two-piece bonus of 7000 Thorns.

The blocking mechanic pulses Thorns around you with a 20% chance, and this damage counts as a Gorilla Skill. The three-piece adds 30% Block Chance and 20% Damage Reduction, while the five-piece makes Gorilla Skills deal 125% more damage and grants the Gorilla Primary Spirit Hall bonus for free at 250% potency.

There's an important caveat about Multitude's five-piece — it automatically invokes ultimates, which conflicts with ultimate aspects like Supremacy and Vehement Brawler, putting them on cooldown and preventing stacking. That's why the top guides use Multitude as a partial set (2pc with Rezoka's Rage, or 3pc with Crushing Hand and Stinger push) rather than going all the way to five pieces.

Wumba's five-piece is more interesting for new builds because freeing up your Primary Spirit Hall slot at 250% potency means you can choose a different Primary Spirit instead of being locked into Gorilla.

I'm also noting that Balazan's Maxtlatl converts Thorns to poison with 150% Thorns damage plus poison scaling up to 300%, which pairs naturally with Wumba's 7000 Thorns and the pulse mechanic — creating a real Thorns-poison engine. And Hesha e Kesungi gives massive damage bonuses when skills are Gorilla-tagged, which synergizes with both Multitude's two-piece (Protector gets the Gorilla tag) and Wumba's setup. I should note this data is from Season 9, so the numbers might have shifted since then.

Now I'm mapping out two concrete build paths. The first direction leverages Wumba's five-piece for the Gorilla/Thorns engine with a free Spirit Hall at 250% potency — the key insight being that getting Spirit Hall for free opens up your Primary Spirit Hall slot for a second spirit tag without sacrificing the slot itself. Combined with Harmony of Ebewaka's spirit tag damage scaling and Hesha e Kesungi's Gorilla bonuses, this creates a powerful multi-tag synergy.

The critical detail I'm verifying: Wumba's free Gorilla Primary bonus applies the Gorilla tag to all skills at 250% potency, which means every skill in your rotation becomes a Gorilla skill while freeing up your actual Primary slot for additional spirit stacking — essentially the same multi-tag engine Quill Volley builds around, but achieved through Wumba's instead of relying on The Protector uptime.

However, there's a constraint I need to work through: a 5-piece Wumba set consumes all five charm slots, leaving only one slot for a unique charm, which means you can't also run Multitude's 2-piece bonus for the 15% per-tag damage scaling. So while the free Gorilla tag is valuable, you're trading off the multiplicative per-tag damage that makes other spirit stacking builds so potent.

The real scaling comes from Harmony of Ebewaka, which provides per-tag damage scaling in the 25-39% range. I should note that I'm working through these interactions based on what I understand from the mechanics—some of this needs in-game verification to confirm. The key synergy is that Thorns pulses count as Gorilla skills, so they benefit from both the 5-piece Gorilla damage increase and the Primary Spirit Hall bonus at 250% potency. Good — that's a much sharper constraint, and it's worth clearing up something first because "Multitude" and "Wumba's" are not symmetric options.

## What each set actually does

**Bliss of the Multitude** (charms: Phoba / Fer / Mlor / Linta / Berú of the Multitude):
- **2pc** — While an Ultimate is active, your skills gain that Ultimate's Spirit type. Skills deal 15% increased damage per Spirit type they have.
- **3pc** — Casting a Skill grants 35% Resistance to its Spirit's primary damage type and the Passive effect of that Spirit's Incarnate Skill for 10s.
- **5pc** — Casting a Skill has a 5% chance to invoke the Ultimate Spirit of that Skill's type and increase damage from that Spirit by 50% for 10s.

**Wumba's Embrace:**
- **2pc** — Gain 7000 Thorns. Blocking has a 20% chance to pulse your Thorns around you. **This damage counts as a Gorilla Skill.**
- **3pc** — 30% Block Chance and 20% Damage Reduction.
- **5pc** — Gorilla Skills deal 125% increased damage. **Gain the Gorilla Primary Spirit Hall bonus for free with 250% potency.**

## The honest read: Multitude isn't "new"

Multitude is already the backbone of half the class. Quill Volley is *built* around the 2pc: The Protector active → all skills become Gorilla → +20% from Multitude, +25–39% from Harmony of Ebewaka, and it unlocks Hesha e Kesungi as a massive bonus since your skills now count as Gorilla. Crushing Hand runs a 6-slot Seal to hold Berú of Rezoka's Rage 2p *and* Berú of the Multitude 3p simultaneously, plus Protean Heart. Stinger's push variant runs Multitude 3p with Seal of the Golden Epiphany, Ring of the Midnight Sun, Locran's, Protean Heart.

So if you want Multitude, you're not finding a new set — you're finding a **new skill to run through the existing Multitude tag-stack engine.** That's legitimate, but understand what you're doing.

**And do not chase the 5pc.** There's a known anti-synergy: the auto-invoked Ultimates don't work with Ultimate aspects like Supremacy, and because the set casts the Ultimate for you it goes on cooldown, so you can't cast it yourself to stack Supremacy / Vehement Brawler. Multitude is a 2pc/3pc partial, full stop.

## Wumba's 5pc is the actually unexplored lever

Here's why it interests me far more, and it's the "free Spirit Hall slot" clause.

Primary Spirit Hall grants that Spirit's tag to *all* your skills — that's the mechanic every tag-stacking build exploits (Quill Volley takes Centipede Primary for DR and Jaguar Secondary, then borrows Gorilla via The Protector). Wumba's 5pc hands you **the Gorilla Primary bonus for free, at 250% potency**, without spending your Primary slot.

If that resolves the way the text reads, you get:
- Gorilla tag on everything, permanently, with **no Protector uptime requirement** — Quill Volley's whole engine is conditional on The Protector being active; yours wouldn't be.
- Your actual Primary Spirit Hall slot freed for a second spirit → more tags → more Harmony of Ebewaka scaling (which pays per tag) → **Hesha e Kesungi live at all times.**
- 125% increased Gorilla damage on top of it.
- The Thorns pulse itself counts as a Gorilla skill, so it eats the 125% *and* the 250%-potency Gorilla Hall bonus.

**The poison bridge, which is the part you already know how to play:** Balazan's Maxtlatl converts each Thorns retaliation into Poisoning, ramping the poison damage the more you retaliate. Thorns doesn't crit and DoT doesn't crit — which is *the same design space as your Counterswarm*. Your poison/DoT paragon, glyphs, and DoT multiplier instincts largely transfer. You'd be rebuilding the damage engine, not relearning the class.

**Proc-rate driver is Block, not attack speed.** The pulse fires on block (20% chance per block), and the 3pc hands you 30% Block Chance for free. Block sources become your "attack speed" equivalent. Counterattack and Armored Hide already live in the Gorilla/block space.

## Where this can fail, stated up front

1. **Thorns scaling is the class's known weak point.** The Spiritborn class lead flagged Thorns/Fire Rock Splitter as struggling from lack of damage scaling and clunky mechanics — good to T12 and beyond, but that's not a 135+ endorsement. The 125%[x] Gorilla multiplier and 250%-potency Hall bonus are exactly what a thorns build has historically lacked, which is why this is worth testing — but it's a hypothesis, not a proven Pit 140 build.
2. **Sepazontec got buffed directly and through Mythic scaling, making Thorns Rock Splitter stronger than S13** — so the thorns shell is at least trending up, not down.
3. **5 charm slots are consumed by the set**, leaving you ~1 unique charm slot on a 6-slot Seal. You give up the Rezoka's Rage 2pc (+50% Crit Damage, 25% Cast Speed) — but you don't want crit damage on a Thorns/DoT build anyway. That's a *clean* tradeoff, which is a good sign.
4. Some of the item numbers I'm working from (Balazan's Maxtlatl's thorns→poison conversion, Razorplate) predate the current patch's item pass and need re-verification in-game before you commit Pandemonium Fragments.

## What I need to take this from theory to a spec

I'm not going to hand you a full Pit-140 skill tree and paragon board built on multipliers I can't verify — the planners are JS-rendered and I'd be guessing at post-Lord-of-Hatred node values, which would cost you days of farming.

**Two things and I can build the whole thing out:**
1. Go into the game and check the *current* tooltips for: Wumba's 5pc exact wording (specifically whether the free Gorilla Hall bonus applies the Gorilla **tag** to all skills or only the passive damage bonus — the entire build hinges on this), Balazan's Maxtlatl, Hesha e Kesungi, and Harmony of Ebewaka. Paste them to me verbatim.
2. Tell me which Gorilla skill you'd want as the payload — Crushing Hand, Rock Splitter, Counterattack, or "let the Thorns pulse *be* the build."

With those, I'll spec the Spirit Hall pairing, block-stacking, aspect list, and paragon/glyph priorities, and give you an honest go/no-go on whether it can beat your Counterswarm at 130+ before you spend a single Fragment.

There's also an important affix constraint to consider — you can't stack both DoT and Critical Strike Damage multipliers on the same item, which limits how you can build around Thorns damage.

Read that second clause carefully — the Thorns retaliation isn't the damage, it's the **thing that turns the poison amp on**. Thorns is a buff-uptime engine for a poison payload you already know how to scale. (Numbers are from an older patch; verify.)

**2. It's a Gorilla-skill proc event.** Wumba's 2pc: the Thorns pulse on block **counts as a Gorilla Skill**. That means it's a hit event that carries the Gorilla tag — it can feed Gorilla-tagged effects, Hesha e Kesungi, and lucky-hit rolls without you casting anything.

**3. It's the defensive layer.** 3pc gives 30% Block Chance and 20% Damage Reduction. Remember the earlier point — at Pit 130+ monsters deal so much damage that resistances/defense are the top priority. Most people stalling at 130 are dying, not failing DPS checks. And Block is also your *proc rate*, so defense and offense are the same stat here. That's an unusually clean design.

## Now the actual reveal

Look at the 5pc again with fresh eyes:

> **Your Gorilla Skills deal 125% increased damage. Gain the Gorilla Primary Spirit Hall bonus for free with 250% potency.**

Primary Spirit Hall applies its spirit's tag to *all your skills* — that's the documented mechanic (Maxroll: "Jaguar Primary gives bonus damage and **turns all your skills into Jaguar skills**").

So if the free Gorilla Hall bonus carries the tag, then **every skill you have becomes a Gorilla skill — which means the 125% increased damage applies to your entire kit, unconditionally.** Wumba's stops being a Thorns set and becomes:

- A ~125%[x] global damage multiplier on everything
- A **free Primary Spirit Hall slot** (take Centipede for poison/DR — your native space)
- Gorilla Hall bonus at **250% potency**, which is a bigger version of what Quill Volley bends over backwards to get via The Protector uptime — except yours is permanent and unconditional
- Hesha e Kesungi live at all times (it wants Gorilla skills)
- Harmony of Ebewaka paying out on the extra tag
- Plus 30% block, 20% DR, and a self-fueling poison amp

That's not a Thorns build. That's a **poison DoT build wearing a Thorns chassis**, and the payload can be whatever Centipede skill you want — Counterattack of the Swarm, Touch of Death / Erupting Swarm, Withering Fist. Your existing DoT paragon, glyphs, and affix priorities largely carry over.

## The single load-bearing unknown

Everything above collapses to nothing if the 5pc's "gain the Gorilla Primary Spirit Hall bonus" grants only the **damage bonus** and not the **tag**. In that case the 125% applies only to genuinely Gorilla-tagged skills (Crushing Hand, Rock Splitter, Counterattack, The Protector), and you're back to a mediocre Gorilla build.

That one clause is the difference between a possible new S-tier and a dead end. **Go read the in-game tooltip and check your character sheet for whether non-Gorilla skills show the Gorilla tag with the set equipped.** That's a five-minute test and it decides everything.

## The cost, stated plainly

The 5pc eats five charm slots. On a 6-slot Seal you keep exactly one unique charm. That means you surrender the Crushing Hand/Stinger-style setup that runs Berú of Rezoka's Rage 2p + Berú of the Multitude 3p + Ring of the Midnight Sun + Locran's + Protean Heart.

Losing Rezoka's (+50% Crit Damage, 25% Cast Speed) and Locran's costs you nothing — DoT can't crit, so you were never using them. **Losing Ring of the Midnight Sun as a charm hurts**, because that's what frees your ring slot and drives the Rod of Kepeleke resource engine. Decide what your one remaining charm is: almost certainly Ring of the Midnight Sun or Protean Heart.

If the tag test comes back positive, send me the result plus your current Counterswarm tooltip numbers and I'll build the side-by-side calculator so you can see the real gap before committing Fragments.

I'm noticing some significant discrepancies between the live tooltip and the wiki documentation. The 2-piece bonus got buffed from 7,000 to 10,000 Thorns, the 3-piece now grants 30% Block and 25% DR instead of 20%, and the 5-piece Gorilla Skills damage multiplier increased from 125% to 150% with confirmed multiplicative scaling. The tooltip also mentions a Gorilla Primary Spirit Hall bonus that appears to be cut off.

The key insight is that the Gorilla Primary Spirit Hall bonus grants only the passive bonus component (250% additive potency) without adding the Gorilla skill tag to all abilities — which explains why the user didn't see their skills tagged as Gorilla despite equipping the set. The Primary Spirit Hall mechanic has two parts: the tag addition and the passive bonus, and Wumba's 5-piece is specifically granting just the bonus portion.

This opens up alternative paths to actually get the Gorilla tag: you could manually select Gorilla as your Primary Spirit Hall yourself to get both the tag and bonus, though that might create redundancy with the set's free bonus. Or you could use Berú of the Multitude's 2-piece effect, which grants the Gorilla Ultimate's spirit type to all skills while an Ultimate is active — the same engine as Quill Volley — but that requires 2 charm slots while Wumba's already takes 5, creating a tight constraint. have Gorilla as a passive bonus while picking a different Primary Spirit Hall like Centipede for its own tag and bonus. But then the 150% multiplier only amplifies actual Gorilla skills—Crushing Hand, Rock Splitter, Counterattack, and the rest—so Wumba's 5pc is really built around a Gorilla-focused build rather than being universally useful.

The key insight is that if you actually slot Gorilla as your Primary Hall, all your skills become Gorilla skills and get the full 150% multiplier, which is the real power play. That said, the set's free Gorilla bonus at 250% potency might then be redundant or stack in some way—I need to test this. Either way, you're getting solid defensive layers: 10,000 Thorns, 30% block, 25% damage reduction, plus the Thorns pulse effect.

Comparing this to other approaches like Quill Volley using The Protector and Multitude 2pc, the Gorilla Primary Hall route gives you a flat 150% global multiplier across your entire kit for just the cost of your Primary slot and 5 charm slots, which is actually pretty efficient. But I need to figure out what the Gorilla Primary Hall's actual bonus is—something about gaining Resolve stacks—to properly evaluate whether that 250% potency bonus is truly redundant or if there's real synergy there.Excellent test — and it kills the assumption cleanly. Look at the exact wording:

> Gain the Gorilla Primary Spirit Hall **bonus** for free with 250%**[+]** potency.

It grants the **bonus**, not the **tag**. Those are two separate halves of the Spirit Hall mechanic (selecting a Primary Spirit gives you a passive bonus *and* stamps that spirit's tag onto all your skills). The set hands you only the first half. Your in-game result confirms it. My read was wrong — good that you checked before spending anything.

Also worth noting your live tooltip is **buffed** versus the wiki data I was working from: 10,000 Thorns (not 7,000), 25% DR (not 20%), and **150%[x]** Gorilla damage (not 125%). And that `[x]` is explicit — it's a true global multiplier.

## What this actually means

The 150%[x] only applies to skills that genuinely carry the Gorilla tag. So the set is not a universal multiplier — **it's a Gorilla-skill build enabler.** Which leaves exactly two ways to make the 150%[x] cover your whole kit:

**Route 1 — Take Gorilla as your Primary Spirit Hall yourself.**
Your selection provides the tag; every skill becomes Gorilla; the 150%[x] applies to everything. This is the obvious play and it's clean.

The open question: **does the set's free 250%[+] potency Gorilla bonus stack with your own Gorilla Primary selection, or is it wasted/overwritten?** Note the potency is `[+]` (additive), not `[x]`. If it stacks, you're getting a Gorilla Primary at 350% potency. If it's redundant, you're paying nothing extra anyway — you'd still have 150%[x] on your entire kit, 10k Thorns, 30% Block, 25% DR. **Test it: select Gorilla Primary with the set on and see whether the Hall bonus value on your sheet goes up.**

**Route 2 — Berú of the Multitude 2pc.**
Its 2pc gives your skills the Ultimate's Spirit type while that Ultimate is active — The Protector is the Gorilla Ultimate, so it stamps Gorilla on everything. That's precisely the engine Quill Volley uses. **But you can't have both:** Wumba's 5pc eats 5 charm slots, Multitude 2pc needs 2, and the max Seal is 6 slots. Route 2 is mutually exclusive with the Wumba's 5pc.

So: **Route 1 or nothing.**

## Reframing the build honestly

With Gorilla Primary selected, Wumba's becomes:

- **150%[x] global multiplier on your entire kit** — that's a genuinely large, unconditional, no-uptime-requirement multiplier
- Gorilla Primary Hall bonus, possibly at inflated potency
- 30% Block Chance, 25% Damage Reduction — real Pit 130+ survivability, which is where most people actually stall
- 10,000 Thorns + a Gorilla-tagged pulse on block, which (via Maxtlatl) feeds the poison amp — Thorns as *enabler*, exactly as you reframed it

**The cost:** your Primary Spirit Hall is locked to Gorilla, so you lose Centipede Primary's damage reduction and you can't run the tag-stacking that Quill Volley/Crushing Hand use to pile up Harmony of Ebewaka scaling. You also lose Ring of the Midnight Sun / Locran's / Protean Heart as charms (one slot left on a 6-slot Seal).

## The comparison that decides it

You're trading **Harmony of Ebewaka's per-tag scaling + Multitude's 15%-per-spirit-type + Rezoka's crit package** for **a flat 150%[x] + a big defensive block.**

Multi-tag stacking is a *multiplicative* engine that grows with tag count. A flat 150%[x] is a *fixed* 2.5×. Against a build already running 3–4 spirit tags, the flat 2.5× may well be smaller than what you're giving up.

So the two things I'd want before going further:

1. **Does the 250%[+] potency stack with a self-selected Gorilla Primary?** (Sheet check.)
2. **What is the Gorilla Primary Spirit Hall bonus, exactly, and what does 250%[+] potency turn it into?** Paste that tooltip — if it's a Resolve/damage-reduction bonus, this is a defensive build; if it's a damage bonus, at 250%[+] potency it could be the actual payload and the whole thing changes.

Send me those two and I'll tell you whether this beats Counterswarm or whether it's a very tanky B-tier.

## Short answer: no. Not if a specific [x] Poison Damage transfig is the goal.

The Entropic Tuning Prism **removes both the riskiest and the most powerful outcomes** from the Transfiguration pool. Concretely, per Maxroll, it removes the **Indestructible, Replace Affix, and Greater Affix** outcomes — and critically, **the affixes available via a Bonus Affix outcome are reduced to a handful of generic options.**
