Model confirmed. Let me give you my recommendation on the snapshot behavior, because it's the one piece with real subtlety, and it interacts with the quote-number decision you just made.

**Recommendation: each send re-snapshots — versioned sent-snapshots, same quote number.** Here's the reasoning, and why it fits what you chose:

You said same quote number, new version (customer sees "revised quote DPS-XXXX"). That decision basically forces the snapshot answer, and cleanly. If the customer got DPS-1009 v1, then a revised DPS-1009 v2, you need **both snapshots to persist** — because there's a real scenario where the customer replies "I'm accepting the *first* version you sent," and the PM needs to know exactly what v1 said. If revising just overwrote the snapshot, you'd lose the record of what the customer actually received first. So:

- **Each send writes a new sent-snapshot, tagged with the version** (`version_number` already exists on the schema). DPS-1009 v1 snapshot, DPS-1009 v2 snapshot — both retained.
- **`sent_at` refreshes to the latest send** (or you keep a per-version sent timestamp — the version chain already supports this).
- **The snapshot fleet from Slice 11** (`pdf_layout`/`detail_level`/`include_spec_addendum` + commercial defaults + prepared-by) captures per-version, so each sent version is a faithful record of what that customer saw.

This is actually what the existing versioning machinery was built for — `version_number` auto-increments within `(project_id, scenario_label)`, and `superseded` is the state for "PM edited a sent quote → new draft." So **the schema already supports revise-in-place-with-versioned-snapshots**; you're not inventing it, you're *using* what's there instead of blocking it with the Send-lock. That's another sign this model is the right one — it works *with* the existing design rather than against it.

There's a subtlety worth naming: this connects to something already in the IA-spec — the **"sent-vs-draft mismatch banner"** ("You sent v[N] on [date] · current draft is v[N+1] · the customer is responding to v[N]"). That banner exists precisely for this revise-and-re-send world. So the reversible model doesn't just fit the schema — there's already *design* anticipating it. The old Send-lock was arguably contradicting design intent that was already there.

### Round 2 (REVERSIBILITY MODEL REVISION — Edward, 2026-07-27) — THIS PATCH
**Core insight: the immutability lock was on the wrong event.** Send to Client only means "the customer received a PDF" — no irreversible SYSTEM action occurs. The truly irreversible act is the **NetSuite SO push at Complete**. So:

- **The lock moves from Send → Complete.** Nothing is immutable until the NetSuite SO is created.
- **Send to Client, Client Review, Mark Accepted are ALL REVERSIBLE.** A sent quote can return to draft, be revised in-place, and re-sent.
- **Catch G (Send de-facto irreversible) is REMOVED.** No duplicate-to-revise workaround; no lost-context problem. Revisions happen IN-PLACE on the live quote — notes, associations, cost data, specs, and the Client Review feed all stay intact.
- **NEW: Client Review is a 5th Quote sub-tab** (between Send to Client and Mark Accepted) — a lightweight timestamped activity feed logging customer responses / questions / revision requests. Its "revision requested" entry is answered by revising the live quote in place.
- **Pattern 52 immutability relocates from Send → `complete`.**
- **Revise-and-re-send uses the EXISTING versioning machinery:** same quote number, incrementing `version_number`, each send writes a NEW versioned sent-snapshot (all retained). The already-designed "sent-vs-draft mismatch banner" (IA-spec) surfaces when a draft revision exists against a sent version.
- **New schema:** `quote_review_events` feed table (net-new; Architect §0.5 round 2).

Rationale: the commitment is the NetSuite order, not the emailed PDF. This matches operational reality, uses the versioning machinery already in the schema (`version_number`, `superseded`, `copied_from_quote_id`), and matches design intent already drafted (the mismatch banner). It is SIMPLER than the Send-lock model — it removes Catch G, the duplicate-completeness problem, and the unlock-sent-quote special case.

---

## 1. Background & context
The post-pricing workflow has been operationally messy. PMs build a quote (Setup → Costs → Pricing) then enter an undifferentiated execute phase where the IA doesn't reflect operational reality. The execute phase has discrete lifecycle moments — preview, send, customer review/revision, accept, tier-commit, NetSuite handoff — that share one undifferentiated surface today.

Operational facts driving the restructure:
1. **Customer picks one tier ~95% of the time.** NetSuite SO needs ONE tier's data; there's no explicit "which tier" capture today.
2. **HubSpot deal stage push at acceptance; NetSuite SO push at tier commit** — different events at different times.
3. **The customer-acceptance lifecycle has discrete phases** — send, review/revise, accept, tier-select, advance-to-NetSuite — that the IA didn't reflect.
4. **(v2) Revision is a normal part of the loop, not an exception.** Customers respond, ask questions, request changes. The PM revises and re-sends. This must be a first-class tracked workflow, not a manual out-of-band activity.

## 2. The problem — operational risk
**Symptom 1: Tier ambiguity at NetSuite push.** No explicit record of WHICH tier the customer is buying.
**Symptom 2: HubSpot/NetSuite event conflation.** Prior scope pushed both at acceptance; they're different decisions (deal-won vs operational kickoff).
**Symptom 3: Workflow surface invisibility.** Between send and accept, no surface says "this quote is sent; awaiting customer" — and no surface tracks the review/revision dialogue. **Client Review (v2) fills this.**
**Symptom 4: Reversibility was mis-modeled.** The original brief made Mark Accepted (then Send) the lock point. **v2 correction:** the only irreversible act is the NetSuite SO push at Complete. Everything before it is a proposal and must be revisable. Locking earlier forces lossy duplicate-and-clone workarounds; locking at Complete lets PMs revise in-place with full context.

## 3. The decision — scope and canon impact
**v1 ships the Quote umbrella + lifecycle finalization as a single comprehensive slice.** No X/Y split.

**Canon impact** (canon revision already landed):
- **4 peer top-level surfaces:** Setup · Costs · Pricing · Quote
- **Quote umbrella has 5 sub-tabs** (v2): Preview Quote · Send to Client · **Client Review** · Mark Accepted · Tier Selection
- Operations dissolves to future orchestration wrapper (post-v1)
- Mark Accepted dissolves from peer surface into a Quote sub-tab

**Scope IN — re-house / net-new split:**

*Re-housing (Slice 11 shipped it; move into sub-tab IA + wire Advance):*
- Preview Quote: lift shipped PDF preview into sub-tab context
- Send to Client: shipped `sendQuote` (status flip + snapshot fleet + quote_number + pdf_url + audit + prepared-by + unlinked-deal guard #124) behind the Send Advance
- Snapshot mechanism: shipped (pdf_url pointer + snapshot columns) — no new snapshot infra; **v2 extends it to per-version retention (see §5)**

*Genuinely net-new:*
- 5-sub-tab IA + Advance/navigation scaffolding
- Post-send waiting-state UI on Send to Client
- Version-selection UI in Preview Quote
- **Client Review sub-tab: activity-feed UI + `quote_review_events` table (v2)**
- **Revise-in-place action** (return a sent quote to editable draft; re-send as new version) (v2)
- Mark Accepted accept write-path (shell today — nothing writes accept columns)
- Tier Selection sub-tab UX (PM-proxy tier capture)
- State enum extension (add ONLY `complete`)
- Finalization warning at Tier Selection Advance
- HubSpot deal stage push at Mark Accepted Advance
- NetSuite SO push at Tier Selection Advance
- Pricing "Send to customer" CTA → Quote > Preview Quote

**Scope OUT:**
- Operations wrapper / BOM / packing / freight (post-v1)
- `lifecycle_events` table (Operations slice; v1 uses `audit_log`)
- Customer self-serve tier selection / acceptance (v2)
- **Post-Complete** changes / versioning-after-lock workflow (v1.5+; Complete is the terminal lock)
- Multi-tier orders (v2)
- HubSpot inbound webhook / NetSuite inbound reconciliation (v2)
- **Client Review depth:** v1 is a LOGGED ACTIVITY FEED only (responded / asked / revision-requested). NOT a revision-management engine, NOT customer-facing, NOT threaded messaging. The feed logs; the revise-in-place action responds.

## 4. Solution architecture
### 4.1 Quote umbrella IA — 5 sub-tabs (v2)
Quote is a peer top-level surface (4th of 4). Internally, five sequential sub-tabs:

| Sub-tab | Purpose | Entry state | Advance / action |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Preview Quote** | Internal review before send — PDF preview (re-housed), version selection | `draft` (Preview-ready = runtime `draft AND gates_pass`, not an enum value) | Navigate to Send to Client |
| **Send to Client** | Send action (re-housed `sendQuote`) + post-send waiting state | `draft` + gates pass | `sendQuote` fires; status → `sent`; writes a versioned snapshot. **REVERSIBLE** |
| **Client Review** (NEW v2) | Lightweight activity feed: log customer responses / questions / revision requests | `sent` (feed lives WITHIN `sent` — no new enum state) | No status transition. Affordances: **+ log entry**; **Revise** (→ draft for in-place revision); **Mark Accepted →** |
| **Mark Accepted** | Record customer acceptance (PM proxy) — new write-path | `sent` | Status → `accepted`; **HubSpot push → "Closed Won"**. **REVERSIBLE (Q7 rollback)** |
| **Tier Selection** | Capture chosen tier + finalize | `accepted` | Writes `accepted_tier_id`; status → `complete`; **NetSuite SO push (Pending Fulfillment)**; finalization warning. **IRREVERSIBLE — THE LOCK POINT** |

**Reversibility model (v2):** Nothing is immutable until **Complete** (NetSuite push). Send / Client Review / Mark Accepted are all reversible. Only Tier Selection Advance → `complete` locks (Pattern 52).

### 4.2 Advance / action mechanism
Each transition sub-tab has an Advance button. Click:
1. Pre-advance validation (§4.5)
2. Confirmation dialog for the COMMITTING transition — **Tier Selection Advance only** (finalization warning; it's the sole irreversible act). Send no longer needs an irreversibility warning (it's reversible now), though a light "customer will receive this" confirm is fine.
3. Server action fires (state transition + external integration if applicable)
4. Audit: distinct action — `quote_sent` (existing) / `quote_accepted` / `quote_completed` / `quote_reverted` / **`quote_revised`** (v2). `diff_json` carries `from_state`/`to_state`.
5. UI advances on success

**Reversibility per transition (v2):**
- Preview → Send: reversible (pre-send)
- **Send → (sent): REVERSIBLE.** A sent quote can be revised in-place via the **Revise action** (§4.3a): returns to `draft`, PM edits, re-sends as a new version (same quote number, `version_number`++, prior sent-snapshot retained). `quote_revised` audit. The sent-vs-draft mismatch banner surfaces while a draft revision exists.
- **Mark Accepted → (accepted): REVERSIBLE** via explicit Q7 rollback (reverses HubSpot stage push, status → `sent`, `quote_reverted` audit).
- **Tier Selection → Complete: NOT reversible** without admin override. NetSuite SO fires; Pattern 52 locks all snapshot/accept/netsuite columns. Post-Complete reversal = admin approval + SO deletion + new version (v1.5+).

### 4.3 Client Review sub-tab (NEW v2)
A lightweight, PM-facing **activity feed** for the post-send review window. Lives within the `sent` state (no enum change).

- **Feed:** append-only, timestamped entries. Each entry: `event_type` (responded / asked / revision_requested — extensible), free-text note, author, timestamp.
- **Add-entry affordance:** PM logs an entry (event-type picker + note).
- **Empty state:** "No customer activity logged yet."
- **Not customer-facing, not threaded, not messaging** — it's the PM's log of what's happening with the customer on this quote.
- **Revise affordance** (see §4.3a): a "revision_requested" entry naturally pairs with the Revise action.

### 4.3a Revise-in-place action (NEW v2)
The response to a revision request. On a `sent` (or `accepted`, pre-Complete) quote:
- **Revise** returns the quote to `draft` (editable), preserving ALL context — notes, associations, cost/spec data, tiers, the Client Review feed — because it's the SAME quote, not a copy. **No data loss** (this is the whole point of moving the lock to Complete).
- The prior sent version's snapshot is RETAINED (versioned).
- PM edits, then re-sends → new `version_number`, same quote number, new sent-snapshot.
- `quote_revised` audit; sent-vs-draft mismatch banner active while the draft leads the last-sent version.
- If the quote was `accepted` when revised, reverting to draft also rolls back the HubSpot stage (same mechanism as Q7).

### 4.4 Tier Selection sub-tab UX
- Read-only per-tier compliance summary (reused)
- Single-select radio/dropdown: which tier did the customer pick?
- **Default: ★ recommended tier, pre-filled from `customer_accepted_tier_id` if present** — PM can override
- Validation: tier selected before Advance; below-floor blocks (admin override path)
- Finalization warning preview before final Advance
- Persists to `quotes.accepted_tier_id` (reused column). `quote_completed` audit.

### 4.5 State enum + guards (v2)
**Actual enum:** `draft | sent | accepted | superseded | lost`. **Add ONLY `complete`** → 6 values. `preview_ready` NOT added (runtime-derived). `client_review` NOT added (Client Review is a feed within `sent`).

**`quote-guards.ts` (v2):**
- `complete` is terminal + non-editable (Pattern 52).
- **`sent` and `accepted` are now REVERSIBLE to `draft`** via Revise — guards must ALLOW the sent→draft and accepted→draft transitions (previously would have been blocked). This is the load-bearing guard change for v2. `requireDraft` for edits still holds (revise returns to draft FIRST, then edits are allowed).
- Only `complete` (and existing `superseded`/`lost`) are non-revisable.

### 4.5b Pre-advance validation guards
- **Preview → Send:** SKUs complete, cost rows populated, no below-floor, PDF renders.
- **Send → Mark Accepted (via Client Review):** send completed; quote in `sent`.
- **Mark Accepted → Tier Selection:** quote `accepted`; HubSpot push succeeded.
- **Tier Selection → Complete:** `accepted_tier_id` set; not below floor; finalization confirmed; `projects.hubspot_deal_id` present; NetSuite payload validates.

### 4.6 HubSpot deal stage push (Mark Accepted Advance)
- Maps from **`projects.hubspot_deal_id`** (not `quotes`).
- **Target: "Closed Won"** (Q4). `firm_settings.hubspot_deal_stage_on_accept`.
- **ONE push** — Closed Won at Accept; Complete does NOT move the stage again (§7.2). No `_on_complete`.
- Reversible: if the quote is reverted from `accepted` (Q7 rollback or Revise), the HubSpot stage rolls back.
- Audit `quote_accepted` + response code. Failure: surface, retry, don't advance until success.
- `HUBSPOT_WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN`; `getWriteClient()` — first production invocation.

### 4.7 NetSuite SO push (Tier Selection Advance) — THE LOCK
- **Header:** customer ID (from project's HubSpot deal), terms (FOB Long Beach, 50/50, 8-12wk, 30-day validity).
- **Lines:** selected tier's SKUs at that tier's qty + sell-per-unit, **from the Slice-11.5 ASY/LEAF adapter** (not `quote_skus`). Assembly structure preserved.
- **Notes:** Nexus quote-number (`DPS-1000+` = Nexus prefix, not the SO ID) + URL back.
- **Status on create: "Pending Fulfillment"** (Q5). `firm_settings.netsuite_so_status_on_create`.
- SO ID → `quotes.netsuite_so_id`; timestamp → `quotes.netsuite_pushed_at`. Post-push confirmation UI shows SO ID + link.
- **This is the irreversible commit** — Pattern 52 locks here. Failure: surface, retry, don't advance to `complete` until success. Idempotency (Q6) prevents duplicate SOs.
- Open (catch D / discovery): does HubSpot→NetSuite sync carry assembly metadata or only leaves? Shapes nested-vs-flattened line push. Disposition at impl planning.

## 5. Schema verification gate (Pattern 25) — v2
**Schema changes:**
1. `quotes.status`: add ONLY `complete`. 6-value enum.
2. **DO NOT add `selected_tier_id`** — reuse `accepted_tier_id`, default from `customer_accepted_tier_id`.
3. `quotes.netsuite_so_id` (varchar(50), nullable) + `quotes.netsuite_pushed_at` (timestamptz, nullable). Net-new.
4. `firm_settings.hubspot_deal_stage_on_accept` (default "Closed Won") + `firm_settings.netsuite_so_status_on_create` (default "Pending Fulfillment"). NO `_on_complete`.
5. **NEW (v2): `quote_review_events` table** — the Client Review feed. Proposed shape (Architect confirms): `id` PK, `quote_id` FK, `version_number` (which sent version the entry pertains to), `event_type` enum (`responded`|`asked`|`revision_requested`|…extensible), `note` text, `created_by_user_id` FK, `created_at` timestamptz. Append-only.

**Snapshot behavior (v2):** each send writes a versioned sent-snapshot; ALL retained (same quote number, `version_number`++). This uses existing `version_number` machinery. The Slice-11 snapshot fleet captures per-version. Rationale: a customer may accept an earlier sent version — the record of each version they received must persist.

**HARD GATE (Architect §6):** new `firm_settings` columns MUST join `versionedFirmSettingsUpdate` (silent-null-on-margin-edit bug otherwise).

**FK cascade:** `accepted_tier_id` tighten SET NULL → RESTRICT.

**Audit actions:** `quote_accepted` / `quote_completed` / `quote_reverted` / **`quote_revised`** (v2). Not generic `quote_advanced`.

**Pattern 52 (v2 — RELOCATED):** immutability freezes at **`complete`**, NOT at send. Frozen on complete: `pdf_url`, snapshot fleet, `accepted_*`, `customer_accepted_*`, `netsuite_*`, and the `quote_review_events` feed. Before `complete`, the quote (and its feed) remain mutable via Revise.

### 5.1 SECOND Architect §0.5 pass required (v2)
The v2 changes introduce NEW verification surface beyond round 1. Architect must verify:
- **`quote_review_events`** table shape + FK semantics + append-only enforcement + audit interaction.
- **Reversibility guards:** `sent → draft` and `accepted → draft` transitions in `quote-guards.ts` — confirm they don't break the 7 `requireDraft` callers or the versioning/superseded machinery.
- **Pattern 52 relocation** from send → `complete` — confirm nothing in Slice 11 relied on send-time immutability that this loosens (e.g., does anything assume a `sent` quote's snapshot is frozen? Slice 11's snapshot is per-send, so re-sending writes a new one — confirm no overwrite/loss of prior versions).
- **Versioned snapshot retention** — confirm `version_number` + snapshot columns support multiple retained sent-snapshots per quote (same number), and that the sent-vs-draft mismatch banner logic reads them correctly.
- **Quote-number continuity** on revise+re-send (same number, new version).

## 6. Workflow scenarios (v2)
**Happy path (no revision):**
1. Build (Setup/Costs/Pricing) → Pricing clean → "Send to customer" → Quote > Preview
2. Preview → Advance → Send to Client
3. Send Advance → `sendQuote`; status `sent`; v1 snapshot written
4. Client Review: PM logs "customer responded — approved" (optional)
5. Advance → Mark Accepted; status `accepted`; HubSpot → Closed Won
6. Customer picks T2 → Tier Selection (T2 pre-filled) → finalization warning → confirm
7. NetSuite SO push (Pending Fulfillment); status `complete`; SO ID shown; **quote locks (Pattern 52)**

**Revision path (v2 — the new normal):**
1–3. As above; quote is `sent` (v1 snapshot)
4. Client Review: PM logs "revision_requested — customer wants Tier 2 qty at 12k"
5. PM clicks **Revise** → quote returns to `draft`, ALL context intact (notes, feed, cost data)
6. PM edits (adjusts the tier), re-sends → status `sent` again, v2 snapshot written (same quote number, version 2); v1 snapshot retained; mismatch banner clears
7. Continue to accept/tier-select/complete as normal — OR revise again if needed

**Edge cases:**
- **Customer accepts an earlier version.** Both sent-snapshots retained; PM references the accepted version; mismatch banner shows which version leads.
- **Tier below floor at Tier Selection.** Advance blocked; admin override or different tier.
- **HubSpot/NetSuite push failure.** Surface, retry; don't advance until success.
- **NetSuite idempotency.** External ID `quote_id + quote_version` — retry returns original SO.
- **Revert after accept.** Q7 rollback (or Revise from accepted) → HubSpot stage rolls back → `sent`/`draft`.
- **Post-Complete change.** Admin override (v1.5+): SO deletion + new version. Out of v1 scope — Complete is the hard lock.

**Pattern 47:** Tier Selection radio/dropdown + Client Review add-entry input are controlled inputs (optimistic, debounced, wait-for-quiet). Sub-tab nav respects focus stability.

## 7. Discovery questions — DISPOSITIONED
| Q | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Q1 sub-tab order | Strict sequential (now 5 sub-tabs) |
| Q2 finalization copy | Strong, action-specific (Tier Selection Advance only — the sole lock) |
| Q3 tier default | Recommended ★, pre-filled from `customer_accepted_tier_id` |
| Q4 HubSpot stage on accept | ✅ "Closed Won" → `firm_settings.hubspot_deal_stage_on_accept` |
| Q5 NetSuite SO status | ✅ "Pending Fulfillment" → `firm_settings.netsuite_so_status_on_create` |

| Q7 Mark-Accepted reversibility | Explicit rollback button → `sent`, HubSpot rollback, `quote_reverted` |
| §7.2 Complete → HubSpot? | ✅ ONE push (Closed Won at Accept only); no `_on_complete` |
| **Catch G (v2 REVERSED)** | ✅ **Send is REVERSIBLE.** Lock moves to Complete. Revise-in-place; no duplicate/clone. |
| **Client Review (v2 NEW)** | ✅ 5th sub-tab between Send and Mark Accepted; lightweight logged activity feed |
| **Revise (v2 NEW)** | ✅ In-place revision returning sent/accepted quote to draft; same number, new version, retained snapshots |

- **The lock moves from Send → Complete.** Nothing is immutable until the NetSuite SO is created.
- **Send to Client, Client Review, Mark Accepted are ALL REVERSIBLE.** A sent quote can return to draft, be revised in-place, and re-sent.
- **Catch G (Send de-facto irreversible) is REMOVED.** No duplicate-to-revise workaround; no lost-context problem. Revisions happen IN-PLACE on the live quote — notes, associations, cost data, specs, and the Client Review feed all stay intact.
- **NEW: Client Review is a 5th Quote sub-tab** (between Send to Client and Mark Accepted) — a lightweight timestamped activity feed logging customer responses / questions / revision requests. Its "revision requested" entry is answered by revising the live quote in place.
- **Pattern 52 immutability relocates from Send → `complete`.**
- **Revise-and-re-send uses the EXISTING versioning machinery:** same quote number, incrementing `version_number`, each send writes a NEW versioned sent-snapshot (all retained). The already-designed "sent-vs-draft mismatch banner" (IA-spec) surfaces when a draft revision exists against a sent version.
- **New schema:** `quote_review_events` feed table (net-new; Architect §0.5 round 2).

Rationale: the commitment is the NetSuite order, not the emailed PDF. This matches operational reality, uses the versioning machinery already in the schema (`version_number`, `superseded`, `copied_from_quote_id`), and matches design intent already drafted (the mismatch banner). It is SIMPLER than the Send-lock model — it removes Catch G, the duplicate-completeness problem, and the unlock-sent-quote special case.

---

## 1. Background & context
The post-pricing workflow has been operationally messy. PMs build a quote (Setup → Costs → Pricing) then enter an undifferentiated execute phase where the IA doesn't reflect operational reality. The execute phase has discrete lifecycle moments — preview, send, customer review/revision, accept, tier-commit, NetSuite handoff — that share one undifferentiated surface today.

Operational facts driving the restructure:
1. **Customer picks one tier ~95% of the time.** NetSuite SO needs ONE tier's data; there's no explicit "which tier" capture today.
2. **HubSpot deal stage push at acceptance; NetSuite SO push at tier commit** — different events at different times.
3. **The customer-acceptance lifecycle has discrete phases** — send, review/revise, accept, tier-select, advance-to-NetSuite — that the IA didn't reflect.
4. **(v2) Revision is a normal part of the loop, not an exception.** Customers respond, ask questions, request changes. The PM revises and re-sends. This must be a first-class tracked workflow, not a manual out-of-band activity.

## 2. The problem — operational risk
**Symptom 1: Tier ambiguity at NetSuite push.** No explicit record of WHICH tier the customer is buying.
**Symptom 2: HubSpot/NetSuite event conflation.** Prior scope pushed both at acceptance; they're different decisions (deal-won vs operational kickoff).
**Symptom 3: Workflow surface invisibility.** Between send and accept, no surface says "this quote is sent; awaiting customer" — and no surface tracks the review/revision dialogue. **Client Review (v2) fills this.**
**Symptom 4: Reversibility was mis-modeled.** The original brief made Mark Accepted (then Send) the lock point. **v2 correction:** the only irreversible act is the NetSuite SO push at Complete. Everything before it is a proposal and must be revisable. Locking earlier forces lossy duplicate-and-clone workarounds; locking at Complete lets PMs revise in-place with full context.

## 3. The decision — scope and canon impact
**v1 ships the Quote umbrella + lifecycle finalization as a single comprehensive slice.** No X/Y split.

**Canon impact** (canon revision already landed):
- **4 peer top-level surfaces:** Setup · Costs · Pricing · Quote
- **Quote umbrella has 5 sub-tabs** (v2): Preview Quote · Send to Client · **Client Review** · Mark Accepted · Tier Selection
- Operations dissolves to future orchestration wrapper (post-v1)
- Mark Accepted dissolves from peer surface into a Quote sub-tab

**Scope IN — re-house / net-new split:**

*Re-housing (Slice 11 shipped it; move into sub-tab IA + wire Advance):*
- Preview Quote: lift shipped PDF preview into sub-tab context
- Send to Client: shipped `sendQuote` (status flip + snapshot fleet + quote_number + pdf_url + audit + prepared-by + unlinked-deal guard #124) behind the Send Advance
- Snapshot mechanism: shipped (pdf_url pointer + snapshot columns) — no new snapshot infra; **v2 extends it to per-version retention (see §5)**

*Genuinely net-new:*
- 5-sub-tab IA + Advance/navigation scaffolding
- Post-send waiting-state UI on Send to Client
- Version-selection UI in Preview Quote
- **Client Review sub-tab: activity-feed UI + `quote_review_events` table (v2)**
- **Revise-in-place action** (return a sent quote to editable draft; re-send as new version) (v2)
- Mark Accepted accept write-path (shell today — nothing writes accept columns)
- Tier Selection sub-tab UX (PM-proxy tier capture)
- State enum extension (add ONLY `complete`)
- Finalization warning at Tier Selection Advance
- HubSpot deal stage push at Mark Accepted Advance
- NetSuite SO push at Tier Selection Advance
- Pricing "Send to customer" CTA → Quote > Preview Quote

**Scope OUT:**
- Operations wrapper / BOM / packing / freight (post-v1)
- `lifecycle_events` table (Operations slice; v1 uses `audit_log`)
- Customer self-serve tier selection / acceptance (v2)
- **Post-Complete** changes / versioning-after-lock workflow (v1.5+; Complete is the terminal lock)
- Multi-tier orders (v2)
- HubSpot inbound webhook / NetSuite inbound reconciliation (v2)
- **Client Review depth:** v1 is a LOGGED ACTIVITY FEED only (responded / asked / revision-requested). NOT a revision-management engine, NOT customer-facing, NOT threaded messaging. The feed logs; the revise-in-place action responds.

## 4. Solution architecture
### 4.1 Quote umbrella IA — 5 sub-tabs (v2)
Quote is a peer top-level surface (4th of 4). Internally, five sequential sub-tabs:

| Sub-tab | Purpose | Entry state | Advance / action |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Preview Quote** | Internal review before send — PDF preview (re-housed), version selection | `draft` (Preview-ready = runtime `draft AND gates_pass`, not an enum value) | Navigate to Send to Client |
| **Send to Client** | Send action (re-housed `sendQuote`) + post-send waiting state | `draft` + gates pass | `sendQuote` fires; status → `sent`; writes a versioned snapshot. **REVERSIBLE** |
| **Client Review** (NEW v2) | Lightweight activity feed: log customer responses / questions / revision requests | `sent` (feed lives WITHIN `sent` — no new enum state) | No status transition. Affordances: **+ log entry**; **Revise** (→ draft for in-place revision); **Mark Accepted →** |
| **Mark Accepted** | Record customer acceptance (PM proxy) — new write-path | `sent` | Status → `accepted`; **HubSpot push → "Closed Won"**. **REVERSIBLE (Q7 rollback)** |
| **Tier Selection** | Capture chosen tier + finalize | `accepted` | Writes `accepted_tier_id`; status → `complete`; **NetSuite SO push (Pending Fulfillment)**; finalization warning. **IRREVERSIBLE — THE LOCK POINT** |

**Reversibility model (v2):** Nothing is immutable until **Complete** (NetSuite push). Send / Client Review / Mark Accepted are all reversible. Only Tier Selection Advance → `complete` locks (Pattern 52).

### 4.2 Advance / action mechanism
Each transition sub-tab has an Advance button. Click:
1. Pre-advance validation (§4.5)
2. Confirmation dialog for the COMMITTING transition — **Tier Selection Advance only** (finalization warning; it's the sole irreversible act). Send no longer needs an irreversibility warning (it's reversible now), though a light "customer will receive this" confirm is fine.
3. Server action fires (state transition + external integration if applicable)
4. Audit: distinct action — `quote_sent` (existing) / `quote_accepted` / `quote_completed` / `quote_reverted` / **`quote_revised`** (v2). `diff_json` carries `from_state`/`to_state`.
5. UI advances on success

**Reversibility per transition (v2):**
- Preview → Send: reversible (pre-send)
- **Send → (sent): REVERSIBLE.** A sent quote can be revised in-place via the **Revise action** (§4.3a): returns to `draft`, PM edits, re-sends as a new version (same quote number, `version_number`++, prior sent-snapshot retained). `quote_revised` audit. The sent-vs-draft mismatch banner surfaces while a draft revision exists.
- **Mark Accepted → (accepted): REVERSIBLE** via explicit Q7 rollback (reverses HubSpot stage push, status → `sent`, `quote_reverted` audit).
- **Tier Selection → Complete: NOT reversible** without admin override. NetSuite SO fires; Pattern 52 locks all snapshot/accept/netsuite columns. Post-Complete reversal = admin approval + SO deletion + new version (v1.5+).

### 4.3 Client Review sub-tab (NEW v2)
A lightweight, PM-facing **activity feed** for the post-send review window. Lives within the `sent` state (no enum change).

- **Feed:** append-only, timestamped entries. Each entry: `event_type` (responded / asked / revision_requested — extensible), free-text note, author, timestamp.
- **Add-entry affordance:** PM logs an entry (event-type picker + note).
- **Empty state:** "No customer activity logged yet."
- **Not customer-facing, not threaded, not messaging** — it's the PM's log of what's happening with the customer on this quote.
- **Revise affordance** (see §4.3a): a "revision_requested" entry naturally pairs with the Revise action.

### 4.3a Revise-in-place action (NEW v2)
The response to a revision request. On a `sent` (or `accepted`, pre-Complete) quote:
- **Revise** returns the quote to `draft` (editable), preserving ALL context — notes, associations, cost/spec data, tiers, the Client Review feed — because it's the SAME quote, not a copy. **No data loss** (this is the whole point of moving the lock to Complete).
- The prior sent version's snapshot is RETAINED (versioned).
- PM edits, then re-sends → new `version_number`, same quote number, new sent-snapshot.
- `quote_revised` audit; sent-vs-draft mismatch banner active while the draft leads the last-sent version.
- If the quote was `accepted` when revised, reverting to draft also rolls back the HubSpot stage (same mechanism as Q7).

### 4.4 Tier Selection sub-tab UX
- Read-only per-tier compliance summary (reused)
- Single-select radio/dropdown: which tier did the customer pick?
- **Default: ★ recommended tier, pre-filled from `customer_accepted_tier_id` if present** — PM can override
- Validation: tier selected before Advance; below-floor blocks (admin override path)
- Finalization warning preview before final Advance
- Persists to `quotes.accepted_tier_id` (reused column). `quote_completed` audit.

### 4.5 State enum + guards (v2)
**Actual enum:** `draft | sent | accepted | superseded | lost`. **Add ONLY `complete`** → 6 values. `preview_ready` NOT added (runtime-derived). `client_review` NOT added (Client Review is a feed within `sent`).

**`quote-guards.ts` (v2):**
- `complete` is terminal + non-editable (Pattern 52).
- **`sent` and `accepted` are now REVERSIBLE to `draft`** via Revise — guards must ALLOW the sent→draft and accepted→draft transitions (previously would have been blocked). This is the load-bearing guard change for v2. `requireDraft` for edits still holds (revise returns to draft FIRST, then edits are allowed).
- Only `complete` (and existing `superseded`/`lost`) are non-revisable.

### 4.5b Pre-advance validation guards
- **Preview → Send:** SKUs complete, cost rows populated, no below-floor, PDF renders.
- **Send → Mark Accepted (via Client Review):** send completed; quote in `sent`.
- **Mark Accepted → Tier Selection:** quote `accepted`; HubSpot push succeeded.
- **Tier Selection → Complete:** `accepted_tier_id` set; not below floor; finalization confirmed; `projects.hubspot_deal_id` present; NetSuite payload validates.

### 4.6 HubSpot deal stage push (Mark Accepted Advance)
- Maps from **`projects.hubspot_deal_id`** (not `quotes`).
- **Target: "Closed Won"** (Q4). `firm_settings.hubspot_deal_stage_on_accept`.
- **ONE push** — Closed Won at Accept; Complete does NOT move the stage again (§7.2). No `_on_complete`.
- Reversible: if the quote is reverted from `accepted` (Q7 rollback or Revise), the HubSpot stage rolls back.
- Audit `quote_accepted` + response code. Failure: surface, retry, don't advance until success.
- `HUBSPOT_WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN`; `getWriteClient()` — first production invocation.

### 4.7 NetSuite SO push (Tier Selection Advance) — THE LOCK
- **Header:** customer ID (from project's HubSpot deal), terms (FOB Long Beach, 50/50, 8-12wk, 30-day validity).
- **Lines:** selected tier's SKUs at that tier's qty + sell-per-unit, **from the Slice-11.5 ASY/LEAF adapter** (not `quote_skus`). Assembly structure preserved.
- **Notes:** Nexus quote-number (`DPS-1000+` = Nexus prefix, not the SO ID) + URL back.
- **Status on create: "Pending Fulfillment"** (Q5). `firm_settings.netsuite_so_status_on_create`.
- SO ID → `quotes.netsuite_so_id`; timestamp → `quotes.netsuite_pushed_at`. Post-push confirmation UI shows SO ID + link.
- **This is the irreversible commit** — Pattern 52 locks here. Failure: surface, retry, don't advance to `complete` until success. Idempotency (Q6) prevents duplicate SOs.
- Open (catch D / discovery): does HubSpot→NetSuite sync carry assembly metadata or only leaves? Shapes nested-vs-flattened line push. Disposition at impl planning.

## 5. Schema verification gate (Pattern 25) — v2
**Schema changes:**
1. `quotes.status`: add ONLY `complete`. 6-value enum.
2. **DO NOT add `selected_tier_id`** — reuse `accepted_tier_id`, default from `customer_accepted_tier_id`.
3. `quotes.netsuite_so_id` (varchar(50), nullable) + `quotes.netsuite_pushed_at` (timestamptz, nullable). Net-new.
4. `firm_settings.hubspot_deal_stage_on_accept` (default "Closed Won") + `firm_settings.netsuite_so_status_on_create` (default "Pending Fulfillment"). NO `_on_complete`.
5. **NEW (v2): `quote_review_events` table** — the Client Review feed. Proposed shape (Architect confirms): `id` PK, `quote_id` FK, `version_number` (which sent version the entry pertains to), `event_type` enum (`responded`|`asked`|`revision_requested`|…extensible), `note` text, `created_by_user_id` FK, `created_at` timestamptz. Append-only.

**Snapshot behavior (v2):** each send writes a versioned sent-snapshot; ALL retained (same quote number, `version_number`++). This uses existing `version_number` machinery. The Slice-11 snapshot fleet captures per-version. Rationale: a customer may accept an earlier sent version — the record of each version they received must persist.

**HARD GATE (Architect §6):** new `firm_settings` columns MUST join `versionedFirmSettingsUpdate` (silent-null-on-margin-edit bug otherwise).

**FK cascade:** `accepted_tier_id` tighten SET NULL → RESTRICT.

**Audit actions:** `quote_accepted` / `quote_completed` / `quote_reverted` / **`quote_revised`** (v2). Not generic `quote_advanced`.

**Pattern 52 (v2 — RELOCATED):** immutability freezes at **`complete`**, NOT at send. Frozen on complete: `pdf_url`, snapshot fleet, `accepted_*`, `customer_accepted_*`, `netsuite_*`, and the `quote_review_events` feed. Before `complete`, the quote (and its feed) remain mutable via Revise.

### 5.1 SECOND Architect §0.5 pass required (v2)
The v2 changes introduce NEW verification surface beyond round 1. Architect must verify:
- **`quote_review_events`** table shape + FK semantics + append-only enforcement + audit interaction.
- **Reversibility guards:** `sent → draft` and `accepted → draft` transitions in `quote-guards.ts` — confirm they don't break the 7 `requireDraft` callers or the versioning/superseded machinery.
- **Pattern 52 relocation** from send → `complete` — confirm nothing in Slice 11 relied on send-time immutability that this loosens (e.g., does anything assume a `sent` quote's snapshot is frozen? Slice 11's snapshot is per-send, so re-sending writes a new one — confirm no overwrite/loss of prior versions).
- **Versioned snapshot retention** — confirm `version_number` + snapshot columns support multiple retained sent-snapshots per quote (same number), and that the sent-vs-draft mismatch banner logic reads them correctly.
- **Quote-number continuity** on revise+re-send (same number, new version).

## 6. Workflow scenarios (v2)
**Happy path (no revision):**
1. Build (Setup/Costs/Pricing) → Pricing clean → "Send to customer" → Quote > Preview
2. Preview → Advance → Send to Client
3. Send Advance → `sendQuote`; status `sent`; v1 snapshot written
4. Client Review: PM logs "customer responded — approved" (optional)
5. Advance → Mark Accepted; status `accepted`; HubSpot → Closed Won
6. Customer picks T2 → Tier Selection (T2 pre-filled) → finalization warning → confirm
7. NetSuite SO push (Pending Fulfillment); status `complete`; SO ID shown; **quote locks (Pattern 52)**

**Revision path (v2 — the new normal):**
1–3. As above; quote is `sent` (v1 snapshot)
4. Client Review: PM logs "revision_requested — customer wants Tier 2 qty at 12k"
5. PM clicks **Revise** → quote returns to `draft`, ALL context intact (notes, feed, cost data)
6. PM edits (adjusts the tier), re-sends → status `sent` again, v2 snapshot written (same quote number, version 2); v1 snapshot retained; mismatch banner clears
7. Continue to accept/tier-select/complete as normal — OR revise again if needed

**Edge cases:**
- **Customer accepts an earlier version.** Both sent-snapshots retained; PM references the accepted version; mismatch banner shows which version leads.
- **Tier below floor at Tier Selection.** Advance blocked; admin override or different tier.
- **HubSpot/NetSuite push failure.** Surface, retry; don't advance until success.
- **NetSuite idempotency.** External ID `quote_id + quote_version` — retry returns original SO.
- **Revert after accept.** Q7 rollback (or Revise from accepted) → HubSpot stage rolls back → `sent`/`draft`.
- **Post-Complete change.** Admin override (v1.5+): SO deletion + new version. Out of v1 scope — Complete is the hard lock.

**Pattern 47:** Tier Selection radio/dropdown + Client Review add-entry input are controlled inputs (optimistic, debounced, wait-for-quiet). Sub-tab nav respects focus stability.

# CD Design Brief — Quote umbrella (5-sub-tab reversible lifecycle) · R-round kickoff

**To:** CD
**From:** CA
**Re:** Design round for the Quote umbrella — 5 sub-tabs, reversible lifecycle, Client Review feed
**Status:** Kickoff. This round is a LIVE BLOCKER for Slice 12 CC implementation. Pattern 30 deliverables required in-repo before CC can build (nothing exists today — see §0).

---

## §0 · Why this round exists (read first)

Slice 12 (the Quote umbrella) is fully scoped and dispositioned — but the Pattern
30 design deliverables **do not exist in the repo.** `docs/design-prototypes/dist/`
has R7a (nav IA) and R7b (setup redesign) only; there is no Quote-umbrella round.
Design *thinking* happened; the deliverables (prototype HTML, unbundled canonical
CSS, designer notes, data-source map) were never produced.

**CC cannot build until they exist.** Without canonical CD source, CC builds from
CSS interpretation — the §6.b trap that cost 12+ polish-amendment commits. This
round produces the canonical deliverables that prevent that.

**Design against the reconciled brief** (`quote-umbrella-brief-RECONCILED-v2`),
not the original. The original was written pre-Slice-11 and pre-reversibility-
revision; several assumptions changed. Key deltas are inline below.

---

## §1 · What you're designing — the 5-sub-tab Quote umbrella

Quote is the 4th peer surface (Setup · Costs · Pricing · Quote). Inside it, a
**5-sub-tab lifecycle**, strictly sequential, most stages REVERSIBLE:

```
Preview Quote → Send to Client → Client Review → Mark Accepted → Tier Selection
   (draft)         (sent)          (sent/feed)      (accepted)      (→ complete)
   reversible      reversible      reversible       reversible      THE LOCK
```

**The single most important model fact: nothing is locked until the final step.**
The lock is the **NetSuite SO push at Tier Selection → Complete** — that's the only
irreversible act (an order enters the operational system). Everything before it is
a proposal that can be revised. Design the *weight* of each transition accordingly:
Tier Selection Advance is heavy/ceremonial (finalization warning); the others are
light (they're reversible).

---

## §2 · Sub-tab-by-sub-tab design scope

### 2.1 Sub-tab strip (the container)
- **5-wide strip** — active / inactive / locked / completed states per tab.
- Strict-sequential: a tab is reachable only when the quote is in its state.
- Completed-earlier tabs read as done-but-revisitable (they're reversible), EXCEPT
  after Complete (fully locked).
- Client Review is visually a **logging tab** (see 2.3) — distinct from the
  transition tabs around it. Consider a subtle treatment that signals "this is a
  place to track, not a gate to pass."
- Stacked / narrow-viewport variant required (Pattern 30 standard).

### 2.2 Preview Quote
- Lifts the **already-shipped** customer PDF preview into sub-tab context (Slice 11
  built this — you're framing it, not redesigning the PDF).
- **Version-selection UI** (NEW — no picker exists): when a quote has multiple
  versions (from revisions), the PM picks which to preview. Design the version
  chooser.
- Advance → Send to Client (light; reversible).

### 2.3 Send to Client
- The send action (re-housed `sendQuote` — shipped). Design the **Send Advance**
  affordance + a **post-send waiting state** (NEW — "sent, awaiting customer" —
  there's no such surface today; this is a core gap this round fills).
- Send is **reversible** — no heavy irreversibility warning. A light "the customer
  will receive this PDF" confirm is appropriate; NOT a finalization-grade warning.

### 2.4 Client Review (NEW — the new sub-tab)
A lightweight, PM-facing **activity feed** for the post-send review window. Lives
within the `sent` state.
- **Feed:** append-only, timestamped entries. Each entry = an **event-type**
  (responded / asked / revision_requested — extensible), a free-text note, author,
  timestamp. Design the feed list + the add-entry affordance + event-type picker.
- **Empty state:** "No customer activity logged yet."
- **NOT** customer-facing, **NOT** threaded messaging, **NOT** a revision-manager.
  It's the PM's log. Keep it visually a *log*, not a *form-heavy surface*.
- Pairs with the **Revise** affordance (2.4a) — a "revision_requested" entry
  naturally sits next to a "Revise this quote" action.

### 2.4a Revise affordance + sent-vs-draft mismatch banner (NEW)
The response to a revision request — the piece that makes reversibility real:
- **Revise** returns the sent quote to editable draft, **preserving ALL context**
  (it's the same quote, not a copy — notes, associations, cost data, the feed all
  stay). Design the Revise entry point (likely in Client Review, near a
  revision_requested entry, and/or on the Preview/Send tabs).
- **Sent-vs-draft mismatch banner** (design intent already exists in the IA-spec —
  honor it): shows when a draft revision leads a sent version. Copy pattern: "You
  sent v[N] on [date] · current draft is v[N+1] · the customer is responding to
  v[N]." Design this banner + its affordances (view sent version, etc.).
- Same quote number across versions (customer sees "revised quote DPS-XXXX"),
  incrementing version.

### 2.5 Mark Accepted
- Records customer acceptance (PM proxy). Design the acceptance-recording action +
  the **HubSpot push state** (pushing → Closed Won → confirmed/error).
- **Reversible** — design the explicit **"Roll back to Send to Client"** affordance
  (reverses the HubSpot stage; returns to `sent`).
- (Existing Mark-Accepted peer-surface design in the IA-spec is a strong reference —
  the gates/verdict/tier-selection panels — but this now lives as a sub-tab, and
  tier selection has moved to its own sub-tab. Reconcile.)

### 2.6 Tier Selection — THE LOCK
- Read-only per-tier compliance summary (reuse the Pricing per-tier block).
- Single-select tier control (radio/dropdown), **default ★ recommended tier,
  pre-filled from the customer's recorded signal**, PM can override.
- **Finalization warning** (heavy, ceremonial — this is the irreversible act):
  design the warning modal. Copy is action-specific: names the NetSuite SO push +
  irreversibility. e.g. "Advancing pushes a NetSuite Sales Order (Pending
  Fulfillment). This finalizes the quote — no further changes without admin
  approval. Confirm?"
- **Post-push confirmation state:** NetSuite SO ID + link to NetSuite.
- Below-floor tier → blocked Advance + admin-override path (R5 firm-policy-gate
  pattern reference).

---

## §3 · Cross-cutting design requirements

- **Advance button treatment varies by weight:** light on the reversible
  transitions (Preview/Send/Mark-Accepted), **heavy/ceremonial ONLY on Tier
  Selection** (the lock). This visual asymmetry teaches the model — reversible
  steps feel light, the irreversible one feels weighty.
- **Error states:** HubSpot push failure (Mark Accepted), NetSuite push failure
  (Tier Selection) — design the surface + retry affordance. State does NOT advance
  on failure.
- **Locked (post-Complete) state:** once complete, the whole umbrella is read-only
  (Pattern 52). Design the locked/completed treatment — SO ID, "canonical record,"
  no edit affordances.
- **Reuse, don't reinvent:** the per-tier compliance block (Pricing), the PDF
  preview (Slice 11), the mismatch-banner intent (IA-spec) all exist. Frame and
  integrate them; don't redesign.

---

## §4 · Pattern 30 deliverables (what this round must produce)

Per standing Pattern 30 shape, committed to `docs/design-prototypes/dist/` (+
`/docs/` subfolder) per the R7b precedent:

1. **Prototype HTML** — the 5-sub-tab umbrella, all sub-tabs, all states
   (active/locked/error/empty/completed), the feed, the banners, the modals.
2. **Unbundled canonical CSS** — the stylesheet CC adopts verbatim (this is the
   artifact that prevents CSS-interpretation drift).
3. **Designer notes** — rationale, state logic, interaction behavior, the
   reversibility model's visual language.
4. **Data-source map** — each UI element → its data source (existing/new), so CC
   wires against real fields. Flag the NEW ones: `quote_review_events` (feed),
   `netsuite_so_id`, version chain, mismatch-banner derivation.
5. **Stacked / narrow-viewport variant.**

---

## §5 · What's locked (design AGAINST these — don't reopen)

- **5 sub-tabs**, strict sequential, order fixed (Preview · Send · Client Review ·
  Mark Accepted · Tier Selection).
- **Lock at Complete only** (NetSuite push). Everything before is reversible.
- **Client Review = lightweight logged feed** (not messaging, not revision-mgmt).
- **Revise = in-place**, same quote, same number, incrementing version, retained
  snapshots.
- **HubSpot push = Closed Won at Accept (one push).** NetSuite = Pending
  Fulfillment at Complete.
- **Mark Accepted reversible** (rollback button); **Tier Selection irreversible**
  (finalization warning).

These are dispositioned (Edward + Architect). Pushback on *design execution* is
welcome (per standing pushback workflow); pushback that reopens these settled
decisions should route to CA/Edward first, not get designed around.

---

## §6 · Sequencing + what unblocks after

1. **This round runs** → Pattern 30 deliverables land in repo.
2. In parallel: **Architect §0.5 round 2** verifies the v2 schema surface (feed
   table, reversibility guards, Pattern 52 relocation) — independent of design.
3. Both clear → **CC Phase 3 kicks off** from the reconciled brief + your canonical
   deliverables (re-housing first: IA/Preview/Send; then net-new: Client Review /
   Mark Accepted / Tier Selection / integrations).

You are the longer pole on the critical path — this round is what Slice 12 waits
on. The scope is well-specified (everything upstream is locked), so it should be a
clean design round, not a discovery one.

chat_messages.text:
Right — and that's a genuinely different kind of work than everything we've been doing, so it's worth flagging clearly: **the NetSuite integration has a real-world setup dependency that sits outside the code.** CC can build the push logic, but it can't create a NetSuite connection out of thin air — that requires actual NetSuite account configuration that only you (with NetSuite admin access) can do, and some of it is genuinely joint work between us.

Let me lay out what "configure NetSuite together" actually involves, because it splits into things you do in NetSuite, things we decide together, and things CC wires up — and it's worth knowing the shape before Tier Selection's NetSuite push gets built.

**What YOU do in NetSuite (admin access required — CC can't):**
- **Create the integration record** — enable the SuiteTalk/REST API, generate the connection credentials (NetSuite uses token-based auth: consumer key/secret + token ID/secret, or OAuth 2.0). These become environment secrets Nexus uses.
- **Confirm the Sales Order form/record structure** — what fields the SO expects, which are required, custom fields if any.
- **Confirm the customer-mapping approach** — how a HubSpot deal maps to a NetSuite customer record (by ID? by name-match? does the customer already exist in NetSuite or does the SO create it?). This is the trickiest real-world piece and it's an open question in the brief (§4.7).
- **Confirm "Pending Fulfillment" is a valid status** on your SO form and behaves the way you expect.

**What WE decide together (business/data-modeling calls):**
- **The assembly question the brief already flagged** (§4.7, catch D): does your existing HubSpot→NetSuite sync carry assembly metadata, or only flat leaves? This determines whether Nexus pushes nested assemblies or flattened lines — and it depends on how your NetSuite is set up today. This is exactly the kind of thing we figure out by looking at your actual NetSuite together.
- **Line-item mapping** — how a Nexus SKU (from the ASY/LEAF adapter) maps to a NetSuite item. Do the items already exist in NetSuite? Matched by SKU code?
- **The terms/header defaults** — FOB Long Beach, 50/50 payment, lead time — confirming these map to real NetSuite fields.

**What CC wires (once the above exists):**
- The push action, the payload builder (consuming the Slice-11.5 adapter), the idempotency key, error handling/retry, capturing the SO ID back.

That's a significant architectural decision and it answers the open question the brief flagged (§4.7 / catch D) — so let me make sure I understand it correctly, because it shapes the entire NetSuite payload design.

**What you're saying:** Nexus's assembly structure (the ASY/LEAF hierarchy) maps to NetSuite's **Item Group** feature. So a Nexus assembly becomes a NetSuite Item Group, and its leaves become the member items within that group on the Sales Order. That's the translation layer between how Nexus models products and how NetSuite represents them on the SO.

This is actually a clean answer to the assembly question — and it resolves the "nested assemblies vs. flattened leaves" fork the brief left open: **you push the assembly structure as Item Groups, preserving the hierarchy, rather than flattening to loose leaves.** The ASY/LEAF adapter output (which Slice 11.5 already produces) maps its groupings onto Item Groups.

But a few things about NetSuite Item Groups matter for how CC builds the payload, and some are worth confirming because Item Groups have specific behaviors:

**1. Item Groups vs. Assembly Items — these are different NetSuite features, and you picked Item Group deliberately.** NetSuite has *both* "Assembly/BOM Items" (a manufactured item with a build process) and "Item Groups" (a bundle of items sold together, presented as a group on transactions but not manufactured as a unit). Choosing **Item Group** means: the assembly is a *sales/presentation* grouping on the SO, not a manufactured BOM in NetSuite. That's probably right for a quoting→SO handoff (you're selling a grouped set, ops handles the build separately) — but it's worth confirming that's the intent, because it affects whether pricing/qty sits at the group level or the member level.

**2. Do the Item Groups already exist in NetSuite, or does the push create them?** This is the big one. Item Groups are typically **predefined records** in NetSuite (you set up "Item Group X" with its members). If Nexus assemblies are dynamic (a PM composes a new assembly per quote), there's a mismatch: NetSuite Item Groups aren't usually created on-the-fly per SO. So the question is:
   - **(a)** Do your assemblies correspond to *pre-existing* NetSuite Item Groups (Nexus references them by ID)? or
   - **(b)** Does each quote's assembly need a *new* Item Group created in NetSuite at push time? or
   - **(c)** Do you add the group's *member items* to the SO with group-level formatting, without a formal Item Group record?

These are very different integration shapes, and (b) especially is complex (creating master records as a side effect of an SO push).

**3. Pricing at group vs. member level.** On a NetSuite SO, an Item Group can show a group price or roll up member prices. Nexus prices at the tier level with per-leaf sell prices. How that maps — group-level total, or per-member unit prices under the group — needs to line up with how your NetSuite SOs are structured.

**4. The adapter already groups — this is a mapping, not a restructure.** The good news: Slice 11.5's ASY/LEAF adapter already outputs the assembly hierarchy, so CC isn't computing structure — it's *translating* the adapter's groups into Item Group payload shape. That keeps the Nexus side clean; the work is the NetSuite-side mapping.

So this decision (assembly → Item Group) is exactly the kind of thing that belongs in the NetSuite readiness checklist and the brief's §4.7 — it converts an open question into a design constraint. But it opens the sub-questions above, and **2 and 3 in particular are things we'd confirm by looking at your actual NetSuite setup together** (do the groups pre-exist, how are they priced).

**Captured:**
- Assembly → NetSuite **Item Group**
- **Push CREATES a new Item Group per assembly at SO time**
- **Per-member unit prices rolled under the group**

**The one I want to flag honestly, because it's the hardest part of the whole NetSuite integration:** "create a new Item Group per assembly at SO time" means the SO push isn't just *creating a Sales Order* — it's **creating master data (Item Group records) as a side effect.** That's a meaningfully more complex integration than pushing an SO against existing items:

- It's **two operations, not one** — create/find the Item Group(s), *then* create the SO referencing them. Order matters, and partial failure is possible (group created, SO fails → orphaned groups).
- **Idempotency gets harder.** The brief's idempotency key (`quote_id + quote_version`) protects against duplicate *SOs* — but now you also need to not create duplicate *Item Groups* on retry. A re-push has to find-or-create the group, not blindly create. That's a second idempotency surface.
- **Naming/identity** — each created Item Group needs a stable, unique identifier derived from the assembly so retries find the same one (e.g. keyed off the Nexus assembly ID + version).
- **Member items still need to exist** — the Item Group's members (the leaves) presumably map to existing NetSuite items; creating the *group* doesn't create the *members*. So there's still a member-item mapping question underneath (do the leaf SKUs exist in NetSuite?).

None of this is a blocker — it's just genuinely the most involved piece of the integration, and worth CC knowing early that "the NetSuite push" is really "create Item Groups (idempotently) + create SO," not a single call. That affects the time estimate and the retry/error design.

# CC Comm — sendQuote quote-number continuity fix (standalone, pre-Slice-12)

**To:** CC
**From:** CA
**Re:** Real bug in current `sendQuote` — second send fractures the customer-facing quote number. Ship before Slice 12.
**Status:** Standalone hotfix. Architect §0.5 round-2 catch (Item 5). Small, load-bearing. Gates the Slice 12 revise-in-place model — must land first so the revise path doesn't inherit the fracture.

---

## §1 · The bug

`sendQuote` (quotes.ts:1572-1576) calls `SELECT nextval('quote_number_seq')`
**with no guard on whether the quote already has a number.** Today this is latent
(a quote is normally sent once). But ANY second `sendQuote` on the same quote:
- consumes a SECOND sequence value, AND
- overwrites the prior `quote.quoteNumber`

→ the same quote ends up with two different customer-facing numbers. Customer
identity fractured.

**Why it matters now:** Slice 12's reversibility model is "revise in place → re-send
the SAME quote, same number, incrementing version." That path calls `sendQuote` a
second time. Without this fix, the first revise+re-send breaks quote-number
continuity — the exact thing the "same quote number, new version" decision
requires NOT to happen. It's also a genuine latent bug in current prod regardless
of Slice 12.

---

## §2 · The fix (Architect-provided)

Guard the sequence pull on first-send only:

```ts
let quoteNumber: string;
if (quote.quoteNumber === null) {
  const seqResult = await tx.execute(
    sql`SELECT nextval('quote_number_seq') AS next`
  );
  quoteNumber = `${firm.quoteNumberPrefix}-${String(seqResult[0].next)}`;
} else {
  quoteNumber = quote.quoteNumber;  // re-send keeps the existing number
}
```

First send → new number. Re-send → reuse existing number. Sequence is consumed
exactly once per quote.

---

## §3 · Plus: version_number in the send audit

Add `version_number` to the `quote_sent` audit `diff_json`. Today the diff shape
doesn't include it, so an audit reader can't distinguish multiple sends of the
same quote except by `created_at` (guessing). With re-send now a real path
(Slice 12), the audit must record WHICH version each send was. Cheap add now,
prevents an ambiguous audit trail later.

---

## §4 · Scope / guardrails

- **Only** the number-guard + the audit `version_number` add. Do NOT pull in
  Slice 12 work (no revise action, no snapshot table, no reversibility guards —
  those are Slice 12).
- The fix is idempotency-preserving: `assertDraft` still guards re-invocation as
  today; this only changes number assignment within a legitimate send.
- Verify: a quote sent once gets a number; a hypothetical second send (you can
  force one in a test) reuses it, doesn't advance the sequence, doesn't overwrite.
- `tsc` + verifiers green.

---

{"language": "bash", "code": "cat > /mnt/user-data/outputs/cc-comm-sendquote-number-continuity-fix.md << 'FIXEOF'
# CC Comm — sendQuote quote-number continuity fix (standalone, pre-Slice-12)

**To:** CC
**From:** CA
**Re:** Real bug in current `sendQuote` — second send fractures the customer-facing quote number. Ship before Slice 12.
**Status:** Standalone hotfix. Architect §0.5 round-2 catch (Item 5). Small, load-bearing. Gates the Slice 12 revise-in-place model — must land first so the revise path doesn't inherit the fracture.

---

## §1 · The bug

`sendQuote` (quotes.ts:1572-1576) calls `SELECT nextval('quote_number_seq')`
**with no guard on whether the quote already has a number.** Today this is latent
(a quote is normally sent once). But ANY second `sendQuote` on the same quote:
- consumes a SECOND sequence value, AND
- overwrites the prior `quote.quoteNumber`

→ the same quote ends up with two different customer-facing numbers. Customer
identity fractured.

**Why it matters now:** Slice 12's reversibility model is "revise in place → re-send
the SAME quote, same number, incrementing version." That path calls `sendQuote` a
second time. Without this fix, the first revise+re-send breaks quote-number
continuity — the exact thing the "same quote number, new version" decision
requires NOT to happen. It's also a genuine latent bug in current prod regardless
of Slice 12.

---

## §2 · The fix (Architect-provided)

Guard the sequence pull on first-send only:

```ts
let quoteNumber: string;
if (quote.quoteNumber === null) {
  const seqResult = await tx.execute(
    sql`SELECT nextval('quote_number_seq') AS next`
  );
  quoteNumber = `${firm.quoteNumberPrefix}-${String(seqResult[0].next)}`;
} else {
  quoteNumber = quote.quoteNumber;  // re-send keeps the existing number
}
```

First send → new number. Re-send → reuse existing number. Sequence is consumed
exactly once per quote.

---

## §3 · Plus: version_number in the send audit

Add `version_number` to the `quote_sent` audit `diff_json`. Today the diff shape
doesn't include it, so an audit reader can't distinguish multiple sends of the
same quote except by `created_at` (guessing). With re-send now a real path
(Slice 12), the audit must record WHICH version each send was. Cheap add now,
prevents an ambiguous audit trail later.

---

## §4 · Scope / guardrails

- **Only** the number-guard + the audit `version_number` add. Do NOT pull in
  Slice 12 work (no revise action, no snapshot table, no reversibility guards —
  those are Slice 12).
- The fix is idempotency-preserving: `assertDraft` still guards re-invocation as
  today; this only changes number assignment within a legitimate send.
- Verify: a quote sent once gets a number; a hypothetical second send (you can
  force one in a test) reuses it, doesn't advance the sequence, doesn't overwrite.
- `tsc` + verifiers green.

---

## §5 · Sequencing

Ship as a standalone PR **before Slice 12 kickoff.** It's a current-prod bug fix
that also de-risks the revise-in-place model before any Slice 12 sub-tab is built.
Bank as a §0.5 catch on merge: *sequence-backed customer identifiers must guard
on existing-value before pulling a new one — a re-invocable action that pulls a
fresh sequence value each time fractures identity.*
FIXEOF

**Prototype:** `Nexus Round 8.html` → `app/r8/{data.js, styles.css, umbrella.jsx}`

transitions feel *ordinary* and one feel *ceremonial*. If every advance looked the
same, the PM would learn nothing from the interface and would be reading warning
copy to find out where the cliff is. Copy is skimmed; weight is not.

| Transition | Weight | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Preview → Send | light | plain primary + caption "Reversible — you can come back and revise" |
| Send → (sent) | light | plain primary + a *stating* confirm modal (what the customer receives), no consequence list |
| Client Review → Mark Accepted | light | plain primary |
| Mark Accepted → (accepted) | light | plain primary; **rollback shown as a peer** once recorded |
| **Tier Selection → Complete** | **heavy** | dark ceremonial slab, lock glyph, 2px top rule on the bar, consequence list, **typed `FINALIZE` confirmation** |

- **Lock threshold** — a dashed vertical rule in the sub-tab strip between tab 4 and
  tab 5, captioned "lock threshold". The reversible region is visibly *a region*.
- **Reversibility legend** — one line under the strip: steps 1–4 reversible, step 5
  pushes a Sales Order. Present on every non-complete state; removed after Complete
  (replaced by the read-only note), because it no longer describes anything true.

Five tabs, strict-sequential, order locked. Status derives from quote state + index:

| Status | Meaning | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `current` | quote is in this tab's state | accent underline, filled numeral, 600 label |
| `done` | passed, **still reachable** | green check numeral, `done · revisitable` sub-label |
| `upcoming` | not reachable yet | dashed numeral, muted, `disabled`, sub-label `awaiting sent`/`awaiting accepted` |
| `locked` | post-Complete | lock numeral, all tabs, no hover |

`done` deliberately reads *revisitable*, not merely *finished* — a checkmark alone
would imply "closed". The sub-label says so in words because the difference between
"done" and "done and you can go back" is the whole reversibility model.

**Client Review is styled as a logging tab, not a gate.** Two quiet signals, no new
colour: the numeral is a rounded *square* (a ledger, not a step in a sequence), and
the label carries a dotted underline. It also shows a live entry count. It reads as
a place to track rather than a threshold to pass — which is what the brief asked for
and what stops PMs treating it as a step they must "complete".

## 2 · Preview Quote (2.2)

Framing only — the PDF shipped in Slice 11 and is untouched here (rendered as a
labelled stand-in in the prototype).

label, status tag (`sent` / `draft` / `superseded`), the change note, the date, and
the total. Rationale: four versions with different totals is a **comparison**, not a
pick-from-list. A dropdown hides exactly the information the PM needs (which one did
the customer actually see, and what does it cost) — and that same distinction is what
the mismatch banner depends on two tabs later. Newest first. Same quote number on all
of them, stated in the header.

  No consequence list, no typed confirmation. Send is reversible; ceremony here would
  devalue the ceremony that matters.
- **Post-send waiting state** (the core gap — no such surface existed): pulse dot,
  "Sent — awaiting Beth", days elapsed, validity date, feed count, and actions
  (open Client Review, re-send, download). Its real job is to say **nothing is
  expected of you right now**, and point to the one place where something might be.
  Before this round the UI simply went quiet after a send.
- The **Revise** affordance appears here too (not only in Client Review), because
  "I need to change what I just sent" arrives most often immediately after sending.

## 4 · Client Review (2.4) — the new sub-tab

A log. Kept visually a log on purpose:

- **Hairline timeline** — 9px dot on a 1px spine, per-type dot colour, no cards.
- **Append-only, newest first**, each entry = type chip + author + timestamp + note.
- **Add-entry collapsed to a single line** ("+ Log customer activity…") until used.
  A permanently-open form turns a jotting surface into a task-shaped one.
- **Event type as chips, not a select** — three today (`responded`, `asked`,
  `revision_requested`), extensible, each with a one-line hint. Cheap to scan, and
  visible extensibility for CC.
- **Empty state:** "No customer activity logged yet." plus one line on what to log.
- A `revision_requested` entry grows **inline actions** — "↺ Revise quote → v4",
  "Mark handled" — so the response sits next to the trigger.
- Explicitly labelled in-surface as *not* customer-facing, *not* a thread, *not* a
  revision manager (right rail), so the next reader doesn't grow it into one.

## 5 · Revise + mismatch banner (2.4a)

**Revise** is styled as an ordinary secondary action inside a dashed container — never
a primary, never a destructive/danger treatment. Reversibility is *routine* in this
model; making Revise look like an emergency exit would contradict the whole design.
Copy always states the invariant: *same quote, same number, nothing is lost.*

**Sent-vs-draft mismatch banner** honours the IA-spec intent verbatim:

> You sent **v3** on Jul 14 · current draft is **v4**

…plus the consequence the PM actually needs: *the customer is responding to v3, and
acceptance records against the version the customer saw.* Four affordances: view sent,
compare, send the draft, dismiss. Warn-tinted, not error — a draft leading a sent
version is a normal working state, not a fault.

## 6 · Mark Accepted (2.5)

panels are gone from here** — tier selection has moved to its own sub-tab, and the
margin verdict belongs to Pricing. What remains is what this step actually is: record
acceptance, against a specific version, and push HubSpot once.

- **Records against the sent version**, stated explicitly (`v3 — the version the
  customer saw`), with the customer's tier signal shown as context (not selected here).

  the last reversible step and the one most likely to be mis-clicked, so the way back
  is stated where the mistake happens.

  which is the entire model in three words.

  `accepted` **and still reversible**, safe to retry.
- **Post-push confirmation**: SO id, timestamp, tier, turnkey total, link out.

convention).

Applied by `@media (max-width: 900px)` **and** by a forced `.r8-shell.narrow` class so

   PMs would expect the customer's email to appear here.

   One legend line under the strip plus the threshold rule carries it; per-button
   captions state it only where the PM is deciding.
3. **Colour-coding the whole strip by reversibility** (green tabs 1–4, red tab 5).

   make a normal working state look alarming. The threshold rule is structural instead.

   irreversible act in the product, it pushes into an external system of record, and a
   misfire costs a cancelled SO in NetSuite. Typing six characters is proportionate.

   sources of truth for the accepted tier.

`SendConfirmModal` · `ReviewTab` · `MismatchBanner` · `AddEntry` · `AcceptedTab` ·
`TierTab` · `FinalizationModal` · `CompleteTab`.

`r8-strip` `r8-tab`(`.done .current .upcoming .locked .log`) `r8-threshold` `r8-legend`
`r8-body` `r8-cols` `r8-card`(`.flush`) `r8-card-head` `r8-vpick` `r8-vrow` `r8-vtag`
`r8-pdfframe` `r8-wait` `r8-feed` `r8-fitem`(`.t-*`) `r8-etype` `r8-addentry`
`r8-typepick` `r8-empty` `r8-mismatch` `r8-revise` `r8-push`(`.ok .error`)
`r8-rollback` `r8-tier`(`.on .disabled`) `r8-signal` `r8-advance`(`.heavy`)
`r8-adv-btn`(`.heavy`) `r8-final-head` `r8-consequences` `r8-confirmtype`
`r8-locked-ribbon` `r8-solink` `r8-readonly-note` `r8-defs`.

`.r8-proto` / `.r8-dn` are prototype-only (state switcher, inline designer notes) —
**strip both in production.**

# Round 8 — Quote umbrella · Designer notes

**Deliverable:** Pattern 30 canonical source for Slice 12 (the Quote umbrella).
**Prototype:** `Nexus Round 8.html` → `app/r8/{data.js, styles.css, umbrella.jsx}`
**Designed against:** `quote-umbrella-brief-RECONCILED-v2` (not the original).
**Status:** live blocker cleared — CC builds from `app/r8/styles.css` verbatim, not from CSS interpretation.

---

## 0 · The one idea

> **Nothing is locked until the NetSuite SO push.**

Everything in this round is an expression of that. The umbrella has five sequential
sub-tabs and exactly one point of no return, so the design's job is to make four
transitions feel *ordinary* and one feel *ceremonial*. If every advance looked the
same, the PM would learn nothing from the interface and would be reading warning
copy to find out where the cliff is. Copy is skimmed; weight is not.

**The asymmetry is the deliverable. Do not normalize it in implementation.**

| Transition | Weight | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Preview → Send | light | plain primary + caption "Reversible — you can come back and revise" |
| Send → (sent) | light | plain primary + a *stating* confirm modal (what the customer receives), no consequence list |
| Client Review → Mark Accepted | light | plain primary |
| Mark Accepted → (accepted) | light | plain primary; **rollback shown as a peer** once recorded |
| **Tier Selection → Complete** | **heavy** | dark ceremonial slab, lock glyph, 2px top rule on the bar, consequence list, **typed `FINALIZE` confirmation** |

Two supporting devices carry the same idea:

- **Lock threshold** — a dashed vertical rule in the sub-tab strip between tab 4 and
  tab 5, captioned "lock threshold". The reversible region is visibly *a region*.
- **Reversibility legend** — one line under the strip: steps 1–4 reversible, step 5
  pushes a Sales Order. Present on every non-complete state; removed after Complete
  (replaced by the read-only note), because it no longer describes anything true.

---

## 1 · Sub-tab strip (2.1)

Five tabs, strict-sequential, order locked. Status derives from quote state + index:

| Status | Meaning | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `current` | quote is in this tab's state | accent underline, filled numeral, 600 label |
| `done` | passed, **still reachable** | green check numeral, `done · revisitable` sub-label |
| `upcoming` | not reachable yet | dashed numeral, muted, `disabled`, sub-label `awaiting sent`/`awaiting accepted` |
| `locked` | post-Complete | lock numeral, all tabs, no hover |

`done` deliberately reads *revisitable*, not merely *finished* — a checkmark alone
would imply "closed". The sub-label says so in words because the difference between
"done" and "done and you can go back" is the whole reversibility model.

**Client Review is styled as a logging tab, not a gate.** Two quiet signals, no new
colour: the numeral is a rounded *square* (a ledger, not a step in a sequence), and
the label carries a dotted underline. It also shows a live entry count. It reads as
a place to track rather than a threshold to pass — which is what the brief asked for
and what stops PMs treating it as a step they must "complete".

## 2 · Preview Quote (2.2)

Framing only — the PDF shipped in Slice 11 and is untouched here (rendered as a
labelled stand-in in the prototype).

**Version chooser:** a row-per-version *list*, not a dropdown. Each row carries
label, status tag (`sent` / `draft` / `superseded`), the change note, the date, and
the total. Rationale: four versions with different totals is a **comparison**, not a
pick-from-list. A dropdown hides exactly the information the PM needs (which one did
the customer actually see, and what does it cost) — and that same distinction is what
the mismatch banner depends on two tabs later. Newest first. Same quote number on all
of them, stated in the header.

## 3 · Send to Client (2.3)

- **Send confirm** is *stating*, not warning: recipient, attachment, `draft → sent`.
  No consequence list, no typed confirmation. Send is reversible; ceremony here would
  devalue the ceremony that matters.
- **Post-send waiting state** (the core gap — no such surface existed): pulse dot,
  "Sent — awaiting Beth", days elapsed, validity date, feed count, and actions
  (open Client Review, re-send, download). Its real job is to say **nothing is
  expected of you right now**, and point to the one place where something might be.
  Before this round the UI simply went quiet after a send.
- The **Revise** affordance appears here too (not only in Client Review), because
  "I need to change what I just sent" arrives most often immediately after sending.

## 4 · Client Review (2.4) — the new sub-tab

A log. Kept visually a log on purpose:

- **Hairline timeline** — 9px dot on a 1px spine, per-type dot colour, no cards.
- **Append-only, newest first**, each entry = type chip + author + timestamp + note.
- **Add-entry collapsed to a single line** ("+ Log customer activity…") until used.
  A permanently-open form turns a jotting surface into a task-shaped one.
- **Event type as chips, not a select** — three today (`responded`, `asked`,
  `revision_requested`), extensible, each with a one-line hint. Cheap to scan, and
  visible extensibility for CC.
- **Empty state:** "No customer activity logged yet." plus one line on what to log.
- A `revision_requested` entry grows **inline actions** — "↺ Revise quote → v4",
  "Mark handled" — so the response sits next to the trigger.
- Explicitly labelled in-surface as *not* customer-facing, *not* a thread, *not* a
  revision manager (right rail), so the next reader doesn't grow it into one.

## 5 · Revise + mismatch banner (2.4a)

**Revise** is styled as an ordinary secondary action inside a dashed container — never
a primary, never a destructive/danger treatment. Reversibility is *routine* in this
model; making Revise look like an emergency exit would contradict the whole design.
Copy always states the invariant: *same quote, same number, nothing is lost.*

**Sent-vs-draft mismatch banner** honours the IA-spec intent verbatim:

> You sent **v3** on Jul 14 · current draft is **v4**

…plus the consequence the PM actually needs: *the customer is responding to v3, and
acceptance records against the version the customer saw.* Four affordances: view sent,
compare, send the draft, dismiss. Warn-tinted, not error — a draft leading a sent
version is a normal working state, not a fault.

## 6 · Mark Accepted (2.5)

Reconciled with the existing IA-spec Mark-Accepted design: the **gates/verdict/tier
panels are gone from here** — tier selection has moved to its own sub-tab, and the
margin verdict belongs to Pricing. What remains is what this step actually is: record
acceptance, against a specific version, and push HubSpot once.

- **Records against the sent version**, stated explicitly (`v3 — the version the
  customer saw`), with the customer's tier signal shown as context (not selected here).

  important sentence in any integration error.

  Send to Client — reverses the HubSpot stage". Not buried in an admin menu. This is
  the last reversible step and the one most likely to be mis-clicked, so the way back
  is stated where the mistake happens.

  status), read-only. Not redesigned.
- **Single-select, pre-filled from the customer's recorded signal** (T2, from review
  event ev2), with the provenance shown — "stated in review_event ev2 · 2026-07-19" —
  and PM override allowed. Recommended tier keeps its ★.

  the advance disables, and the R5 firm-policy-gate pattern supplies the admin-override
