  NetSuite SO and `Pending Fulfillment`, a five-item consequence list (two lock icons),
  and a **typed `FINALIZE`** gate. Cancel is labelled *"Cancel — keep it reversible"*,
  which is the entire model in three words.
- **NetSuite failure**: 502, *"quote NOT finalized"*, no SO created, state still
  `accepted` **and still reversible**, safe to retry.
- **Post-push confirmation**: SO id, timestamp, tier, turnkey total, link out.

Dark ribbon leading with the SO number and the NetSuite link; every sub-tab `locked`;
one quiet read-only line; Revise disabled; no advance ("No advance — this is the end of
the lifecycle"). Tone is **"here is the record"**, not "you can no longer edit this" —

Every UI element → its data source, so CC wires against real fields rather than
inventing them. Prototype fixtures live in `app/r8/data.js` (`window.NXR8`).

**Legend:** `EXISTING` = already in the schema / shipped · **`NEW`** = does not exist
yet, must be created (flagged per brief §4) · `REUSED` = a shipped component's data,
framed here · `DERIVED` = computed at render · `PROTO` = prototype-only, strip in production.

## Shell · topbar · sub-tab strip

| UI element | Source | Field / note |
|---|---|---|
| Breadcrumb (client · deal · scenario · Quote) | EXISTING | `project.{client, deal}`, `scenario.label` |
| Quote number | EXISTING | `quote.quote_number` — stable across all versions |
| State chip | DERIVED | `quote.state` ∈ `draft` \| `sent` \| `accepted` \| `complete` |

| PDF preview | REUSED | Slice 11 customer PDF render — unchanged, framed only |
| Download PDF | REUSED | Slice 11 render/download path |

| UI element | Source | Field / note |
|---|---|---|

| Version being sent | EXISTING | `quote.draft_version` |

| Post-send waiting state | **NEW** *(surface)* | reads `quote.{sent_version, sent_at, sent_to, valid_until}` + feed count. No new fields — new surface. |

| Auto-logged `sent` feed entry | **NEW** | `quote_review_events` row, `type='sent'`, `system=true` |

| UI element | Source | Field / note |
|---|---|---|
| Feed entries | **NEW** | **`quote_review_events`** — `{id, quote_id, type, note, author_user_id, created_at, system}`. Append-only. |
| Event type chip | **NEW** | `quote_review_events.type` ∈ `responded` \| `asked` \| `revision_requested` \| `sent`(system) — **extensible enum** |

| Timestamp | **NEW** | `quote_review_events.created_at` |
| Add-entry form | **NEW** | inserts one `quote_review_events` row |
| Empty state | DERIVED | `count = 0` |
| Inline "Revise" on a `revision_requested` entry | **NEW** *(affordance)* | triggers the Revise action (below) |
| "not customer-facing" rail copy | — | static |

| UI element | Source | Field / note |
|---|---|---|

|---|---|---|

| Below-floor block + override | EXISTING | R5 firm-policy gate + admin-override path |

| Typed `FINALIZE` gate | — | UI-only |
| NetSuite push | **NEW** | creates SO, status **`Pending Fulfillment`**; stores **`netsuite_so_id`** + `pushed_at` |
| Push failure copy | DERIVED | no SO created; `state` still `accepted`, still reversible |
| SO confirmation + link | **NEW** | `netsuite_so_id`, deep link |

## 7 · Post-Complete (Pattern 52)

| UI element | Source | Field / note |
|---|---|---|
| Locked ribbon (SO id, finalized-by, timestamp) | **NEW** | `netsuite_so_id`, `completed_by`, `completed_at` |
| Final-record rows | EXISTING | accepted tier, turnkey total, accepted version, HubSpot stage/amount |
| Review log (read-only) | **NEW** | `quote_review_events`, retained |
| All sub-tabs read-only / Revise disabled | DERIVED | `quote.state = 'complete'` |
| Request unlock (admin) | EXISTING | admin unlock + reason, audit-logged (R5 pattern) |

---

## NEW items summary — for Architect §0.5 round 2

1. **`quote_review_events`** table — `{id, quote_id, type, note, author_user_id, created_at, system}`; append-only; extensible `type` enum (`responded`, `asked`, `revision_requested`, `sent`).
2. **`netsuite_so_id`** (+ `pushed_at`, `completed_by`, `completed_at`) on the quote.
3. **`customer_signal_tier_id`** on the quote (+ provenance ref into the feed).
4. **Version chain exposure** — snapshots exist; the picker needs `{version_number, status, created_at, note, total}` queryable per quote.
5. **Reversibility guards** — `sent → draft` (Revise), `accepted → sent` (rollback), and a hard stop on any transition out of `complete` without admin approval.
6. **Mismatch derivation** — `draft_version > sent_version AND state='sent'` (no stored flag; derive).
7. **Version diff view** (`Compare v3 ↔ v4`) — flagged as its own scope item, not assumed.

**Sequencing note (brief §5):** the turnkey totals shown in Tier Selection depend on
Slice 11 F1.5 service-fee/freight wiring (currently stubbed). Tier Selection ships
with F1.5, per CA's note — design is complete either way.

For Item 5 — ship it standalone, now, ahead of Slice 12. Three reasons it shouldn't wait: it's a real bug in *current* prod (any double-send fractures the number, Slice 12 or not), it's tiny (a null-guard + an audit field), and it de-risks the entire revise-in-place model before a single sub-tab exists. Folding it into Slice 12 as "the first migration" works mechanically, but then it rides Slice 12's timeline — and Slice 12 is the biggest slice in v1. No reason to make a prod bug fix wait behind a multi-week slice when it's a self-contained patch. The comm's already drafted (`cc-comm-sendquote-number-continuity-fix`). Ship it.

For the v3 patch — that's already written (`quote-umbrella-brief-RECONCILED-v3.md`, done earlier this session with all 7 amendments folded in). So there's nothing to decide there; it's done and it's the current source of truth. The only open thread on it now is landing it *plus* the R8 deliverables in the repo together.

**Version-diff "Compare" view: defer to v1.5+, design the entry point now.**

CD already pointed the right way by flagging it as "its own scope item, not assumed." My reasoning for deferring:
- **It's genuinely separable.** The reversibility model works completely without it — Revise, versioned snapshots, the mismatch banner all function. Compare-v3↔v4 is a *convenience* for the PM, not a load-bearing part of the loop.
- **It's more work than it looks.** A real diff view means rendering two snapshots side by side and computing/highlighting deltas across the whole quote structure (tiers, SKUs, costs, specs). That's a meaningful sub-project, and Slice 12 is already the largest in v1.
- **The brief already anticipated this** — the IA-spec's mismatch banner lists "Compare v[N]↔v[N+1]" as an affordance "when audit-log diff surface ships," i.e. it was always envisioned as a later capability, not a v1 given.
- **Deferring loses almost nothing now.** The mismatch banner still tells the PM "you sent v3, draft is v4" and lets them view each version. Not having an automated *diff* just means the PM eyeballs the two — acceptable for v1, especially at ~12 users.

So: **design the entry point** (CD already did — the "Compare" affordance sits in the mismatch banner), **build the view in v1.5+.** In Slice 12, the Compare button either renders disabled with a "coming soon" affordance or is omitted from the build (CC's call at impl); the *hook* is designed so it slots in later without rework. # CC Comm — Packaging duplicate-line delete wipes sibling's cost (PROD DATA LOSS)

**To:** CC
**From:** CA
**Re:** Deleting a duplicate packaging line silently wipes a sibling line's cost — live prod bug, real data loss
**Status:** Standalone fix. **Diagnose-first** (root cause not yet pinned). Queue AFTER the sendQuote number-continuity PR merges — don't run two branches at once. Then this is the last standalone fix before Slice 12 Phase 1.

---

## §0 · Why this is priority

This is a **live prod bug that destroys untouched data.** Reported symptom: on the
Costs surface, when a PM deletes a *duplicate* packaging line, a **sibling
packaging line's cost data silently disappears** — data the PM never touched. No
error, no warning; the cost is just gone. A real PM will hit this, and silent
data loss is the worst failure class (no signal that anything broke).

It's been carried as a one-line flag across sessions without a proper diagnosis.
This fix starts by pinning down what actually happens.

---

## §1 · Diagnose first — do NOT write the fix yet

The root cause and code path are not yet known. **Step 1 is diagnosis, not a
patch.** Report back with the diagnosis before proposing the fix (same discipline
as the sendQuote number bug — repro + root cause + code path, then fix).

Diagnosis questions to answer:
1. **Repro** — on a THROWAWAY fixture (see §3), reproduce it: create a packaging
   line, duplicate it, delete the duplicate, confirm the sibling's cost is wiped.
   Capture the exact before/after.
2. **What "duplicate line" means here** — is this the packaging inputs table keyed
   by `(quote_sku_id, tier_id)`? Two rows that share a key? A UI-duplicated row
   that points at the same underlying record? The nature of the "duplicate"
   probably IS the bug.
3. **Root cause hypotheses to check:**
   - **Shared identity:** does the duplicate share a primary key / row id with the
     sibling, so deleting one deletes both (or nulls the shared row)?
   - **Delete-by-wrong-key:** does the delete action target by a non-unique field
     (e.g. `sku_id` + section rather than the row's own `id`), catching the sibling?

Let me be honest about what I actually know vs. what I'm inferring, because for a data-loss bug the difference matters.

**What I actually know** — and it's just the one-line symptom that's been carried across sessions:

> On the Costs surface, when a PM deletes a *duplicate* packaging line, a *sibling* packaging line's cost data silently disappears — data the PM never touched. No error, no warning.

That's the entire confirmed fact. Everything past that is hypothesis, not diagnosis. I don't have the root cause or the code path — CC found those for the sendQuote bug by actually reading the code, and it hasn't done that yet for this one.

**What I can explain is the *shape* of the problem and the plausible causes** — the hypotheses I put in the comm for CC to check. Here's the reasoning behind each, so you understand what we're likely looking at:

The packaging cost data is stored in a table keyed by `(quote_sku_id, tier_id)` — one row per SKU per tier. The word "duplicate" in the symptom is the tell, and it splits into a few candidate mechanisms:

1. **Shared identity** — if "duplicating" a packaging line created a second row that somehow shares a primary key or reference with the original, then deleting "the duplicate" deletes the row both point at. The sibling isn't really a sibling — they're the same underlying record, so deleting one destroys both. This is the most common way "delete one, lose two" happens.

2. **Delete-by-wrong-key** — if the delete action targets rows by a *non-unique* field (say, `quote_sku_id` + section, rather than the row's own unique `id`), then a delete meant for one line matches and removes *every* line sharing that field — catching the sibling. The delete is too broad because it's keyed on the wrong column.

3. **Unintended cascade** — an `ON DELETE CASCADE` (DB-level) or an app-level cascade that reaches further than intended, so deleting the packaging line also nulls or removes a related cost row it shouldn't touch.

4. **Optimistic-store desync** — and this is the one I'd bet on, because it *rhymes with a bug pattern this codebase already has.* If the delete is a fire-and-forget client-side mutation (optimistic update to the React store, then a DB write that isn't awaited/checked), a mis-targeted store update could remove the sibling from state, and then the next save *persists* that wipe. This is the exact silent-data-loss class from Slice 11 (the fire-and-forget `startTransition` that swallowed errors, the #126 fix). If it's this, the sibling's cost "disappears" because the client dropped it from state and then wrote the depleted state back — no error, because the failure was swallowed.

"Silent, no error, data just gone" is the signature of a swallowed-error store desync more than a DB cascade (which usually leaves cleaner evidence). But I genuinely don't know — it could equally be #1 (shared identity on duplicate).

**The honest bottom line:** I can tell you what the bug *does* (delete a duplicate packaging line → a sibling's cost silently vanishes) and the four ways it plausibly happens, but I can't tell you *which* until CC reads the delete action and the duplicate-line creation path. That's the diagnosis gate in the comm — and it's deliberately a gate, with CA review before the fix, *because* it's data loss and a plausible-but-wrong fix would leave real cost data still at risk.

chat_messages.text: how does client review work? are we tracking responses?

content.text: how does client review work? are we tracking responses?

chat_messages.text:
Good question to pause on — because what got built is deliberately narrow, and it's worth being clear it does *less* than the name might suggest.

**What Client Review actually is: a manual PM log.** It's a timestamped feed where the PM types entries about what's happening with the customer — "Beth responded, wants the capsule SKU dropped," "asked about splitting the PO," "requested a revision." Three entry types: responded / asked / revision_requested (plus a system-generated "sent" entry). That's it. The PM writes it; it's an internal activity log.

**Are we tracking responses? No — not automatically.** This is the important distinction. There's **no inbound integration.** The customer's actual emails/replies don't flow into Nexus. Nothing syncs from HubSpot or a mailbox. If Beth emails back, *nothing appears* in Client Review unless the PM manually logs "customer responded." So "tracking responses" in the automated sense — no. It's the PM's hand-written record of responses that happened elsewhere (email, calls), not a capture of the responses themselves.

That was a deliberate scope decision (yours, earlier): **lightweight logged activity feed, explicitly NOT threaded messaging, NOT customer-facing, NOT a revision manager.** CD's design even labels it in-surface as "not a thread, not customer-facing" so nobody mistakes it for two-way sync. The reasoning at the time: threading/inbound-sync implies infrastructure we don't have (mailbox integration, webhook handlers), and PMs would then *expect* the customer's email to show up — which it wouldn't.

So the honest summary: **Client Review gives the send→accept window a home and a paper trail, and its real payoff is the Revise hook** (a "revision_requested" entry sits next to a Revise button). It answers Symptom 3 ("no surface for the waiting/dialogue phase") — but as a *manual log*, not an automated response tracker.

If what you actually want is **automated response tracking** (customer replies flowing into Nexus), that's a genuinely different, bigger feature — inbound email/HubSpot sync, out of current scope (it was on the v2 list). Worth flagging now if that's the real need, because the current build won't do it and the design deliberately steers away from implying it will.

Is the manual-log version what you intended, or were you expecting some response capture? That determines whether this is on-target or needs a scope rethink before Step 6 goes further.
